+       && (regionId === '' || c.parentId === regionId)
+       && (needle === '' || c.name.toLowerCase().includes(needle))
+     ));
+     // The places most people mean come first: the biggest.
+     pool.sort((a, b) => b.population - a.population || a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
+     return pool;
+   }, [countryId, regionId, query, loadedTick]);
+
+   const known = cityCount(countryId);
+
+   return (
+     <div className="col gap-3">
+       {map && (
+         <div className="row-between wrap gap-2">
+           <p className="xs dim" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
+             {mapOpen
+               ? 'Pick a country on the map, or find it in the list below.'
+               : 'The map is hidden. The list below does the same thing.'}
+           </p>
+           <button
+             type="button"
+             className="btn btn-ghost btn-sm"
+             aria-expanded={mapOpen}
+             onClick={() => setMapOpen((open) => !open)}
+           >
+             {mapOpen ? 'Hide Map' : 'Show Map'}
+           </button>
+         </div>
+       )}
+
+       {map && mapOpen && (
+         <WorldMap
+           countryId={countryId}
+           marker={selected && selected.countryId === countryId
+             ? { latitude: selected.latitude, longitude: selected.longitude, name: selected.name }
+             : undefined}
+           onPick={(picked) => {
+             if (picked === countryId) return;
+             setCountryId(picked);
+             setRegionId('');
+             setQuery('');
+           }}
+         />
+       )}
+
+       <div className="grid grid-2">
+         <div className="field">
+           <label htmlFor={`${prefix}-country`}>Country</label>
+           <select
+             id={`${prefix}-country`}
+             value={countryId}
+             onChange={(e) => { setCountryId(e.target.value); setRegionId(''); setQuery(''); }}
+           >
+             {countries.map((c) => (
+               <option key={c.id} value={c.id} data-source="gazetteer">{c.name}</option>
+             ))}
+           </select>
+           <p className="hint">
+             {known > 0
+               ? `${known.toLocaleString('en-US')} town${known === 1 ? '' : 's'} and cit${known === 1 ? 'y' : 'ies'} on record.`
+               : 'No towns or cities on record for this country.'}
+           </p>
+         </div>
+
+         <div className="field">
+           <label htmlFor={`${prefix}-region`}>State Or Region</label>
+           <select
+             id={`${prefix}-region`}
+             value={regionId}
+             onChange={(e) => { setRegionId(e.target.value); setQuery(''); }}
+             disabled={regions.length === 0}
+           >
+             <option value="">
+               {regions.length === 0 ? 'None' : anywhereIn(COUNTRIES.get(countryId)?.name)}
+             </option>
+             {regions.map((r) => (
+               <option key={r.id} value={r.id}>{r.name}</option>
+             ))}
+           </select>
+           <p className="hint">
+             {regions.length > 0
+               ? `${regions.length} to choose from.`
+               : 'There are no states or regions to choose from in this country.'}
+           </p>
+         </div>
+       </div>
+
+       <div className="field">
+         <label htmlFor={`${prefix}-search`}>Town Or City</label>
+         <input
+           id={`${prefix}-search`}
+           type="search"
+           value={query}
+           placeholder={loading ? 'Loading its towns…' : 'Start typing a town name'}
+           onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)}
+           autoComplete="off"
+         />
+         {problem && <p className="hint" role="alert">{problem}</p>}
+       </div>
+
+       <div className="picker-results" role="listbox" aria-label="Matching Places">
+         {matches.length === 0 && !loading && (
+           <p className="hint" style={{ padding: 'var(--s3)' }}>
+             {/* Each variant says what's true of it (from 2026-10-19, brief 15): until then an empty search in a country
+                 with no towns read “No town or city matches “” there.”, and “widen the region” named no control. */}
+             {query.trim() === ''
+               ? 'There’s no town or city on record there.'
+               : `No town or city matches “${query.trim()}” there. Try a different spelling${regionId ? `, or choose ${anywhereIn(COUNTRIES.get(countryId)?.name)}` : ''}.`}
+           </p>
+         )}
+         {matches.slice(0, VISIBLE_MATCHES).map((c) => (
+           <button
+             type="button"
+             key={c.id}
+             role="option"
+             aria-selected={c.id === cityId}
+             className="picker-option"
+             data-selected={c.id === cityId ? 'true' : undefined}
+             onClick={() => onPick(c)}
+           >
+             <span className="picker-option-name truncate" title={c.name} data-source="gazetteer">{c.name}</span>
+             <span
+               className="picker-option-meta truncate"
+               title={[
+                 REGIONS.get(c.parentId)?.name ?? COUNTRIES.get(c.countryId)?.name,
+                 c.population > 0 ? `${c.population.toLocaleString('en-US')} people` : '',
+               ].filter(Boolean).join(' · ')}
+             >
+               {REGIONS.get(c.parentId)?.name ?? COUNTRIES.get(c.countryId)?.name}
+               {c.population > 0 && ` · ${c.population.toLocaleString('en-US')} people`}
+             </span>
+           </button>
+         ))}
+         {matches.length > VISIBLE_MATCHES && (
+           <p className="hint" style={{ padding: 'var(--s3)' }}>
+             {(matches.length - VISIBLE_MATCHES).toLocaleString('en-US')} more match. Keep typing to narrow it down.
+           </p>
+         )}
+       </div>
+     </div>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * Your headshot.
+  *
+  * Takes whatever photo the player has — any size, any shape, any of the
+  * formats a browser can decode — and turns it into one headshot: four by five,
+  * 512 across, re-encoded small enough to live inside a save.
+  *
+  * The photo is never stored as it arrived. It is drawn into a fixed frame and
+  * re-encoded, which fits it, strips whatever metadata the camera wrote into
+  * it, and keeps a nine-thousand-pixel phone picture from turning a save into
+  * something that will not fit in storage.
+  */
+
+ import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
+ import {
+   CANNOT_DECODE, CANNOT_ENCODE, CENTRED, MAX_ZOOM, PORTRAIT_HEIGHT, PORTRAIT_WIDTH,
+   clampPlacement, dataUrlBytes, describeRejection, drawRect,
+   type Placement,
+ } from './portrait';
+
+ /** Quality to re-encode at. High enough for a face, small enough for a save. */
+ const JPEG_QUALITY = 0.86;
+
+ /**
+  * The picture-with-an-arrow every upload control has.
+  *
+  * Drawn rather than fetched, so it costs nothing, scales to any screen and
+  * takes the frame's color — including the accent it turns while a photo is
+  * being dragged over it.
+  */
+ function UploadGlyph() {
+   return (
+     <svg className="portrait-glyph" viewBox="0 0 48 48" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">
+       <rect x="5" y="8" width="38" height="32" rx="5" />
+       <circle cx="15" cy="18.5" r="3" />
+       <path d="M7 36.5 16 27.5l4.5 4" />
+       <path d="M31 37V21.5" />
+       <path d="M25.5 27 31 21.5 36.5 27" />
+     </svg>
+   );
+ }
+
+ export function PortraitPicker({
+   portrait, name, onChange,
+ }: {
+   portrait: string | undefined;
+   name: string;
+   onChange: (portrait: string | undefined) => void;
+ }) {
+   const [source, setSource] = useState<HTMLImageElement | null>(null);
+   const [placement, setPlacement] = useState<Placement>(CENTRED);
+   const [problem, setProblem] = useState<string | undefined>();
+   const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
+   const [dragging, setDragging] = useState(false);
+   const canvasRef = useRef<HTMLCanvasElement | null>(null);
+   const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null);
+   const dragFrom = useRef<{ x: number; y: number; placement: Placement } | null>(null);
+
+   /** Draws the current source at the current placement. */
+   const paint = useCallback(() => {
+     const canvas = canvasRef.current;
+     if (!canvas || !source) return;
+     const context = canvas.getContext('2d');
+     if (!context) return;
+
+     context.clearRect(0, 0, PORTRAIT_WIDTH, PORTRAIT_HEIGHT);
+     const rect = drawRect(source.naturalWidth, source.naturalHeight, placement);
+     context.drawImage(source, rect.x, rect.y, rect.width, rect.height);
+   }, [source, placement]);
+
+   useEffect(() => { paint(); }, [paint]);
+
+   /** Hands the framed result up, re-encoded. */
+   const commit = useCallback(() => {
+     const canvas = canvasRef.current;
+     if (!canvas || !source) return;
+     try {
+       onChange(canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg', JPEG_QUALITY));
+     } catch {
+       setProblem(CANNOT_ENCODE);
+     }
+   }, [onChange, source]);
+
+   useEffect(() => {
+     if (source) commit();
+     // Re-encode whenever the framing changes, so what is stored is what is seen.
+   }, [source, placement, commit]);
+
+   const accept = useCallback((file: File) => {
+     const rejection = describeRejection(file);
+     if (rejection) { setProblem(rejection); return; }
+
+     setProblem(undefined);
+     setBusy(true);
+     const url = URL.createObjectURL(file);
+     const image = new Image();
+     image.onload = () => {
+       URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
+       setSource(image);
+       setPlacement(CENTRED);
+       setBusy(false);
+     };
+     image.onerror = () => {
+       URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
+       setProblem(CANNOT_DECODE);
+       setBusy(false);
+     };
+     image.src = url;
+   }, []);
+
+   const onDrop = (event: React.DragEvent) => {
+     event.preventDefault();
+     setDragging(false);
+     const file = event.dataTransfer.files[0];
+     if (file) accept(file);
+   };
+
+   // Dragging inside the frame moves the photo within it.
+   const onPointerDown = (event: React.PointerEvent) => {
+     if (!source) return;
+     (event.target as HTMLElement).setPointerCapture(event.pointerId);
+     dragFrom.current = { x: event.clientX, y: event.clientY, placement };
+   };
+   const onPointerMove = (event: React.PointerEvent) => {
+     const from = dragFrom.current;
+     if (!from || !source) return;
+     const box = (event.currentTarget as HTMLElement).getBoundingClientRect();
+     setPlacement(clampPlacement({
+       zoom: from.placement.zoom,
+       // A full drag across the frame moves the photo the whole of its slack.
+       offsetX: from.placement.offsetX + ((event.clientX - from.x) / Math.max(1, box.width)) * 2,
+       offsetY: from.placement.offsetY + ((event.clientY - from.y) / Math.max(1, box.height)) * 2,
+     }));
+   };
+   const endDrag = () => { dragFrom.current = null; };
+
+   const clear = () => {
+     setSource(null);
+     setPlacement(CENTRED);
+     setProblem(undefined);
+     onChange(undefined);
+     if (inputRef.current) inputRef.current.value = '';
+   };
+
+   const storedBytes = portrait ? dataUrlBytes(portrait) : 0;
+
+   return (
+     <div className="portrait-picker">
+       <div
+         className="portrait-frame"
+         data-dragging={dragging ? 'true' : undefined}
+         data-empty={!source && !portrait ? 'true' : undefined}
+         onDragOver={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); setDragging(true); }}
+         onDragLeave={() => setDragging(false)}
+         onDrop={onDrop}
+         onPointerDown={onPointerDown}
+         onPointerMove={onPointerMove}
+         onPointerUp={endDrag}
+         onPointerCancel={endDrag}
+         title={source ? 'Drag to reposition' : undefined}
+       >
+         {/* The canvas is the picture: what is drawn here is exactly what is stored. */}
+         <canvas
+           ref={canvasRef}
+           width={PORTRAIT_WIDTH}
+           height={PORTRAIT_HEIGHT}
+           hidden={!source}
+           aria-label={source ? `Headshot for ${name || 'your character'}` : undefined}
+         />
+         {!source && portrait && <img src={portrait} alt={`Headshot for ${name || 'your character'}`} />}
+         {!source && !portrait && (
+           <button
+             type="button"
+             className="portrait-empty"
+             onClick={() => inputRef.current?.click()}
+           >
+             <UploadGlyph />
+             <span className="portrait-empty-title">Upload Custom Photo</span>
+             <span className="portrait-empty-note">
+               {busy ? 'Opening the photo…' : 'Tap here, or drop one in.'}
+             </span>
+           </button>
+         )}
+       </div>
+
+       <div className="portrait-controls">
+         <input
+           ref={inputRef}
+           id="portrait-file"
+           type="file"
+           accept="image/*"
+           className="visually-hidden"
+           onChange={(e) => { const f = e.target.files?.[0]; if (f) accept(f); }}
+         />
+         {/* The frame itself is the upload control now, so this is the plain
+             file-picker route rather than a second copy of the same words. */}
+         <label htmlFor="portrait-file" className="btn btn-sm">
+           {portrait || source ? 'Replace Photo' : 'Choose File'}
+         </label>
+         {(portrait || source) && (
+           <button type="button" className="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" onClick={clear}>Remove</button>
+         )}
+
+         {source && (
+           <div className="field portrait-zoom">
+             <label htmlFor="portrait-zoom">Zoom</label>
+             <input
+               id="portrait-zoom"
+               type="range"
+               min={1}
+               max={MAX_ZOOM}
+               step={0.02}
+               value={placement.zoom}
+               onChange={(e) => setPlacement((p) => clampPlacement({ ...p, zoom: Number(e.target.value) }))}
+             />
+           </div>
+         )}
+
+         <p className="hint" role={problem ? 'alert' : undefined}>
+           {problem
+             ? problem
+             : source
+               ? 'Drag the photo to move it in the frame, and use Zoom to size it.'
+               : storedBytes > 0
+                 ? `Saved at ${PORTRAIT_WIDTH}×${PORTRAIT_HEIGHT}, ${Math.round(storedBytes / 1024)}KB.`
+                 : 'Any size or shape works. SLATE crops it to a headshot and keeps a small copy in the save. It’s only for show: the game never looks at what’s in it.'}
+         </p>
+       </div>
+     </div>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * Tapping a part of the world.
+  *
+  * A hundred and seventy-four country outlines, drawn once and pointed at.
+  * Picking a country here does exactly what picking it from the list does — the
+  * map is a second way in, not a second source of truth — and the list stays
+  * the one that works with a keyboard, a screen reader, and for the small
+  * states and territories this scale of outline simply does not contain.
+  *
+  * The map is fetched when it is opened and never bundled.
+  */
+
+ import { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from 'react';
+ import { COUNTRIES, cityCount } from '@/engine/content/geography';
+ import {
+   boxFromCorners, frameBox, loadWorldMap, markerRadiusAt, projectPoint,
+   strokeAt, viewBoxOf, wholeWorld, type WorldMapData,
+ } from './world-map';
+
+ export function WorldMap({
+   countryId, marker, onPick,
+ }: {
+   /** The country currently chosen, highlighted and framed. */
+   countryId: string;
+   /** A point to mark — the chosen town, when there is one. */
+   marker?: { latitude: number; longitude: number; name: string } | undefined;
+   onPick: (countryId: string) => void;
+ }) {
+   const [data, setData] = useState<WorldMapData | null>(null);
+   const [problem, setProblem] = useState<string | undefined>();
+   const [hovered, setHovered] = useState<string | undefined>();
+   // The whole world, until somebody asks for a closer look. Framing the
+   // chosen country on open would put every other country off the canvas,
+   // which is the one thing a map for tapping countries must not do.
+   const [framed, setFramed] = useState(false);
+
+   useEffect(() => {
+     let cancelled = false;
+     loadWorldMap()
+       .then((loaded) => { if (!cancelled) setData(loaded); })
+       .catch((error: unknown) => {
+         if (!cancelled) {
+           setProblem(error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'The world map couldn’t be loaded.');
+         }
+       });
+     return () => { cancelled = true; };
+   }, []);
+
+   const ids = useMemo(() => (data ? Object.keys(data.countries).sort() : []), [data]);
+
+   const view = useMemo(() => {
+     if (!data) return null;
+     const world = wholeWorld(data);
+     if (!framed) return world;
+     const corners = data.bounds[countryId];
+     const box = corners ? boxFromCorners(corners) : null;
+     return box ? frameBox(box, data) : world;
+   }, [data, countryId, framed]);
+
+   if (problem) {
+     return (
+       <div className="worldmap-shell worldmap-empty">
+         <p className="hint" role="alert">{problem} Use the country list below instead.</p>
+       </div>
+     );
+   }
+
+   if (!data || !view) {
+     return (
+       <div className="worldmap-shell worldmap-empty">
+         <p className="hint">Drawing the world…</p>
+       </div>
+     );
+   }
+
+   const nameOf = (id: string) => COUNTRIES.get(id)?.name ?? data.names[id] ?? id;
+   const stroke = strokeAt(view, data);
+   const readout = hovered ?? countryId;
+   // The antimeridian is both edges of the map, so a marker just past it is
+   // looked for a turn either way before it is given up on.
+   const projected = marker ? projectPoint(marker.latitude, marker.longitude, data) : null;
+   const inView = (x: number) => x >= view.x && x <= view.x + view.width;
+   const markerX = projected === null
+     ? null
+     : [projected.x, projected.x + data.width, projected.x - data.width].find(inView) ?? null;
+   const showMarker = projected !== null && markerX !== null
+     && projected.y >= view.y && projected.y <= view.y + view.height;
+
+   return (
+     <div className="worldmap-shell">
+       <div className="worldmap-bar">
+         <span
+           className="worldmap-readout truncate"
+           title={readout
+             ? `${nameOf(readout)}${cityCount(readout) > 0 ? ` · ${cityCount(readout).toLocaleString('en-US')} places` : ''}`
+             : 'Tap anywhere on the map'}
+         >
+           {readout ? nameOf(readout) : 'Tap anywhere on the map'}
+           {readout && cityCount(readout) > 0 && (
+             <span className="dim"> · {cityCount(readout).toLocaleString('en-US')} places</span>
+           )}
+         </span>
+         <button
+           type="button"
+           className="btn btn-ghost btn-sm"
+           onClick={() => setFramed((on) => !on)}
+           disabled={!data.bounds[countryId]}
+         >
+           {framed ? 'Whole World' : 'Zoom In'}
+         </button>
+       </div>
+
+       <svg
+         className="worldmap"
+         viewBox={viewBoxOf(view)}
+         preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"
+         role="group"
+         aria-label="World map. Tap a country to choose it."
+         onPointerLeave={() => setHovered(undefined)}
+       >
+         <rect
+           className="worldmap-sea"
+           x={0} y={0} width={data.width} height={data.height}
+         />
+         {ids.map((id) => {
+           const known = cityCount(id) > 0;
+           return (
+             <path
+               key={id}
+               d={data.countries[id]}
+               className="worldmap-country"
+               data-selected={id === countryId ? 'true' : undefined}
+               data-empty={known ? undefined : 'true'}
+               strokeWidth={stroke}
+               role={known ? 'button' : undefined}
+               tabIndex={-1}
+               aria-label={known ? nameOf(id) : undefined}
+               onPointerEnter={() => setHovered(id)}
+               onClick={known ? () => onPick(id) : undefined}
+             >
+               <title>
+                 {known
+                   ? nameOf(id)
+                   : `${nameOf(id)}: no towns or cities on record`}
+               </title>
+             </path>
+           );
+         })}
+         {showMarker && projected && markerX !== null && (
+           <>
+             <circle
+               className="worldmap-marker-halo"
+               cx={markerX} cy={projected.y} r={markerRadiusAt(view, data) * 2.2}
+             />
+             <circle
+               className="worldmap-marker"
+               cx={markerX} cy={projected.y} r={markerRadiusAt(view, data)}
+             />
+           </>
+         )}
+       </svg>
+
+       <p className="worldmap-note xs dim">
+         {marker ? `${marker.name} is marked. ` : ''}
+         Outlines from {data.source} Countries too small to draw at this scale are still in the list below.
+       </p>
+     </div>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — headshots.
+  *
+  * A player brings whatever photo they have: a phone picture nine thousand
+  * pixels wide, a tiny avatar, a landscape crop, a portrait one. All of them
+  * have to end up as the same thing — one headshot, one shape, one modest file
+  * that fits inside a save.
+  *
+  * Everything in this file is pure arithmetic and validation, deliberately kept
+  * apart from the canvas work so the hard part — making any photo fit — can be
+  * tested rather than eyeballed.
+  */
+
+ /**
+  * The frame every headshot ends up in.
+  *
+  * Four by five, because that is the shape a performer's headshot has been since
+  * eight-by-tens, and 512 across because it stays sharp on a retina screen at
+  * the size it is actually shown while staying small enough to live in a save.
+  */
+ export const PORTRAIT_WIDTH = 512;
+ export const PORTRAIT_HEIGHT = 640;
+ export const PORTRAIT_ASPECT = PORTRAIT_WIDTH / PORTRAIT_HEIGHT;
+
+ /** Anything larger than this is refused before it is decoded. */
+ export const MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 24 * 1024 * 1024;
+
+ /** Formats a browser can reliably decode and re-encode. */
+ export const ACCEPTED_TYPES = [
+   'image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/webp', 'image/gif', 'image/bmp', 'image/avif',
+ ] as const;
+
+ /** How far in the player may zoom past the fitted size. */
+ export const MAX_ZOOM = 4;
+
+ export interface Placement {
+   /** Multiplier on the cover-fit scale. 1 is exactly filling the frame. */
+   zoom: number;
+   /** Where the image sits, as a fraction of the slack in each direction. */
+   offsetX: number;
+   offsetY: number;
+ }
+
+ export const CENTRED: Placement = { zoom: 1, offsetX: 0, offsetY: 0 };
+
+ export interface DrawRect {
+   x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number;
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * The two things that go wrong after a file has been accepted, said the same
+  * way wherever a photo is framed: the headshot picker and the phone's.
+  */
+ export const CANNOT_ENCODE = 'That photo couldn’t be saved. Try a different one.';
+ export const CANNOT_DECODE = 'That photo couldn’t be opened. It may be damaged, so try a different one.';
+
+ /** Why a file was refused, in words a player can act on. */
+ export function describeRejection(file: { type: string; size: number; name: string }): string | null {
+   if (!file.type.startsWith('image/')) {
+     return `${file.name || 'That file'} isn’t an image. Choose a JPEG, PNG or WebP photo.`;
+   }
+   if (!(ACCEPTED_TYPES as readonly string[]).includes(file.type)) {
+     return `${file.type.replace('image/', '').toUpperCase()} images aren’t supported. Try a JPEG, PNG or WebP.`;
+   }
+   if (file.size > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES) {
+     return `That photo is ${(file.size / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(1)}MB, over the ${MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES / 1024 / 1024}MB limit. Try a smaller one.`;
+   }
+   if (file.size === 0) {
+     return 'That file is empty. Choose a different photo.';
+   }
+   return null;
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * The scale at which an image of these dimensions just covers the frame.
+  *
+  * Cover rather than contain: a headshot with letterboxing down the sides is
+  * not a headshot. The wider-relative-to-the-frame the source is, the more its
+  * sides are cropped, and the reverse for a tall one.
+  */
+ export function coverScale(sourceWidth: number, sourceHeight: number, frameWidth = PORTRAIT_WIDTH, frameHeight = PORTRAIT_HEIGHT): number {
+   // A decode that went wrong can report zero, a negative, or NaN. None of
+   // those may be allowed to become a NaN rectangle further down.
+   if (!usableDimension(sourceWidth) || !usableDimension(sourceHeight)) return 1;
+   return Math.max(frameWidth / sourceWidth, frameHeight / sourceHeight);
+ }
+
+ /** Whether a reported dimension is something we can compute with. */
+ function usableDimension(value: number): boolean {
+   return Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0;
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * How far the image may slide in each direction before its edge would come
+  * inside the frame. Zero on an axis means that axis exactly fits and cannot
+  * move — which is what happens to the short side of a cover fit at zoom 1.
+  */
+ export function slack(sourceWidth: number, sourceHeight: number, placement: Placement, frameWidth = PORTRAIT_WIDTH, frameHeight = PORTRAIT_HEIGHT): { x: number; y: number } {
+   if (!usableDimension(sourceWidth) || !usableDimension(sourceHeight)) return { x: 0, y: 0 };
+   const scale = coverScale(sourceWidth, sourceHeight, frameWidth, frameHeight) * Math.max(1, placement.zoom);
+   return {
+     x: Math.max(0, (sourceWidth * scale - frameWidth) / 2),
+     y: Math.max(0, (sourceHeight * scale - frameHeight) / 2),
+   };
+ }
+
+ /** Keeps a placement inside what the image can actually cover. */
+ export function clampPlacement(placement: Placement): Placement {
+   return {
+     zoom: Math.min(MAX_ZOOM, Math.max(1, Number.isFinite(placement.zoom) ? placement.zoom : 1)),
+     offsetX: Math.min(1, Math.max(-1, Number.isFinite(placement.offsetX) ? placement.offsetX : 0)),
+     offsetY: Math.min(1, Math.max(-1, Number.isFinite(placement.offsetY) ? placement.offsetY : 0)),
+   };
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * Where to draw the source image so it covers the frame under this placement.
+  *
+  * The result is always at least as large as the frame in both directions and
+  * always overlaps it, whatever the source's shape — which is the whole promise
+  * of "any photo fits".
+  */
+ export function drawRect(
+   sourceWidth: number,
+   sourceHeight: number,
+   placement: Placement = CENTRED,
+   frameWidth = PORTRAIT_WIDTH,
+   frameHeight = PORTRAIT_HEIGHT,
+ ): DrawRect {
+   const safe = clampPlacement(placement);
+   // Fall back to the frame's own shape when the source did not report a usable
+   // size, so a broken image yields a plain filled frame rather than nonsense.
+   const width0 = usableDimension(sourceWidth) ? sourceWidth : frameWidth;
+   const height0 = usableDimension(sourceHeight) ? sourceHeight : frameHeight;
+
+   const scale = coverScale(width0, height0, frameWidth, frameHeight) * safe.zoom;
+   const width = width0 * scale;
+   const height = height0 * scale;
+   const room = slack(width0, height0, safe, frameWidth, frameHeight);
+
+   return {
+     x: (frameWidth - width) / 2 + room.x * safe.offsetX,
+     y: (frameHeight - height) / 2 + room.y * safe.offsetY,
+     width,
+     height,
+   };
+ }
+
+ /** Roughly how many bytes a data URL of this length occupies once decoded. */
+ export function dataUrlBytes(dataUrl: string): number {
+   const comma = dataUrl.indexOf(',');
+   if (comma < 0) return 0;
+   const body = dataUrl.slice(comma + 1);
+   const padding = body.endsWith('==') ? 2 : body.endsWith('=') ? 1 : 0;
+   return Math.max(0, Math.floor((body.length * 3) / 4) - padding);
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * The world map, as geometry.
+  *
+  * Everything here is arithmetic on a fixed equirectangular surface: no React,
+  * no DOM, no network beyond the one fetch. The outlines themselves are Natural
+  * Earth's, projected at build time by tools/build-world-map.mjs and served from
+  * public/geo, because an outline of every country on Earth belongs in a file
+  * that is fetched when somebody opens a map rather than in the bundle.
+  *
+  * The projection is a convenience for pointing at a country, not a claim about
+  * area. Greenland is the size Mercator's cousins always make it. Nothing in the
+  * simulation reads these coordinates; they exist so a tap can become a country.
+  */
+
+ /** A rectangle on the map surface. */
+ export interface Box {
+   x: number;
+   y: number;
+   width: number;
+   height: number;
+ }
+
+ export interface WorldMapData {
+   /** The surface the paths are drawn on. */
+   width: number;
+   height: number;
+   projection: string;
+   /** Provenance of the outlines. Shown to the player. */
+   source: string;
+   /** SVG path data by SLATE country id. */
+   countries: Record<string, string>;
+   /** Country names as the source spells them. SLATE's own names win. */
+   names: Record<string, string>;
+   /** [x1, y1, x2, y2] framing each country. */
+   bounds: Record<string, [number, number, number, number]>;
+ }
+
+ /** Longitude and latitude onto the surface. The projection, in one place. */
+ export function projectPoint(
+   latitude: number,
+   longitude: number,
+   surface: { width: number; height: number },
+ ): { x: number; y: number } {
+   const lon = wrapLongitude(longitude);
+   const lat = Math.max(-90, Math.min(90, latitude));
+   return {
+     x: ((lon + 180) / 360) * surface.width,
+     y: ((90 - lat) / 180) * surface.height,
+   };
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * Longitude folded back into [-180, 180], however many turns out it was.
+  *
+  * The antimeridian is both ends of the map at once. A point given as 180 stays
+  * at the right-hand edge rather than being folded to the left one, so a marker
+  * on it lands next to the country it belongs to instead of an ocean away.
+  */
+ export function wrapLongitude(longitude: number): number {
+   if (!Number.isFinite(longitude)) return 0;
+   const folded = ((longitude + 180) % 360 + 360) % 360 - 180;
+   return folded === -180 && longitude > 0 ? 180 : folded;
+ }
+
+ /** The whole surface as a box. */
+ export function wholeWorld(surface: { width: number; height: number }): Box {
+   return { x: 0, y: 0, width: surface.width, height: surface.height };
+ }
+
+ /** A stored [x1, y1, x2, y2] pair of corners as a box. */
+ export function boxFromCorners(corners: readonly number[]): Box | null {
+   const [x1, y1, x2, y2] = corners;
+   if (x1 === undefined || y1 === undefined || x2 === undefined || y2 === undefined) return null;
+   if (![x1, y1, x2, y2].every(Number.isFinite)) return null;
+   return {
+     x: Math.min(x1, x2),
+     y: Math.min(y1, y2),
+     width: Math.abs(x2 - x1),
+     height: Math.abs(y2 - y1),
+   };
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * A view of the given box, at the surface's shape, inside the surface.
+  *
+  * Three things at once, because they only make sense together: a country is
+  * not the shape of the viewport, so the box grows to match; a country the size
+  * of Monaco would be a view no bigger than a full stop, so it is never allowed
+  * below a floor; and the result is slid back inside the surface rather than
+  * showing empty space past the edge of the world.
+  */
+ export function frameBox(
+   target: Box,
+   surface: { width: number; height: number },
+   options: { padding?: number; minimumWidth?: number } = {},
+ ): Box {
+   const padding = options.padding ?? 0.25;
+   const minimumWidth = options.minimumWidth ?? surface.width * 0.06;
+   const aspect = surface.width / surface.height;
+
+   const centreX = target.x + target.width / 2;
+   const centreY = target.y + target.height / 2;
+
+   let width = Math.max(target.width * (1 + padding * 2), minimumWidth);
+   let height = Math.max(target.height * (1 + padding * 2), minimumWidth / aspect);
+
+   // Grow the short side until the view is the shape of the viewport.
+   if (width / height < aspect) width = height * aspect;
+   else height = width / aspect;
+
+   // Never larger than the world, and never outside it.
+   if (width > surface.width) { width = surface.width; height = width / aspect; }
+   if (height > surface.height) { height = surface.height; width = height * aspect; }
+
+   const x = Math.max(0, Math.min(surface.width - width, centreX - width / 2));
+   const y = Math.max(0, Math.min(surface.height - height, centreY - height / 2));
+   return { x, y, width, height };
+ }
+
+ /** A box as an SVG viewBox attribute. */
+ export function viewBoxOf(box: Box): string {
+   const round = (n: number) => Number(n.toFixed(2));
+   return `${round(box.x)} ${round(box.y)} ${round(box.width)} ${round(box.height)}`;
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * How thick a hairline should be drawn at this zoom.
+  *
+  * Strokes are scaled with the view so that borders stay a hairline whether the
+  * view is the whole world or one province of it, rather than swelling into
+  * blobs the moment somebody zooms in.
+  */
+ export function strokeAt(box: Box, surface: { width: number }): number {
+   const zoom = surface.width / Math.max(box.width, 1);
+   return Number(Math.max(0.25, 1.4 / zoom).toFixed(3));
+ }
+
+ /** Marker radius, likewise kept the same visual size at any zoom. */
+ export function markerRadiusAt(box: Box, surface: { width: number }): number {
+   const zoom = surface.width / Math.max(box.width, 1);
+   return Number(Math.max(1.8, 10 / zoom).toFixed(3));
+ }
+
+ /** Where the outlines live. Fetched once; asking again is free. */
+ const MAP_URL = `${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}geo/world-map.json`;
+
+ let pending: Promise<WorldMapData> | null = null;
+
+ /**
+  * Pulls the outlines in.
+  *
+  * One request for the whole world, shared by every map on the page and kept
+  * for the rest of the session. A failure is left to the caller to report;
+  * the map is a convenience and the country list works without it.
+  */
+ export function loadWorldMap(): Promise<WorldMapData> {
+   if (pending) return pending;
+   pending = fetch(MAP_URL)
+     .then((response) => {
+       if (!response.ok) throw new Error('The world map couldn’t be loaded.');
+       return response.json() as Promise<WorldMapData>;
+     })
+     .then((data) => {
+       if (!data?.countries || !data.width || !data.height) {
+         throw new Error('The world map file isn’t readable.');
+       }
+       return data;
+     })
+     .catch((error: unknown) => {
+       pending = null;
+       throw error instanceof Error ? error : new Error('The world map couldn’t be loaded.');
+     });
+   return pending;
+ }
+
+ /** Forgets the cached map. Tests only; nothing in the game calls it. */
+ export function forgetWorldMap(): void {
+   pending = null;
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — the guide on screen.
+  *
+  * A new life starts with everything shut but the guide, which opens on the
+  * first chapter by itself. Each chapter says what one part of the game does,
+  * and "I’ve Read It" opens it: the buttons wake, the panels on Home fill in,
+  * and the underlined words start opening. Then the guide says what opened
+  * and offers the next chapter, or the chance to try what just opened first.
+  *
+  * A locked control still shows, so the life ahead is visible; pressed, it
+  * opens the guide at the chapter that opens it. The engine refuses the
+  * command behind it as well (`world/tutorial.ts`), so the lock isn’t only
+  * paint.
+  *
+  * Words only, as the rail is: a locked thing says Locked, not a padlock.
+  *
+  * From 2026-10-12 every chapter can be opened and read at any time, and only the next one can be marked read, so a
+  * player can see what a later part of the game does before getting there; until then the later chapters were shut in
+  * the contents. The clock holds while the guide is open. The counts count only the chapters there are now: a save
+  * from before the chapters were cut to these seventeen still holds the old ones' ids.
+  *
+  * From 2026-10-17 (the owner's brief 14) a chapter's figures and finer conditions (`more`) are behind The Details,
+  * under its steps, so a chapter reads as a task first: until then every chapter was one run of paragraphs.
+  */
+
+ import { createContext, useCallback, useContext, useEffect, useMemo, useState, type ButtonHTMLAttributes, type ReactNode } from 'react';
+ import { useGame, useWorld } from '@/app/game-context';
+ import { Modal } from '@/ui/components/primitives';
+ import { CHAPTERS, CHAPTER_BY_ID } from '@/engine/content/tutorial';
+ import { READ_KIND, chapterFor, chaptersRead, guided, isOpen, lockedBecause, nextChapter } from '@/engine/world/tutorial';
+
+ interface GuideApi {
+   /** Opens the guide, at a chapter or at the next one. */
+   show: (chapterId?: string) => void;
+ }
+
+ const GuideContext = createContext<GuideApi>({ show: () => {} });
+
+ export function useGuide(): GuideApi {
+   return useContext(GuideContext);
+ }
+
+ /** Whether a part of the game is open, and what to say while it isn’t. */
+ export function useFeature(feature: string): { open: boolean; reason?: string; ask: () => void } {
+   const guide = useGuide();
+   const open = useWorld((s) => isOpen(s, feature), [feature]);
+   const reason = useWorld((s) => lockedBecause(s, feature), [feature]);
+   const ask = useCallback(() => guide.show(chapterFor(feature)?.id), [guide, feature]);
+   return { open, reason, ask };
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * The guide itself, and everything under it that can ask for it. Opens on
+  * its own when a guided life hasn’t read a chapter yet.
+  */
+ export function GuideProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
+   const [showing, setShowing] = useState<string | null>(null);
+   const fresh = useWorld((s) => guided(s) && chaptersRead(s).length === 0);
+
+   useEffect(() => {
+     if (fresh) setShowing(CHAPTERS[0]!.id);
+     // Only on arriving: closing it isn't undone by the next render.
+     // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
+   }, []);
+
+   const api = useMemo<GuideApi>(() => ({
+     show: (chapterId) => setShowing(chapterId ?? ''),
+   }), []);
+
+   return (
+     <GuideContext.Provider value={api}>
+       {children}
+       {showing !== null && <GuideDialog start={showing} onClose={() => setShowing(null)} />}
+     </GuideContext.Provider>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * A button for a part of the game the guide opens. Open, it is the button.
+  * Locked, it shows as locked and opens the guide at its chapter.
+  */
+ export function Gated({
+   feature, className = 'btn btn-sm', onClick, children, title, ...rest
+ }: { feature: string } & ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>) {
+   const { open, reason, ask } = useFeature(feature);
+   if (open) {
+     return <button type="button" className={className} onClick={onClick} title={title} {...rest}>{children}</button>;
+   }
+   return (
+     <button
+       type="button"
+       {...rest}
+       disabled={false}
+       className={`${className} is-locked`}
+       title={reason}
+       onClick={ask}
+     >
+       {children}
+       <span className="lock-word">Locked</span>
+     </button>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * A panel on Home before its chapter is read: its name, what it shows, and the chapter that opens it.
+  *
+  * Until 2026-10-20 (brief 17, the frame editor's finding) it said only the chapter's lead after the chapter's title,
+  * which is the chapter's subject and not the panel's: on a first Home, Where You Are's ended with chapter 1's, “how
+  * SLATE works, and how to read Home”. Each panel says what it shows now, read from what Home draws in it.
+  */
+ export function LockedPanel({ feature, title }: { feature: string; title: string }) {
+   const { open, ask } = useFeature(feature);
+   const chapter = chapterFor(feature);
+   if (open || !chapter) return null;
+   const shows: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
+     'ui.calendar': 'What’s coming up, and when.',
+     'ui.needs': 'What happened while you weren’t looking, and the questions waiting on you.',
+     'ui.how': 'Your energy, stress and readiness, and a line on how you are.',
+     'ui.where': 'The town you live in, its local time and its daylight.',
+     'ui.weather': 'The weather in your town, today and the days ahead.',
+     'ui.money': 'What your main account holds, and what you’re worth after what you owe.',
+     'ui.school': 'Your year at the School, your standing, your place in the class and what’s next.',
+     'ui.papers': 'Your health cover, and any tax return due, tax owed or unemployment you’re paid.',
+   };
+   return (
+     <section className="card card-tight panel-locked" aria-label={`${title}, Locked`}>
+       <div className="panel-head">
+         <div><h2>{title}</h2></div>
+         <span className="lock-word">Locked</span>
+       </div>
+       <p className="small muted" style={{ margin: '0 0 var(--s3)' }}>
+         {shows[feature] ?? chapter.lead} It opens when you read “{chapter.title}” in the guide.
+       </p>
+       <button type="button" className="btn btn-sm" onClick={ask}>Read About It</button>
+     </section>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * Where the guide is, under the bar, until every chapter is read: the next
+  * chapter and the way into it.
+  */
+ export function GuideStrip() {
+   const guide = useGuide();
+   const next = useWorld((s) => (guided(s) ? nextChapter(s) : undefined));
+   const done = useWorld((s) => readNow(s).length);
+   if (!next) return null;
+   return (
+     <div className="guide-strip" role="status">
+       <span className="small">
+         <span className="eyebrow">Guide · {done + 1} Of {CHAPTERS.length}</span>{' '}
+         <strong>{next.title}</strong>
+         <span className="muted hide-sm"> · {next.lead}</span>
+       </span>
+       <button type="button" className="btn btn-sm btn-primary" onClick={() => guide.show(next.id)}>Read</button>
+     </div>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /** The top bar’s way back into the guide, for any chapter, any time. */
+ export function GuideButton() {
+   const guide = useGuide();
+   // None left on a guide finished, whatever came after it was read through (from 2026-10-13: until then it counted
+   // chapters added later, which a finished guide offers no way to take; found by the review of that day).
+   const left = useWorld((s) => (s.universe.tutorial?.finished ? 0 : CHAPTERS.length - readNow(s).length));
+   return (
+     <button type="button" className="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" onClick={() => guide.show()}>
+       Guide{left > 0 ? ` (${left} Left)` : ''}
+     </button>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /** The chapters read that are chapters now. */
+ const readNow = (s: Parameters<typeof chaptersRead>[0]) => chaptersRead(s).filter((id) => CHAPTER_BY_ID[id]);
+
+ function GuideDialog({ start, onClose }: { start: string; onClose: () => void }) {
+   const { run, hold } = useGame();
+   useEffect(() => { hold('guide', true); return () => hold('guide', false); }, [hold]);
+   const read = useWorld((s) => chaptersRead(s));
+   const next = useWorld((s) => nextChapter(s));
+   const isGuided = useWorld((s) => guided(s));
+   // A guide finished leaves a chapter added after it open and unread for good: there’s no I’ve Read It for it, and what
+   // it names is open already. Until 2026-10-13 it was listed as Later, over What Reading It Opens (What It Opens from
+   // 2026-10-19, brief 15).
+   const finished = useWorld((s) => Boolean(s.universe.tutorial?.finished));
+   // An empty start is the next chapter; any chapter asked for opens, to read.
+   const [at, setAt] = useState(() => CHAPTER_BY_ID[start]?.id ?? next?.id ?? CHAPTERS[0]!.id);
+   // The chapter asked for, when it had to wait for another.
+   const [waiting] = useState(() => {
+     const asked = CHAPTER_BY_ID[start];
+     return asked && !read.includes(asked.id) && asked.id !== next?.id ? asked : undefined;
+   });
+   const [justOpened, setJustOpened] = useState<string | null>(null);
+
+   const chapter = CHAPTER_BY_ID[at]!;
+   const index = CHAPTERS.findIndex((c) => c.id === at);
+   const isNext = next?.id === at && isGuided;
+   const opened = justOpened ? CHAPTER_BY_ID[justOpened] : undefined;
+
+   const markRead = () => {
+     const answer = run<{ read: string; next?: string }>(READ_KIND, { chapterId: chapter.id });
+     if (answer.ok) setJustOpened(chapter.id);
+   };
+   const goTo = (id: string) => { setJustOpened(null); setAt(id); };
+
+   const footer = opened ? (
+     <>
+       <button className="btn" onClick={onClose}>Try It</button>
+       {next
+         ? <button className="btn btn-primary" onClick={() => goTo(next.id)}>Next: {next.title}</button>
+         : <button className="btn btn-primary" onClick={onClose}>Start Playing</button>}
+     </>
+   ) : isNext ? (
+     <>
+       <button className="btn" onClick={onClose}>Later</button>
+       <button className="btn btn-primary" onClick={markRead}>I’ve Read It</button>
+     </>
+   ) : (
+     <>
+       <button className="btn" onClick={onClose}>Close</button>
+       {next && next.id !== at && (
+         <button className="btn btn-primary" onClick={() => goTo(next.id)}>Next Unread: {next.title}</button>
+       )}
+     </>
+   );
+
+   return (
+     <Modal title="Guide" onClose={onClose} wide footer={footer}>
+       <div className="guide">
+         <nav className="guide-toc" aria-label="Chapters">
+           {CHAPTERS.map((c, i) => {
+             const status = read.includes(c.id) ? 'Read' : next?.id === c.id ? 'Next' : finished ? 'Open' : 'Later';
+             return (
+               <button
+                 key={c.id}
+                 type="button"
+                 className="guide-toc-item"
+                 aria-current={c.id === at ? 'step' : undefined}
+                 aria-label={`${i + 1}. ${c.title}, ${status}`}
+                 onClick={() => goTo(c.id)}
+               >
+                 <span className="guide-toc-num mono">{i + 1}</span>
+                 <span className="grow truncate">{c.title}</span>
+                 <span className="xs dim">{status}</span>
+               </button>
+             );
+           })}
+         </nav>
+
+         <article className="guide-page">
+           {opened ? (
+             <>
+               <div className="eyebrow">Opened</div>
+               <h3 style={{ margin: 'var(--s1) 0 var(--s3)' }}>{opened.title}</h3>
+               <ul className="small guide-opens">
+                 {opened.names.map((name) => <li key={name}>{name}</li>)}
+               </ul>
+               <p className="small muted">
+                 {next
+                   ? `It’s open now. Press Try It to go and use it, or go straight on to “${next.title}”. Next time you open the guide, it starts there.`
+                   : 'That was the last chapter, and every part of the game is open now. To read any chapter again, press Guide at the top of the screen.'}
+               </p>
+             </>
+           ) : (
+             <>
+               {waiting && at === waiting.id && next && (
+                 <div className="callout small" style={{ marginBottom: 'var(--s3)' }}>
+                   This chapter opens what you pressed. The chapters open in order, so read “{next.title}” first.
+                 </div>
+               )}
+               {!isNext && isGuided && !read.includes(chapter.id) && !waiting && next && (
+                 <div className="callout small" style={{ marginBottom: 'var(--s3)' }}>
+                   You can read ahead, but the chapters open in order, and “{next.title}” is next.
+                 </div>
+               )}
+               <div className="eyebrow">Chapter {index + 1} Of {CHAPTERS.length}</div>
+               <h3 style={{ margin: 'var(--s1) 0 var(--s1)' }}>{chapter.title}</h3>
+               <p className="small muted" style={{ marginTop: 0 }}>{chapter.lead}</p>
+               {chapter.body.map((paragraph) => <p key={paragraph} className="small">{paragraph}</p>)}
+               {chapter.more && chapter.more.length > 0 && (
+                 <details className="help-section guide-more">
+                   <summary>The Details</summary>
+                   <div className="help-section-body">
+                     {chapter.more.map((paragraph) => <p key={paragraph} className="small">{paragraph}</p>)}
+                   </div>
+                 </details>
+               )}
+               <div className="guide-opens-box">
+                 <div className="eyebrow">{read.includes(chapter.id) ? 'What It Opened' : finished ? 'What It Covers, Already Open' : 'What It Opens'}</div>
+                 <ul className="small guide-opens">
+                   {chapter.names.map((name) => <li key={name}>{name}</li>)}
+                 </ul>
+               </div>
+             </>
+           )}
+         </article>
+       </div>
+     </Modal>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — the guide's reference on screen (from 2026-10-12; `content/guide/`).
+  *
+  * The chapters are the onboarding (`Guide.tsx`). This is the rest: an entry for every feature, opened from How This
+  * Works beside it, from ? (the contents, by what the player is trying to do) or / (search) anywhere, or from an
+  * address (`#/workspace/school?help=coursework.partners`), so an entry can be linked to. Until 2026-10-13 that example
+  * named `school.partners`, which is no entry and covers no feature, so its link opened nothing. Inside, every entry
+  * links to the entries it's connected to, a trail of breadcrumbs goes back along the way it came, and Back goes back one.
+  *
+  * What it doesn't do is as much the point. It runs no command and writes nothing to the save. The live clock holds
+  * while it's open (`hold`), so reading moves no time. It opens over the screen, which stays mounted with its tab and
+  * whatever was typed in it, and closing it gives focus back to the control that opened it. Until 2026-10-13 that wasn’t
+  * so for the top bar’s Advance and Look After Yourself menus: the first press in the help, or Escape, closed the menu
+  * under it, and the How This Works it was opened from went with it, so focus fell to the page (`useDropdown`,
+  * `ui/shell/TimeControls.tsx`). Show Me Where is the one thing in it that moves the player: it goes to the entry's
+  * screen and tab, and Back To Help returns to the trail. `tests/help-mechanics.test.ts` presses each of them.
+  *
+  * From 2026-10-17 (the owner's brief 14): an entry reads in the order of the brief's eight questions, what it's for,
+  * where to find it, what to press, what you need first, what happens, how it connects, what to do next and what if you
+  * can't, with what decides it and the worked example last. Until then its sections ran Steps, What It Needs, Time And
+  * Money, What The Game Reads, then what changed, with Connected Systems near the end and nothing on what to do next.
+  * Show Me Where leaves a way back to the screen and tab the player was on as well as to the help, and the contents open
+  * with the entries for the screen the help was opened on, each marked Locked where its chapter isn't read.
+  */
+
+ import { useCallback, useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
+ import { useGame, useWorld } from '@/app/game-context';
+ import { Modal, dialogOpen } from '@/ui/components/primitives';
+ import { GOALS, GUIDE_BY_ID, SEARCH_EXAMPLES, connectionsTo, entriesOf, entryFor, search, type ConnectionKind, type Fact, type GuideEntry } from '@/engine/content/guide';
+ import { CHAPTERS } from '@/engine/content/tutorial';
+ import { chapterFor, chaptersRead, guided, isOpen } from '@/engine/world/tutorial';
+ import { kept } from '@/ui/kept';
+ import { ALL_DESTINATIONS } from '@/ui/shell/destinations';
+ import { SECTIONS, tabKey } from '@/ui/shell/sections';
+ import { HelpContext, type HelpApi } from './help-context';
+ import { useGuide } from './Guide';
+
+ type Page = { kind: 'contents' } | { kind: 'search'; q: string } | { kind: 'entry'; id: string };
+
+ const pageLabel = (p: Page): string => (p.kind === 'contents' ? 'Contents' : p.kind === 'search' ? (p.q ? `Search: ${p.q}` : 'Search') : GUIDE_BY_ID[p.id]?.title ?? p.id);
+
+ /** Each kind of connection, as a heading under How It Connects, in the order a player meets them. */
+ export const CONNECTION_HEADING: Readonly<Record<ConnectionKind, string>> = {
+   prerequisite: 'Comes First',
+   immediate: 'Changes Straight Away',
+   scheduled: 'Changes Later',
+   evaluation: 'Counts Toward',
+   history: 'Kept In Your Record',
+   optional: 'Worth Doing With It',
+ };
+ const KIND_ORDER: readonly ConnectionKind[] = ['prerequisite', 'immediate', 'scheduled', 'evaluation', 'history', 'optional'];
+
+ /** The screen the address names, as `writeAddress` reads it: Home when it names none. */
+ function screenInAddress(): string {
+   const hash = typeof window === 'undefined' ? '' : window.location?.hash ?? '';
+   return hash.startsWith('#/') ? hash.slice(1).split('?')[0]! : '/home';
+ }
+
+ /** A screen's name, as the rail and Home name it. */
+ const SCREEN_NAME: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = Object.fromEntries([['/home', 'Home'], ...ALL_DESTINATIONS.map((d) => [d.route, d.label])]);
+ const screenName = (route: string): string => SCREEN_NAME[route] ?? 'The Last Screen';
+
+ /** Where the player stood when Show Me Where moved them: the screen, and the tab it had showing. */
+ interface Place { route: string; tab?: string }
+
+ /** The address's help entry, if it names one. */
+ function helpInAddress(): string | undefined {
+   const q = window.location.hash.split('?')[1];
+   const id = q ? new URLSearchParams(q).get('help') : null;
+   return id && entryFor(id) ? entryFor(id)!.id : undefined;
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * The address with its help entry set, or taken out: the screen and anything else in it are kept as they are.
+  *
+  * Until 2026-10-13 it wrote the screen the provider held instead, which on a page’s first commit is still Home: React
+  * runs a child’s effects before its parent’s, so this one ran before `GameProvider` had read the address, and a reload
+  * or a link to `#/workspace/school` was rewritten to `#/home` and opened Home, with any entry it named open over it
+  * (found by the guide audit of that day). The address is the screen’s own by the time the trail changes after that:
+  * `navigate` pushes it before this runs, so Show Me Where and Back To Help write the screen they arrive at.
+  */
+ function writeAddress(entry?: string): void {
+   const [path, query] = (window.location.hash.startsWith('#/') ? window.location.hash.slice(1) : '/home').split('?') as [string, string | undefined];
+   const params = new URLSearchParams(query ?? '');
+   if (entry) params.set('help', entry);
+   else params.delete('help');
+   const rest = params.toString();
+   try { window.history.replaceState(window.history.state, '', `#${path}${rest ? `?${rest}` : ''}`); } catch { /* no address to keep */ }
+ }
+
+ export function HelpProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
+   const { hold, navigate } = useGame();
+   const [trail, setTrail] = useState<Page[] | null>(() => {
+     const id = helpInAddress();
+     return id ? [{ kind: 'contents' }, { kind: 'entry', id }] : null;
+   });
+   // The trail left by Show Me Where, for Back To Help, and the place it was pressed from, for the way back there.
+   const [left, setLeft] = useState<Page[] | null>(null);
+   const [from, setFrom] = useState<Place | null>(null);
+
+   const open = useCallback<HelpApi['open']>((id) => {
+     const entry = id ? entryFor(id) : undefined;
+     setLeft(null);
+     setTrail((t) => {
+       const base = t ?? [{ kind: 'contents' } as Page];
+       if (!entry) return t ? t : base;
+       const top = base[base.length - 1];
+       return top?.kind === 'entry' && top.id === entry.id ? base : [...base, { kind: 'entry', id: entry.id }];
+     });
+   }, []);
+   const find = useCallback<HelpApi['find']>((words = '') => {
+     setLeft(null);
+     setTrail((t) => [...(t ?? [{ kind: 'contents' } as Page]), { kind: 'search', q: words }]);
+   }, []);
+   const api = useMemo<HelpApi>(() => ({ open, find }), [open, find]);
+
+   const showing = trail !== null;
+   // The clock holds while the reference is open.
+   useEffect(() => { hold('help', showing); return () => hold('help', false); }, [hold, showing]);
+   // The address names the entry on top, so it can be copied or reloaded; closed, it's the screen's own again.
+   const top = trail?.[trail.length - 1];
+   useEffect(() => { writeAddress(top?.kind === 'entry' ? top.id : undefined); }, [top]);
+
+   // ? for the contents, / to search, anywhere but a text box, and not behind another dialog.
+   useEffect(() => {
+     const onKey = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
+       const target = event.target as HTMLElement | null;
+       if (target && ['INPUT', 'TEXTAREA', 'SELECT'].includes(target.tagName)) return;
+       if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.altKey || dialogOpen()) return;
+       if (event.key === '?') { event.preventDefault(); open(); }
+       else if (event.key === '/') { event.preventDefault(); find(); }
+     };
+     window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey);
+     return () => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey);
+   }, [open, find]);
+
+   const close = useCallback(() => setTrail(null), []);
+   const goWhere = useCallback((e: GuideEntry) => {
+     const here = screenInAddress();
+     const tab = kept<string>(tabKey(here));
+     setLeft(trail);
+     // Gone somewhere else, the way back is offered; to the place the player already stood, it isn't.
+     setFrom(here === e.where.route && (!e.where.tab || e.where.tab === (tab ?? SECTIONS[here]?.[0]?.id)) ? null : { route: here, tab });
+     setTrail(null);
+     navigate(`${e.where.route}${e.where.tab ? `?tab=${e.where.tab}` : ''}`);
+   }, [navigate, trail]);
+   const goBack = useCallback((place: Place) => {
+     setLeft(null);
+     setFrom(null);
+     navigate(`${place.route}${place.tab ? `?tab=${place.tab}` : ''}`, screenName(place.route));
+   }, [navigate]);
+
+   return (
+     <HelpContext.Provider value={api}>
+       {children}
+       {trail && <HelpDialog trail={trail} setTrail={setTrail} onClose={close} onWhere={goWhere} />}
+       {!trail && left && (
+         <div className="help-return" role="status">
+           <button type="button" className="btn btn-sm btn-primary" onClick={() => { setTrail(left); setLeft(null); setFrom(null); }}>Back To Help</button>
+           {from && <button type="button" className="btn btn-sm" onClick={() => goBack(from)}>Back To {screenName(from.route)}</button>}
+           <button type="button" className="btn btn-sm btn-ghost" aria-label="Dismiss Back To Help" onClick={() => { setLeft(null); setFrom(null); }}>✕</button>
+         </div>
+       )}
+     </HelpContext.Provider>
+   );
+ }
+
+ function HelpDialog({ trail, setTrail, onClose, onWhere }: {
+   trail: Page[]; setTrail: (t: Page[]) => void; onClose: () => void; onWhere: (e: GuideEntry) => void;
+ }) {
+   const page = trail[trail.length - 1]!;
+   const push = (p: Page) => setTrail([...trail, p]);
+   const back = () => { if (trail.length > 1) setTrail(trail.slice(0, -1)); };
+   const [q, setQ] = useState(page.kind === 'search' ? page.q : '');
+   useEffect(() => { if (page.kind === 'search') setQ(page.q); }, [page]);
+   const body = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
+   useEffect(() => { body.current?.scrollTo?.({ top: 0 }); }, [page]);
+
+   const submit = (words: string) => {
+     if (page.kind === 'search') setTrail([...trail.slice(0, -1), { kind: 'search', q: words }]);
+     else push({ kind: 'search', q: words });
+   };
+
+   const footer = (
+     <>
+       <span className="xs dim grow" data-clock-held="">The clock waits while you read.</span>
+       {trail.length > 1 && <button type="button" className="btn" onClick={back}>Back</button>}
+       <button type="button" className="btn btn-primary" onClick={onClose}>Close</button>
+     </>
+   );
+
+   return (
+     <Modal title="How This Works" onClose={onClose} wide footer={footer}>
+       <div className="help" ref={body}>
+         <nav className="breadcrumbs help-trail" aria-label="Help Trail">
+           {trail.map((p, i) => (
+             <span key={`${i}-${pageLabel(p)}`} className="row gap-2">
+               {i > 0 && <span aria-hidden="true">›</span>}
+               {i === trail.length - 1
+                 ? <span className="muted" aria-current="page">{pageLabel(p)}</span>
+                 : <button type="button" onClick={() => setTrail(trail.slice(0, i + 1))}>{pageLabel(p)}</button>}
+             </span>
+           ))}
+         </nav>
+         <form className="help-search" role="search" onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); submit(q); }}>
+           <label className="xs dim" htmlFor="help-q">Search How This Works</label>
+           <div className="row gap-2">
+             <input
+               id="help-q"
+               className="input grow"
+               type="search"
+               value={q}
+               placeholder="A feature, a word or a question"
+               data-autofocus={page.kind === 'search' ? true : undefined}
+               onChange={(e) => { setQ(e.target.value); if (page.kind === 'search') setTrail([...trail.slice(0, -1), { kind: 'search', q: e.target.value }]); }}
+             />
+             <button type="submit" className="btn btn-sm">Search</button>
+           </div>
+         </form>
+         {page.kind === 'contents' && <Contents onOpen={(id) => push({ kind: 'entry', id })} />}
+         {page.kind === 'search' && <Results q={page.q} onOpen={(id) => push({ kind: 'entry', id })} />}
+         {page.kind === 'entry' && GUIDE_BY_ID[page.id] && <Entry e={GUIDE_BY_ID[page.id]!} onOpen={(id) => push({ kind: 'entry', id })} onWhere={onWhere} />}
+       </div>
+     </Modal>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /** Whether every feature an entry covers is still shut on this life. */
+ const shutOn = (s: Parameters<typeof isOpen>[0], e: GuideEntry): boolean => e.covers.length > 0 && e.covers.every((f) => !isOpen(s, f));
+
+ /** An entry's place in a list: its title, and Locked while its chapter isn't read. */
+ function EntryLink({ e, onOpen, strong }: { e: GuideEntry; onOpen: (id: string) => void; strong?: boolean }) {
+   const shut = useWorld((s) => shutOn(s, e), [e]);
+   return (
+     <>
+       <button type="button" className={`help-link${strong ? ' strong' : ''}`} onClick={() => onOpen(e.id)}>{e.title}</button>
+       {shut && <span className="xs dim"> Locked</span>}
+     </>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * The entries for the screen the help was opened over, and its showing tab: an entry with a tab shows on that tab
+  * only, one without on any tab of its screen (from 2026-10-17). Until then ? opened the contents at Getting Started,
+  * whichever screen it was pressed on.
+  */
+ function onThisScreen(): { title: string; entries: GuideEntry[] } {
+   const route = screenInAddress();
+   const tab = kept<string>(tabKey(route)) ?? SECTIONS[route]?.[0]?.id;
+   const tabName = SECTIONS[route]?.find((x) => x.id === tab)?.label;
+   const entries = GOALS.flatMap((g) => entriesOf(g.id)).filter((e) => e.where.route === route && (!e.where.tab || e.where.tab === tab));
+   return { title: tabName ? `${screenName(route)}, ${tabName}` : screenName(route), entries };
+ }
+
+ /** Until 2026-10-17 the hint's example was “why is my rehearsal refused”, which found nothing. */
+ const HINT = `Type a feature’s name, a word for it or a question, such as ${SEARCH_EXAMPLES.map((x) => `“${x}”`).join(' or ')}.`;
+
+ function Contents({ onOpen }: { onOpen: (id: string) => void }) {
+   const guide = useGuide();
+   // A guide finished is counted as no guide, whatever chapters came after it (from 2026-10-13, as the top bar’s Guide
+   // button was that day): until then it read “15 of 17 read: each opens a part of the game.” on a guide finished
+   // before two chapters were added, though they open nothing there and the guide offers no way to mark them read.
+   const isGuided = useWorld((s) => guided(s) && !s.universe.tutorial?.finished);
+   const read = useWorld((s) => chaptersRead(s).filter((id) => CHAPTERS.some((c) => c.id === id)).length);
+   const onScreen = useMemo(onThisScreen, []);
+   const said = !isGuided
+     ? 'Everything is already open. You can read the chapters in any order.'
+     : read === 0
+       ? `You haven’t read any of its ${CHAPTERS.length} chapters yet. Each one you read opens a part of the game.`
+       : `You’ve read ${read} of its ${CHAPTERS.length} chapters. Each one you read opens a part of the game.`;
+   return (
+     <div className="col gap-4">
+       <div className="callout small">
+         <strong>The Guide.</strong>{' '}{said}{' '}
+         <button type="button" className="btn btn-sm" onClick={() => guide.show()}>Open The Guide</button>
+       </div>
+       {onScreen.entries.length > 0 && (
+         <section aria-labelledby="goal-here">
+           <h3 id="goal-here" style={{ margin: '0 0 var(--s1)' }}>On This Screen</h3>
+           <p className="xs dim" style={{ margin: '0 0 var(--s2)' }}>{onScreen.title}: what you can do here.</p>
+           <ul className="help-list">
+             {onScreen.entries.map((e) => <li key={e.id}><EntryLink e={e} onOpen={onOpen} /></li>)}
+           </ul>
+         </section>
+       )}
+       {GOALS.map((g) => {
+         const entries = entriesOf(g.id);
+         if (!entries.length) return null;
+         return (
+           <section key={g.id} aria-labelledby={`goal-${g.id}`}>
+             <h3 id={`goal-${g.id}`} style={{ margin: '0 0 var(--s1)' }}>{g.title}</h3>
+             <p className="xs dim" style={{ margin: '0 0 var(--s2)' }}>{g.lead}</p>
+             <ul className="help-list">
+               {entries.map((e) => <li key={e.id}><EntryLink e={e} onOpen={onOpen} /></li>)}
+             </ul>
+           </section>
+         );
+       })}
+     </div>
+   );
+ }
+
+ function Results({ q, onOpen }: { q: string; onOpen: (id: string) => void }) {
+   const found = useMemo(() => search(q), [q]);
+   if (!q.trim()) return <p className="small muted">{HINT}</p>;
+   if (!found.length) return <p className="small muted">Nothing matches “{q}”. Try fewer or different words, or go back to Contents.</p>;
+   return (
+     <ul className="help-results" aria-label={`${found.length} ${found.length === 1 ? 'Result' : 'Results'}`}>
+       {found.map((e) => (
+         <li key={e.id}>
+           <EntryLink e={e} onOpen={onOpen} strong />
+           <p className="xs dim" style={{ margin: 0 }}>{e.short.length > 180 ? `${e.short.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').slice(0, 177)}…` : e.short.replace(/\s+/g, ' ')}</p>
+         </li>
+       ))}
+     </ul>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /** Figures, each with its name; one the game had to estimate says so. */
+ function Facts({ facts }: { facts: readonly Fact[] }) {
+   return (
+     <dl className="help-facts small">
+       {facts.map((f) => (
+         <div key={f.label}><dt>{f.label}</dt><dd>{f.value}{f.estimate ? <span className="xs dim"> (estimated)</span> : null}</dd></div>
+       ))}
+     </dl>
+   );
+ }
+
+ function List({ items }: { items: readonly string[] }) {
+   return <ul className="small help-items">{items.map((x) => <li key={x}>{x}</li>)}</ul>;
+ }
+
+ /** A part of a section under its own small heading, drawn only when it has something in it. */
+ function Part({ title, show = true, children }: { title?: string; show?: boolean; children: ReactNode }) {
+   if (!show) return null;
+   return <div>{title && <div className="eyebrow" style={{ marginBottom: 'var(--s1)' }}>{title}</div>}{children}</div>;
+ }
+
+ function Entry({ e, onOpen, onWhere }: { e: GuideEntry; onOpen: (id: string) => void; onWhere: (e: GuideEntry) => void }) {
+   const guide = useGuide();
+   const [all, setAll] = useState(false);
+   // Locked for this life: the first of its features whose chapter isn't read. Until 2026-10-20 (brief 17, section 9)
+   // one shut feature said the whole entry wasn't open: How You Are's entry, whose panel opens with “How You Are” and
+   // whose own page with “A Whole Life”, told a player using the panel for eleven chapters “This isn’t open yet. Read “A
+   // Whole Life” in the guide to open it.”, while the contents marked it open (`shutOn`). Part open, it says so now.
+   const locked = useWorld((s) => e.covers.find((f) => !isOpen(s, f)), [e]);
+   const partly = useWorld((s) => e.covers.some((f) => isOpen(s, f)), [e]);
+   const chapter = locked ? chapterFor(locked) : undefined;
+   const leads = useMemo(() => connectionsTo(e.id), [e]);
+   // The brief's eight questions, in its order, then the deeper parts. The first two, what it's for and where to find it,
+   // are always showing; what to press opens with the entry; the rest open when pressed, or all with Show Everything.
+   const sections: { title: string; show: boolean; open?: boolean; body: ReactNode }[] = [
+     { title: 'What To Press', show: e.steps.length > 0, open: true, body: <ol className="small help-items">{e.steps.map((x) => <li key={x}>{x}</li>)}</ol> },
+     {
+       title: 'What You Need First', show: e.needs.length + e.costs.length > 0, body: (
+         <div className="col gap-3">
+           <Part show={e.needs.length > 0}><List items={e.needs} /></Part>
+           <Part title="Time And Money" show={e.costs.length > 0}><Facts facts={e.costs} /></Part>
+         </div>
+       ),
+     },
+     {
+       title: 'What Happens', show: e.now.length + e.later.length + e.interpret.length > 0, body: (
+         <div className="col gap-3">
+           <Part title="Straight Away" show={e.now.length > 0}><List items={e.now} /></Part>
+           <Part title="Later On" show={e.later.length > 0}><List items={e.later} /></Part>
+           <Part title="Reading The Result" show={e.interpret.length > 0}><List items={e.interpret} /></Part>
+         </div>
+       ),
+     },
+     {
+       title: 'How It Connects', show: e.connections.length + leads.length > 0, body: (
+         <div className="col gap-3">
+           {KIND_ORDER.map((k) => {
+             const cs = e.connections.filter((c) => c.kind === k);
+             if (!cs.length) return null;
+             return (
+               <Part key={k} title={CONNECTION_HEADING[k]}>
+                 <ul className="small help-items">
+                   {cs.map((c) => (
+                     <li key={c.to + c.why}>
+                       <button type="button" className="help-link" onClick={() => onOpen(c.to)}>{GUIDE_BY_ID[c.to]?.title ?? c.to}</button>: {c.why}
+                     </li>
+                   ))}
+                 </ul>
+               </Part>
+             );
+           })}
+           <Part title="What Leads Here" show={leads.length > 0}>
+             <ul className="small help-items">
+               {leads.map(({ from, connection }) => (
+                 <li key={from.id + connection.why}>
+                   <button type="button" className="help-link" onClick={() => onOpen(from.id)}>{from.title}</button>: {connection.why}
+                 </li>
+               ))}
+             </ul>
+           </Part>
+         </div>
+       ),
+     },
+     { title: 'What To Do Next', show: e.next.length > 0, body: <List items={e.next} /> },
+     {
+       title: 'If You Can’t', show: e.unavailable.length + e.mistakes.length > 0, body: (
+         <div className="col gap-3">
+           <Part show={e.unavailable.length > 0}><List items={e.unavailable} /></Part>
+           <Part title="Mistakes, And Putting Them Right" show={e.mistakes.length > 0}><List items={e.mistakes} /></Part>
+         </div>
+       ),
+     },
+     { title: 'What Decides It', show: e.reads.length > 0, body: <Facts facts={e.reads} /> },
+     {
+       title: 'A Worked Example', show: true, body: (
+         <div className="small">
+           <p style={{ margin: '0 0 var(--s2)' }}>{e.example.setup}</p>
+           <ol className="help-items">{e.example.steps.map((x) => <li key={x}>{x}</li>)}</ol>
+           <p style={{ margin: 'var(--s2) 0 0' }}><strong>What comes of it.</strong> {e.example.result}</p>
+         </div>
+       ),
+     },
+   ];
+   return (
+     <article className="help-entry" aria-labelledby={`entry-${e.id}`}>
+       <div className="row-between" style={{ alignItems: 'baseline' }}>
+         <h3 id={`entry-${e.id}`} style={{ margin: 0 }}>{e.title}</h3>
+         {/* The label says what a press does, and has no pressed state (from 2026-10-19, brief 15): until then it was
+             Show Everything and Fold It Up with `aria-pressed`, so a screen reader said “Fold It Up, pressed”, a toggle
+             whose name changed with its state (WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, Button pattern), as Play and Pause were until
+             2026-10-13 (`ui/shell/TimeControls.tsx`). */}
+         <button type="button" className="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" onClick={() => setAll((x) => !x)}>{all ? 'Show Less' : 'Show Everything'}</button>
+       </div>
+       {chapter && (
+         <div className="callout callout-warning small" style={{ margin: 'var(--s2) 0 var(--s3)' }}>
+           {partly ? `Part of this isn’t open yet. Read “${chapter.title}” in the guide to open the rest.` : `This isn’t open yet. Read “${chapter.title}” in the guide to open it.`}{' '}
+           <button type="button" className="btn btn-sm" onClick={() => guide.show(chapter.id)}>Read About It</button>
+         </div>
+       )}
+       {/* A summary in short paragraphs, a blank line between (from 2026-10-20, brief 16, section 7): what it means for you
+           now and what to do first, then what it costs or needs. Until then one paragraph, up to seven sentences. */}
+       {e.short.split(/\n\n+/).map((para, i) => <p key={i} className="help-short" style={{ marginTop: 'var(--s2)' }}>{para}</p>)}
+       <dl className="help-where xs">
+         <div><dt>Where To Find It</dt><dd>{e.where.label}.</dd></div>
+         <div><dt>When You Can Use It</dt><dd>{e.available}</dd></div>
+       </dl>
+       <div className="row gap-2" style={{ margin: 'var(--s2) 0 var(--s4)' }}>
+         <button type="button" className="btn btn-sm" onClick={() => onWhere(e)}>Show Me Where</button>
+       </div>
+       {sections.filter((s) => s.show).map((s) => (
+         <details key={`${s.title}-${all}`} className="help-section" open={all || s.open || undefined}>
+           <summary>{s.title}</summary>
+           <div className="help-section-body">{s.body}</div>
+         </details>
+       ))}
+       {e.related.length > 0 && (
+         <div className="help-related">
+           <div className="eyebrow">Read With It</div>
+           <ul className="help-list">
+             {e.related.filter((r) => GUIDE_BY_ID[r]).map((r) => <li key={r}><EntryLink e={GUIDE_BY_ID[r]!} onOpen={onOpen} /></li>)}
+           </ul>
+         </div>
+       )}
+     </article>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — How This Works, beside a feature (from 2026-10-12): opens the guide's reference at the feature's entry,
+  * over the screen, so nothing under it is lost. It runs no command and moves no clock.
+  *
+  * Its prop is `help`, never `feature`: `tests/tutorial.test.ts` counts a literal feature prop as a gated control, and a help
+  * link mustn't stand in for one.
+  */
+
+ import { entryFor } from '@/engine/content/guide';
+ import { useHelp } from './help-context';
+
+ export function HowItWorks({ help, label = 'How This Works' }: { help: string; label?: string }) {
+   const { open } = useHelp();
+   const entry = entryFor(help);
+   if (!entry) return null;
+   return (
+     <button
+       type="button"
+       className="btn btn-ghost btn-sm how-it-works"
+       aria-label={`${label}: ${entry.title}`}
+       aria-haspopup="dialog"
+       onClick={() => open(entry.id)}
+     >
+       {label}
+     </button>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — the way into the guide's reference, for anything on screen (from 2026-10-12; `ui/guide/Help.tsx`).
+  *
+  * Kept apart from the dialog so a panel can offer How This Works without importing the dialog, which imports the
+  * panel's own primitives.
+  */
+
+ import { createContext, useContext } from 'react';
+
+ export interface HelpApi {
+   /** Opens the reference at an entry, by its id or a feature it covers, or at the contents. */
+   open: (id?: string) => void;
+   /** Opens the reference's search, with words already in it if given. */
+   find: (words?: string) => void;
+ }
+
+ export const HelpContext = createContext<HelpApi>({ open: () => {}, find: () => {} });
+
+ export const useHelp = (): HelpApi => useContext(HelpContext);
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — looking at a thing, in the place where it is named.
+  *
+  * `<Open>` is the noun. It renders the world’s own word for a thing as a
+  * pressable word — `button.link`, which the stylesheet has defined since it
+  * was written, and commented "a name that is also a way in", and never once
+  * used. Pressing it opens the thing.
+  *
+  * The trigger is inline and the body is a block, so the two cannot be the same
+  * element: a paragraph cannot hold a card inside a sentence. `<LookRegion>` is
+  * the block that hosts them. Every `<Open>` opens into the nearest region
+  * above it, so a noun in the middle of a sentence expands beneath the
+  * paragraph that sentence is in rather than tearing it in half.
+  *
+  * A look body opens its own region, so a noun inside a look expands inside
+  * that look. That is the whole of how depth works here — no stack, no router,
+  * no modal over a modal. Closing a level unmounts everything under it, which
+  * is what makes getting out of four levels one press rather than four.
+  */
+
+ import { createContext, useContext, useMemo, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
+ import { useWorld } from '@/app/game-context';
+ import { isOpen as guideAllows } from '@/engine/world/tutorial';
+ import { resolveLook, lookExists, type Facet, type Looked, type Way } from './registry';
+ import { sameSubject, subjectKey, type Subject } from './subject';
+
+ interface RegionValue {
+   open: Subject | null;
+   setOpen: (subject: Subject | null) => void;
+   /** Names of every look this region sits inside, outermost first. */
+   ancestry: readonly string[];
+   depth: number;
+ }
+
+ const RegionContext = createContext<RegionValue | null>(null);
+
+ /**
+  * A block that things can open into.
+  *
+  * Put one around any group of prose or stats whose nouns should be openable.
+  * A screen needs no other machinery: no state, no handler, no modal.
+  */
+ export function LookRegion({
+   children, ancestry = [], className,
+ }: {
+   children: ReactNode;
+   ancestry?: readonly string[];
+   className?: string;
+ }) {
+   const [open, setOpen] = useState<Subject | null>(null);
+   const outer = useContext(RegionContext);
+   const value = useMemo<RegionValue>(() => ({
+     open,
+     setOpen,
+     ancestry: ancestry.length ? ancestry : (outer?.ancestry ?? []),
+     depth: (outer?.depth ?? -1) + 1,
+   }), [open, ancestry, outer]);
+
+   return (
+     <RegionContext.Provider value={value}>
+       <div className={className}>
+         {children}
+         {open && <LookPanel subject={open} onClose={() => setOpen(null)} />}
+       </div>
+     </RegionContext.Provider>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * The world’s word for a thing, as the way into it.
+  *
+  * Renders plain text — not a dead control — when the thing is not there to be
+  * looked at, or when nothing has declared what its kind opens into. A name is
+  * never painted as a way in unless it is one.
+  */
+ export function Open({
+   subject, children, plain,
+ }: {
+   subject: Subject;
+   children: ReactNode;
+   /** Render as text even if it would open. For places a control would be wrong. */
+   plain?: boolean;
