+ }) {
+   const region = useContext(RegionContext);
+   const exists = useWorld((sim) => lookExists(sim, subject), [subject.kind, subject.id]);
+   // Plain text until the chapter in the guide for it is read (`world/tutorial.ts`).
+   const guideOpen = useWorld((sim) => guideAllows(sim, `look.${subject.kind}`), [subject.kind]);
+
+   if (plain || !region || !exists || !guideOpen) return <>{children}</>;
+
+   const isOpen = sameSubject(region.open, subject);
+   return (
+     <button
+       type="button"
+       className={`link${isOpen ? ' is-open' : ''}`}
+       aria-expanded={isOpen}
+       onClick={() => region.setOpen(isOpen ? null : subject)}
+     >
+       {children}
+     </button>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /** What a resolved look renders as. */
+ function LookPanel({ subject, onClose }: { subject: Subject; onClose: () => void }) {
+   const region = useContext(RegionContext);
+   const found = useWorld((s) => resolveLook(s, subject), [subject.kind, subject.id]);
+
+   if (!found) return null;
+
+   if ('gone' in found) {
+     return (
+       <div className="look look-gone">
+         <p className="small muted" style={{ margin: 0 }}>{found.gone}</p>
+         <button type="button" className="link look-close" onClick={onClose}>Close</button>
+       </div>
+     );
+   }
+
+   const ancestry = [...(region?.ancestry ?? []), found.name];
+   return (
+     <div className="look" data-depth={region?.depth ?? 0}>
+       <LookHeader look={found} ancestry={ancestry} onClose={onClose} />
+       <LookRegion ancestry={ancestry} className="look-inner">
+         <p className="look-summary">{found.summary}</p>
+         {found.body}
+         {found.facets && found.facets.length > 0 && <Facets facets={found.facets} />}
+         {found.ways && found.ways.length > 0 && <Ways ways={found.ways} as={found.waysAs} />}
+         {found.provenance && <p className="look-provenance">{found.provenance}</p>}
+       </LookRegion>
+     </div>
+   );
+ }
+
+ function LookHeader({
+   look, ancestry, onClose,
+ }: {
+   look: Looked;
+   ancestry: readonly string[];
+   onClose: () => void;
+ }) {
+   return (
+     <div className="look-head">
+       <div style={{ minWidth: 0 }}>
+         {ancestry.length > 1 && (
+           <div className="look-trail">{ancestry.slice(0, -1).join(' · ')}</div>
+         )}
+         <div className="eyebrow">{look.kind}</div>
+         <h3 className="look-name">{look.name}</h3>
+       </div>
+       <button type="button" className="link look-close" onClick={onClose} aria-label={`Close ${look.name}`}>
+         Close
+       </button>
+     </div>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /** Another face of the same thing. Costs no depth and has no address. */
+ function Facets({ facets }: { facets: readonly Facet[] }) {
+   const [current, setCurrent] = useState(facets[0]?.id ?? '');
+   const shown = facets.find((f) => f.id === current) ?? facets[0];
+   if (!shown) return null;
+   return (
+     <div className="look-facets">
+       <div className="tabs" role="tablist">
+         {facets.map((f) => (
+           <button
+             key={f.id}
+             type="button"
+             role="tab"
+             className="tab"
+             aria-selected={f.id === shown.id}
+             onClick={() => setCurrent(f.id)}
+           >
+             {f.label}
+           </button>
+         ))}
+       </div>
+       <div className="look-facet-body">
+         {shown.body}
+         {shown.ways && shown.ways.length > 0 && <Ways ways={shown.ways} />}
+       </div>
+     </div>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * The ways further in.
+  *
+  * Each says what is behind it before you take it, so the shape of the graph
+  * can be read without walking it. A way onto nothing is not painted — the
+  * thing it points at may have left the world since the view was written.
+  */
+ function Ways({ ways, as = 'list' }: { ways: readonly Way[]; as?: 'list' | 'strip' }) {
+   const live = useWorld((s) => ways.filter((w) => lookExists(s, w.to)), [ways]);
+   if (live.length === 0) return null;
+
+   // A strip: the same edges, drawn across instead of down. The whole cell is
+   // the control, so its accessible name reads "Wednesday, Overcast, 3° / -1°"
+   // — the detail line, said rather than printed twice.
+   if (as === 'strip') {
+     return (
+       <div className="look-strip">
+         {live.map((way) => (
+           <div key={subjectKey(way.to)} className={`look-cell${way.glance?.marked ? ' is-here' : ''}`}>
+             <Open subject={way.to}>
+               <span className="look-cell-name">{way.label}</span>
+               {way.glance?.marked && <span className="sr-only">, where you are</span>}
+               {way.glance?.icon && <span aria-hidden="true" className="look-cell-icon">{way.glance.icon}</span>}
+               {(way.glance?.lines ?? []).map((line) => (
+                 <span key={line} className="look-cell-line">{line}</span>
+               ))}
+             </Open>
+           </div>
+         ))}
+       </div>
+     );
+   }
+
+   return (
+     <div className="look-ways">
+       {live.map((way) => (
+         <div key={subjectKey(way.to)} className="look-way">
+           <Open subject={way.to}>{way.label}</Open>
+           <span className="look-way-detail">{way.detail}</span>
+         </div>
+       ))}
+     </div>
+   );
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — the actor as the Player Profile opens it (from the connected
+  * attributes of 2026-10-09): an ability, a genre, and a piece of finished
+  * work. An interest was one too, until the interests went on 2026-10-10.
+  *
+  * Every figure is read from where the engine keeps it: an ability from its
+  * one place (`abilityOf`), its changes from the development history, what it
+  * does from the task profiles that read it (`content/tasks.ts`), a piece of
+  * work from the evaluation it was judged by, its limits as that evaluation
+  * worked them out. Nothing here is computed for the screen alone.
+  */
+
+ import type { Simulation } from '@/engine';
+ import type { Person } from '@/engine/domain/model';
+ import { formatDate } from '@/engine/core/time';
+ import { ABILITY_DEFS, ABILITY_KIN, DEVELOPMENT, MASTERED, TECHNIQUE_LABEL, type AbilityId } from '@/engine/content/abilities';
+ import { DIMENSION_LABEL, DIMENSION_MEANS, TASK_PROFILES, type Dimension } from '@/engine/content/tasks';
+ import { EXERCISES, exerciseFor } from '@/engine/content/practice';
+ import { GENRE_DEFS } from '@/engine/content/genres';
+ import { CONCERNS } from '@/engine/content/concerns';
+ import { concernDraws, concernsOf, concernWords, registerBasisWords } from '@/engine/systems/register';
+ import { FILM_GENRES, GENRE_BY_ID } from '@/engine/content/film-genres';
+ import { abilityDef, abilityFull, abilityOf, developmentOf, isAbility, targetId } from '@/engine/systems/attributes';
+ import { classesGrow, reachOf } from '@/engine/systems/school';
+ import { EVERYDAY_FITNESS, FITNESS } from '@/engine/systems/life';
+ import { genreSpeed, playOfGenre } from '@/engine/systems/engagement';
+ import { chiefLimit, replay, type WorkRecord } from '@/engine/systems/evaluation';
+ import { workloadWords } from '@/engine/systems/workload';
+ import { DEMAND_LABEL, DEMAND_TECHNIQUE, GENRE_DEMANDS, applied } from '@/engine/content/demands';
+ import { COURSES, type Skill } from '@/engine/content/school';
+ import { Stat } from '@/ui/components/primitives';
+ import { Segments } from '@/ui/components/WorkThrough';
+ import { briefKinds } from '@/engine/content/briefs';
+ import { TEMPLATES } from '@/engine/content/coursework';
+ import { abilityReaders } from '@/engine/systems/material';
+ import { defineLook, type Way } from './registry';
+ import { at } from './subject';
+
+ const one = (x: number) => x.toFixed(1);
+ const player = (sim: Simulation): Person | undefined => sim.universe.people[sim.universe.playerId];
+ const zoneOf = (sim: Simulation) => sim.zone;
+
+ /** What a target is called: an ability’s label, or a technique’s. */
+ export const targetLabel = (t: AbilityId | Skill): string => (isAbility(targetId(t)) ? abilityDef(targetId(t) as AbilityId).label : TECHNIQUE_LABEL[t as Skill]);
+ /** Where a target opens: an ability’s look, or a technique’s (the school’s skill). */
+ export const targetSubject = (t: AbilityId | Skill) => (isAbility(targetId(t)) ? at('ability', targetId(t)) : at('skill', t));
+
+ /** The tasks and dimensions that read an ability (`abilityReaders`, systems/material.ts): its look’s and the Profile’s. */
+ export const readersOf = (id: AbilityId): { task: string; label: string; dims: Dimension[] }[] => abilityReaders(id);
+
+ /** The latest changes to an id on the development history, newest first. */
+ export function recentOf(person: Person, id: string, n = 6) {
+   return developmentOf(person).history.filter((h) => h.id === id).slice(-n).reverse();
+ }
+
+ /** A kept band, in words: coursework’s and a brief’s (LAMDA’s), and a night’s (from 2026-10-12: until then shown as stored, in lowercase, two vocabularies in one column). */
+ export const BAND_WORD: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = { unready: 'Unready', working: 'Working', strong: 'Strong', exceptional: 'Exceptional', off: 'An Off Night', solid: 'Solid', remarkable: 'Remarkable' };
+
+ /** What a development source is, in words. */
+ export function sourceWords(source: string): string {
+   const [kind, rest] = source.split(':') as [string, string | undefined];
+   if (kind === 'practice') return EXERCISES.find((e) => e.id === rest)?.label ?? 'Practice';
+   // A class by its name and a coursework step by its part’s words (from 2026-10-17, brief 14): until then the course’s
+   // code alone and the part’s key, "Class: DRAM 153a", "Coursework: interpretation".
+   if (kind === 'class') { const c = COURSES.find((x) => x.code === rest); return c ? `Class: ${c.name} (${c.code})` : `Class: ${rest}`; }
+   // A step with no part of its own said as what it is (from 2026-10-17, brief 14's editorial review): until then the
+   // reader’s evenings showed as their key, "Coursework: reader".
+   if (kind === 'prepare') return `Coursework: ${(TASK_PROFILES.scene?.prepLabel?.[rest ?? ''] ?? ({ reader: 'running it with a reader', approach: 'rehearsing how you play it', genre: 'knowing the genre' } as Record<string, string>)[rest ?? ''] ?? rest ?? 'preparation').toLowerCase()}`;
+   if (kind === 'interest') return 'An interest, from before they were removed';
+   if (kind === 'workout') return rest === 'run' ? 'A run' : 'A workout';
+   if (kind === 'read' || kind === 'research') return 'Reading a play';
+   // A skill grown into another, a brief’s preparation, the nerves of a performance, and working a problem through had no
+   // words until 2026-10-12, and showed as their raw keys.
+   if (kind === 'transfer') return 'Carried over from a related skill';
+   if (kind === 'brief') return `A practice brief: ${rest === 'interpretation' ? 'the breakdown' : rest === 'memorization' ? 'the lines' : rest ?? 'its preparation'}`;
+   if (kind === 'workbook') return 'Working a problem through';
+   if (kind === 'nerves') return 'Nerves before a performance';
+   // A production’s rehearsal call, a lab and its showing, and a coursework activity had none until 2026-10-13, and showed
+   // as "rehearsal", "lab" and "coursework" (found by the review of that day).
+   // The Yale Cabaret’s said by its name since later that day; it showed as its key, “cabaret”, found by its evidence pass.
+   if (kind === 'rehearsal') return rest === 'summer' ? 'A rehearsal call: the Summer Cabaret' : rest === 'cabaret' ? 'A rehearsal call: the Yale Cabaret' : rest ? `A rehearsal call: ${rest}` : 'A rehearsal call';
+   if (kind === 'lab') return rest === 'showing' ? 'A lab’s showing' : 'A lab';
+   if (kind === 'coursework') return `Coursework: ${TEMPLATES.flatMap((t) => t.activities).find((a) => a.id === rest)?.label ?? 'an activity'}`;
+   return ({ 'practice-day': 'A day of practice kept', call: 'A call answered', night: 'A night on stage', 'partner-rehearsal': 'Rehearsing with a partner', 'learn-part': 'Learning the part', blocking: 'The blocking book', 'work-note': 'A director’s note worked', 'self-tape': 'A self-tape' } as Record<string, string>)[kind] ?? kind;
+ }
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // An ability
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ interface TheAbility { id: AbilityId; person: Person }
+
+ defineLook<TheAbility>('ability', {
+   gone: 'That isn’t one of an actor’s abilities.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => {
+     const p = player(sim);
+     return p && ABILITY_DEFS.some((d) => d.id === id) ? { id: id as AbilityId, person: p } : undefined;
+   },
+   seeds: () => ABILITY_DEFS.map((d) => d.id),
+   look: ({ id, person }, { sim }) => {
+     const def = abilityDef(id);
+     if (!person.craft) {
+       // A life that never trained: what the ability is, and nothing measured.
+       return {
+         name: def.label,
+         kind: def.general ? 'A General Ability' : 'An Acting Ability',
+         summary: `You haven’t trained as an actor, so it’s never been measured. ${def.definition}`,
+         body: <p className="small"><strong>How it grows.</strong> {def.develops}</p>,
+         provenance: def.source,
+       };
+     }
+     const level = abilityOf(sim, person, id);
+     const full = abilityFull(sim, person, id);
+     const reach = Math.min(full, reachOf(person, id));
+     const readers = readersOf(id);
+     const exercise = exerciseFor(id);
+     const recent = recentOf(person, id);
+     const kin = ABILITY_KIN[id] ?? [];
+     const ways: Way[] = [
+       ...kin.map((k) => ({ to: at('skill', k), label: TECHNIQUE_LABEL[k], detail: 'A related technique: the classes that grow one grow both' })),
+       ...(person.work ?? []).filter((w) => w.inputs.abilities[id] !== undefined).slice(-3).reverse().map((w) => ({ to: at('work', w.inputs.key), label: w.what, detail: `${w.taskLabel}, ${one(w.overall)} of 100, with yours at ${one(w.inputs.abilities[id]!)}` })),
+     ];
+     return {
+       name: def.label,
+       kind: def.general ? 'A General Ability' : 'An Acting Ability',
+       summary: `You’re at ${one(level)} of ${one(full)}${level >= full ? ', full' : ''}: ${def.definition.charAt(0).toLowerCase()}${def.definition.slice(1)}`,
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <div className="grid grid-3">
+             <Stat label="Now" value={one(level)} note={level >= full ? 'Full: no work asks more of it' : `${one(full - level)} to full`} />
+             <Stat label="Classes Reach" value={classesGrow(id) ? one(reach) : '—'} note={classesGrow(id) ? 'Classes and coursework level off here; practice takes you past it' : id === 'stamina' ? 'No limit from classes: workouts build it, and so do classes that work the body as hard' : id === 'discipline' ? 'Classes don’t build it; practice kept up does' : 'Classes don’t build it; performing in front of people does'} />
+             <Stat label="Last Change" value={recent[0] ? `+${recent[0].delta.toFixed(2)}` : 'None Yet'} note={recent[0] ? `${sourceWords(recent[0].source)}, ${formatDate(recent[0].at, zoneOf(sim))}` : `None in your last ${DEVELOPMENT.historyKept} changes`} />
+           </div>
+           <p className="small"><strong>How it grows.</strong> {def.develops}</p>
+           <p className="small"><strong>Where it started.</strong> {def.derivedFrom}</p>
+           {/* What it does, in its own sentence, and which work reads it (from 2026-10-17, brief 11, A4): until then What It Does
+               was the readers alone, and the ability’s own sentence, corrected against the code in the attributes brief’s
+               phase 2, was shown nowhere: every ability has a reader, so the line that fell back to it never did. */}
+           <p className="small"><strong>What it does.</strong> {def.affects}</p>
+           <p className="small"><strong>Where it counts.</strong> {readers.map((r) => `${r.label}: ${r.dims.map((d) => DIMENSION_LABEL[d].toLowerCase()).join(', ')}`).join('; ')}.</p>
+           {exercise && <p className="small"><strong>To practice it.</strong> {exercise.label}: {exercise.how} {exercise.kind === 'slate' ? '(An exercise made for the game.)' : exercise.kind === 'named' ? '(A named exercise from real acting teaching.)' : '(Put together from real practice.)'}</p>}
+           {id === 'stamina' && <p className="small"><strong>Its scale.</strong> Stamina is your fitness. Full is the fittest a body your age can be ({one(full)} now). A workout builds it and holds it for {FITNESS.heldDays} days, and so does a class that works the body as hard (Movement Invention, stage combat). After that it falls {FITNESS.perDay} a day toward {EVERYDAY_FITNESS}, as an untrained body’s does. A second workout on the same day builds half as much.</p>}
+           {recent.length > 0 && (
+             <ul className="small">
+               {recent.map((h, i) => <li key={i}>{formatDate(h.at, zoneOf(sim))}: +{h.delta.toFixed(3)}, {sourceWords(h.source)}</li>)}
+             </ul>
+           )}
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways,
+       provenance: def.source,
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // A genre
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ interface TheGenre { id: string; person: Person }
+
+ defineLook<TheGenre>('genre', {
+   gone: 'That isn’t one of the genres.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => {
+     const p = player(sim);
+     return p && GENRE_DEFS[id] && GENRE_BY_ID[id] ? { id, person: p } : undefined;
+   },
+   seeds: () => FILM_GENRES.map((g) => g.id),
+   look: ({ id, person }, { sim }) => {
+     const def = GENRE_DEFS[id]!;
+     const g = person.engagement?.byGenre[id];
+     const loved = (person.genres ?? []).includes(id);
+     const speed = genreSpeed(person, [id]);
+     const play = playOfGenre(id);
+     // Its briefs' takes (from 2026-10-12: until then this looked for keys a self-tape stopped writing when briefs came, and listed nothing).
+     // A take of a brief retired on 2026-10-16 is still the genre’s (`briefKinds`): until then only a brief offered now was looked up.
+     const tapes = (person.work ?? []).filter((w) => w.inputs.key.startsWith(`brief:${person.id}:`) && briefKinds(w.inputs.key.split(':')[2] ?? '').includes(id)).slice(-3).reverse();
+     const demand = GENRE_DEMANDS[id];
+     return {
+       name: GENRE_BY_ID[id]!.label,
+       kind: loved ? 'A Genre You Love' : 'A Genre',
+       summary: g ? `Familiarity ${one(g.familiarity)}, work in it ${one(g.practice)}. The better of the two is how well you know the genre: it makes a scene or a part from a play of its kind ${Math.round((speed - 1) * 100)}% quicker to prepare, and it counts as Knowing The Genre when you prepare a brief in it.` : 'You haven’t studied it or worked in it yet. Study it, or tape its brief, to get to know it.',
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <div className="grid grid-3">
+             <Stat label="Familiarity" value={one(g?.familiarity ?? 0)} note="Films watched and plays read" />
+             <Stat label="Work In It" value={one(g?.practice ?? 0)} note="Nights on stage and self-tapes in it" />
+             {/* What it speeds, said (from 2026-10-12: until then "The best of the two, never a cap on the work", beside a
+                 summary saying a brief in it reads knowing it, so it read as speeding the brief; a brief’s steps read the
+                 material met before, `prepSpeed`, and never this). */}
+             <Stat label="Preparation" value={`${Math.round((speed - 1) * 100)}% Faster`} note="For a scene or a part from a play of its kind, by the better of the two. A brief’s steps speed up with material you’ve met before instead." />
+           </div>
+           <p className="small"><strong>Its conventions.</strong> {def.conventions}</p>
+           {demand && (
+             <>
+               <p className="small"><strong>What it asks of an actor.</strong> {demand.claim}</p>
+               <p className="small"><strong>{applied(id) && demand.tags.length ? 'What a self-tape in it asks.' : 'Why it adds no requirement.'}</strong>{' '}
+                 {/* A self-tape’s, which every brief in the genre stages (tests/briefs-content.test.ts); the research’s reasons for
+                     each go in the small print below (from 2026-10-17, brief 14). Until 2026-10-13 this
+                     said “Work in it reads”, and a night of a play of the kind or a class scene from one reads its own
+                     material’s techniques instead (`playReads`, `workContext`): a farce’s night read no clown. */}
+                 {applied(id) && demand.tags.length
+                   ? <>A self-tape in it calls for {demand.tags.map((t, i) => <span key={t.tag}>{i ? ', ' : ''}{TECHNIQUE_LABEL[DEMAND_TECHNIQUE[t.tag]]} (yours: {one(person.craft?.[DEMAND_TECHNIQUE[t.tag]] ?? 0)} of {MASTERED})</span>)}.{demand.basis === 'definition' ? ' This follows from how the genre is defined, not from a source that says so.' : ''} A night of a play of its kind, or a class scene from one, calls for its own material’s techniques instead.</>
+                   : demand.belongsTo ? `What the research found (${demand.tags.map((t) => DEMAND_LABEL[t.tag]).join(', ') || 'no technique'}) belongs to ${demand.belongsTo}, not to the genre as a whole, so the genre adds no requirement of its own.`
+                   : demand.tags.length ? `The research holds this (${demand.tags.map((t) => DEMAND_LABEL[t.tag]).join(', ')}) with low confidence, so the game doesn’t treat it as a requirement of the genre. The small print below says why.` : 'The research found nothing it asks beyond what any self-tape asks.'}
+               </p>
+               {/* The small print in three paragraphs, each under the words it opens with (from 2026-10-17, brief 14's json
+                   area, D1 to D3): until then one paragraph, about 2,000 characters for adventure, some forty lines at 390
+                   wide; its first heading said "in the research’s words" over the game’s wording of the research; and the
+                   sentence above said "only in single examples" of ten genres whose research is low for other reasons,
+                   which this small print gives. Every genre it reaches is low, by `applied`. */}
+               {applied(id) && demand.tags.length ? <p className="xs dim">Why it’s applied: {demand.tags.map((t) => t.why).join(' ')}</p> : null}
+               <p className="xs dim">What the research says: {demand.sourceSupports} ({demand.how}; {demand.confidence} confidence).</p>
+               <p className="xs dim">Still uncertain: {demand.uncertainty}</p>
+             </>
+           )}
+           {/* Its register (from 2026-10-16, `GENRE_REGISTER`): what every take of a brief written for it reads. */}
+           {concernsOf(id).length > 0 && (
+             <>
+               <p className="small"><strong>How its scenes are played.</strong> {registerBasisWords(id)}</p>
+               <ul className="small">{concernsOf(id).map((c) => <li key={c}>{concernWords(c)}</li>)}</ul>
+             </>
+           )}
+           <p className="small"><strong>To study it.</strong> Press Study It beside it under Genres on your Player Profile. {play ? `You’ll read ${play.title}${play.by ? `, by ${play.by}` : ''}, a play of its kind.` : 'You’ll watch a film of its kind.'} To tape its brief, press Open Its Brief beside it instead: the tape is judged beat by beat like any taped brief, on what its own material asks.</p>
+           <p className="xs dim">Source for its definition: {def.source}.{demand ? ` Source for what it asks: ${demand.source}.` : ''}</p>
+           <p className="small">{loved ? 'You love it, so a day of work in it is a better day. Loving it doesn’t make the work faster or limit it.' : 'Loving a genre makes a day of work in it better. It doesn’t make you better at it.'}</p>
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways: [
+         ...(applied(id) ? (demand?.tags ?? []).map((t) => ({ to: at('skill', DEMAND_TECHNIQUE[t.tag]), label: TECHNIQUE_LABEL[DEMAND_TECHNIQUE[t.tag]], detail: `What it asks for: ${DEMAND_LABEL[t.tag]}` })) : []),
+         ...[...new Set(concernsOf(id).flatMap(concernDraws))].map((a) => ({ to: at('ability', a), label: ABILITY_DEFS.find((d) => d.id === a)?.label ?? a, detail: `Its scenes call on it: ${concernsOf(id).filter((c) => concernDraws(c).includes(a)).map((c) => CONCERNS[c].label).join(', ')}` })),
+         ...tapes.map((w) => ({ to: at('work', w.inputs.key), label: w.what, detail: `${one(w.overall)}, ${formatDate(w.at, zoneOf(sim))}` })),
+       ],
+       provenance: `Its definition was ${def.how === 'read directly' ? 'read at the source' : 'taken from a search summary'}, and what it asks is held with ${demand?.confidence ?? 'low'} confidence.`,
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // A piece of finished work
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ interface TheWorkDone { w: WorkRecord; person: Person }
+
+ defineLook<TheWorkDone>('work', {
+   gone: 'That piece isn’t on your record anymore. The record keeps your latest 160 pieces.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => {
+     const p = player(sim);
+     const w = p?.work?.find((x) => x.inputs.key === id);
+     return w && p ? { w, person: p } : undefined;
+   },
+   seeds: (sim) => (player(sim)?.work ?? []).map((w) => w.inputs.key),
+   look: ({ w }, { sim }) => {
+     const dims = Object.entries(w.dims) as [Dimension, number][];
+     const chief = chiefLimit(w);
+     const abilities = Object.keys(w.inputs.abilities) as AbilityId[];
+     const profile = TASK_PROFILES[w.task];
+     const again = profile ? replay(w, profile) : undefined;
+     // Each part of preparation by the task’s own words, the way of playing it as the limits name it, and each family by
+     // its genre’s (from 2026-10-12: until then by their keys, "interpretation 66% of 80%, … approach 49% of 90%;
+     // leaning to science_fiction").
+     const partWords = (k: string) => (profile?.prepLabel?.[k] ?? (k === 'approach' ? 'How you play it' : k.replace(/_/g, ' '))).toLowerCase();
+     const familyWords = (f: string) => (GENRE_BY_ID[f]?.label ?? f.replace(/_/g, ' ')).toLowerCase();
+     const prepared = Object.entries(w.inputs.prep).map(([k, v]) => `${partWords(k)} at ${Math.round(v * 100)}% (complete at ${Math.round((w.inputs.required[k] ?? 1) * 100)}%)`);
+     return {
+       name: w.what,
+       kind: w.taskLabel,
+       summary: `Judged ${one(w.overall)} of 100${w.band ? `, ${BAND_WORD[w.band] ?? w.band}` : ''}, on ${formatDate(w.at, zoneOf(sim))}.${chief ? ` ${chief}.` : w.mastery ? ' You met everything it asked, so it couldn’t have scored higher.' : ''}`,
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <div className="grid grid-3">
+             {dims.map(([d, q]) => <Stat key={d} label={DIMENSION_LABEL[d]} value={one(q)} note={DIMENSION_MEANS[d]} />)}
+           </div>
+           {w.limits.length > 0 && (
+             <ul className="small">
+               {w.limits.map((l, i) => <li key={i}>{l.label}: {l.by} points off {DIMENSION_LABEL[l.dimension].toLowerCase()}{l.whole !== undefined ? `, ${l.whole} off the whole` : ''}</li>)}
+             </ul>
+           )}
+           {again?.piece && <Segments e={again} caption="Moment By Moment" />}
+           {/* A night’s workload, from its own record (from 2026-10-16, brief 10, `workloadWords`): what it asked of stamina
+               and what it cost. A night kept under evaluation-10 kept none, and shows none. */}
+           {workloadWords(w) && <p className="small" data-workload="">{workloadWords(w)} <span className="xs dim">Source for the running time: {w.inputs.piece!.night!.from}.</span></p>}
+           <p className="xs dim">Judged with readiness at {Math.round(w.inputs.condition.readiness)}{w.inputs.condition.ill ? ', with the flu' : ''}{w.inputs.condition.injured ? ', with an injury' : ''}{w.inputs.condition.concussed ? ', with a concussion mending' : ''}; difficulty {w.inputs.difficulty.toFixed(2)}; {prepared.length ? `preparation: ${prepared.join(', ')}` : 'preparation not counted'}{w.inputs.families.length ? `; its genres: ${w.inputs.families.map(familyWords).join(', ')}` : ''}.</p>
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways: abilities.map((a) => ({ to: at('ability', a), label: abilityDef(a).label, detail: `Yours was ${one(w.inputs.abilities[a]!)}` })),
+       provenance: again ? `Judged again from its record, it comes to ${one(again.overall)}.` : w.inputs.levels ? 'The rules have changed since it was judged, so it can’t be judged again. Its result stands.' : 'It was judged before the game kept a result’s details, so it can’t be judged again.',
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ /** For a list: a mastered technique against MASTERED. */
+ export const masteredOf = (level: number) => level >= MASTERED;
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — every kind the game knows how to open.
+  *
+  * Nothing but side-effect imports. Adding a kind is adding a file and a line
+  * here; the crawl in tests/looks.test.ts picks it up without being told, and
+  * so does every tool that enumerates the registry.
+  *
+  * Kept apart from index.ts so that a test can register the whole graph
+  * without pulling in the React layer that renders it. Depth is data first and
+  * markup second, and this is the seam.
+  */
+
+ import './wellbeing';
+ import './place';
+ import './weather';
+ import './money';
+ import './day';
+ import './attention';
+ import './plans';
+ import './bank';
+ import './papers';
+ import './school';
+ import './actor';
+ import './classmate';
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — the things asking for you.
+  *
+  * Home’s "What Needs You" panel is the one place the game admits something is
+  * waiting on the player, and it says the least it possibly could about it. A
+  * decision carries an urgency between nought and a hundred that decides the
+  * whole order of the list, and the panel spends that figure on a colored
+  * stripe marked `aria-hidden` — so the number reaches nobody at all, not the
+  * player who sees a bar and not the screen reader that is told to skip it.
+  * The notifications underneath are rendered `list-static`, deliberately inert:
+  * a wall of sentences about things that happened, with no way back to any of
+  * them.
+  *
+  * Both kinds here do the same job. Say the figure the bar hides, say what
+  * raised it, say when it stops asking, and offer the thing it is about, which
+  * is a pointer five record shapes declare. Nothing in the engine fills it in
+  * any more — everything that did went with the film side — so the pointer is
+  * whatever an older save carries or a caller supplies, and `subjectForRef`
+  * resolves it only when a look has been declared for its kind.
+  *
+  * A decision’s actions are commands. They stay on Home, where pressing one
+  * runs it through `game.run()`. This explains a decision; it never takes one,
+  * and nothing below writes anything at all.
+  */
+
+ import { titleCaseLabel } from '@/engine/core/text';
+ import { formatDate, formatRelative, formatRelativeWords, MS_DAY } from '@/engine/core/time';
+ import { openDecisions, unreadNotifications } from '@/engine/world/world';
+ import type { DecisionItem, Notification as Notice } from '@/engine/domain/model';
+ import type { Simulation } from '@/engine';
+ import { Stat } from '@/ui/components/primitives';
+ import { defineLook, lookExists, resolveLook, type Way } from './registry';
+ import { at, subjectForRef, type Subject } from './subject';
+ import { outOf, spokenList } from './words';
+
+ // Untouched for ninety days, an undated row went quiet (`QUIET_AFTER_DAYS`), and the look said so, until 2026-10-14,
+ // when the owner had the rule go: no raiser left a row undated, and every row has a date now (`expireDecisions`).
+
+ /** And this long after it closes there is nothing left of it. `prune`. */
+ const FORGOTTEN_AFTER_DAYS = 180;
+
+ /** How many the panel has room for before the rest wait their turn. */
+ const PANEL_ROWS = 6;
+
+ /** The world tick that expires a decision runs on this stride, not on the hour. */
+ const TICK_DAYS = 2;
+
+ /** What the save keeps of the notification list before the oldest fall off. */
+ const NOTICES_KEPT = 500;
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // Words
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ const ORDINALS = [
+   'first', 'second', 'third', 'fourth', 'fifth', 'sixth',
+   'seventh', 'eighth', 'ninth', 'tenth', 'eleventh', 'twelfth',
+ ];
+
+ /** "third", and past the words "21st" rather than the "21th" a bare suffix gives. */
+ function ordinal(n: number): string {
+   const word = ORDINALS[n - 1];
+   if (word) return word;
+   const tens = n % 100;
+   if (tens >= 11 && tens <= 13) return `${n}th`;
+   return `${n}${['th', 'st', 'nd', 'rd'][n % 10] ?? 'th'}`;
+ }
+
+ /** Numbers under ten are words in prose. The house rule, kept with the others. */
+ const SMALL = ['no', 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', 'five', 'six', 'seven', 'eight', 'nine'] as const;
+ const countWord = (n: number): string => SMALL[n] ?? String(n);
+
+ /** "3 weeks ago", and "just now" where `formatRelative` says "now". */
+ // In words, as a sentence says it (from 2026-10-17): until then “It came up 2d 3h ago”, the Calendar’s form.
+ const ago = (at: number, now: number): string => { const r = formatRelativeWords(at, now); return r === 'now' ? 'just now' : r; };
+
+ /**
+  * What a question or a notice is about, by who raised it, in the player’s words (from 2026-10-17, brief 14). Until then
+  * it was who "put it in front of you": "the machinery that keeps the days running", "the money", "the roof over your
+  * head". The categories of systems that went (career, property, travel and the rest) stay for what an older save keeps.
+  */
+ const ABOUT: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
+   system: 'the game itself',
+   schedule: 'your calendar',
+   life: 'your day-to-day life',
+   personal: 'your own affairs',
+   money: 'your money',
+   bank: 'your bank',
+   school: 'your school',
+   tax: 'your taxes',
+   taxes: 'your taxes',
+   papers: 'your papers',
+   benefits: 'your benefits',
+   health: 'your health',
+   home: 'your home',
+   career: 'your work',
+   property: 'your home',
+   travel: 'your travel',
+   relationship: 'someone you know',
+   legal: 'a legal matter',
+   business: 'your business',
+   reimbursement: 'a reimbursement',
+ };
+
+ const aboutOf = (category: string): string => ABOUT[category] ?? 'something in your life';
+
+ /** The category as a label, for the one figure grid. */
+ const categoryLabel = (category: string): string =>
+   titleCaseLabel(category.replace(/[_/]+/g, ' ').trim()) || 'Not Recorded';
+
+ /**
+  * A title as a name: no underscore, no slash, no long run of digits, and Title
+  * Case where it reads as a label rather than as a sentence.
+  *
+  * A title is caller-supplied prose and can carry any of the three. Said aloud
+  * there is an "and" in a slash, and a long run of digits is read as the number
+  * it is — the same reading `place` gives a census tract, for the same reason:
+  * a long run of digits is an identifier, not a name. A year is the exception,
+  * and it’s the only four-digit run a title carries ("Welcome To The Class Of
+  * 2029", "Your 2026 Tax Return"): until 2026-10-17 every run of four or more
+  * was grouped, and those looks were named "Class Of 2,029" and "Your 2,026 Tax
+  * Return" (found by brief 13's interface playthroughs).
+  */
+ const YEAR = /^(1[89]|2\d)\d\d$/;
+ function nameOf(title: string, fallback: string): string {
+   const plain = title
+     .replace(/\s*\/\s*/g, ' and ')
+     .replace(/_+/g, ' ')
+     .replace(/\d{4,}/g, (run) => (YEAR.test(run) ? run : Number(run).toLocaleString('en-US')))
+     .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
+     .trim();
+   return plain ? titleCaseLabel(plain) : fallback;
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * A figure on the hundred-point scale, as a word. Until 2026-10-17 each band said where a thing sat ("nothing but an
+  * overdue thing sits above it", "it will keep for a day", "nothing bad happens while it sits there"), which the order
+  * (`openDecisions`) and the dates didn’t bear out: another question of 90 sits above one of 86, and one of 45 can be due
+  * tomorrow.
+  */
+ function weightOf(urgency: number): string {
+   if (urgency >= 85) return 'very high';
+   if (urgency >= 65) return 'high';
+   if (urgency >= 40) return 'ordinary';
+   return 'low';
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * A way onto the thing a record points at, labeled with that thing’s own name.
+  *
+  * The `lookExists` guard is not belt and braces. An older save carries pointers
+  * of kinds the registry has never heard of — `'project'`, `'audition'` and
+  * `'property'` — so the guard fires on real records, and what it buys is a row
+  * with no way out rather than a link onto a page that does not exist.
+  */
+ function wayTo(sim: Simulation, subject: Subject, detail: string): Way | undefined {
+   if (!lookExists(sim, subject)) return undefined;
+   const found = resolveLook(sim, subject);
+   if (!found || 'gone' in found || !found.name) return undefined;
+   return { to: subject, label: found.name, detail };
+ }
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // A decision — something waiting on you
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ type Stage = 'open' | 'answered' | 'ran out' | 'let go';
+
+ /** A closed question’s state, as the figure grid says it. */
+ const STAGE_WORD: Readonly<Record<Stage, string>> = { open: 'Open', answered: 'Dealt with', 'ran out': 'Closed after its date', 'let go': 'Dismissed' };
+
+ function stageOf(decision: DecisionItem): Stage {
+   if (decision.dismissedAt !== undefined) return 'let go';
+   if (decision.resolvedAt !== undefined) {
+     return decision.dueAt <= decision.resolvedAt ? 'ran out' : 'answered';
+   }
+   return 'open';
+ }
+
+ const closedAtOf = (decision: DecisionItem): number | undefined =>
+   decision.dismissedAt ?? decision.resolvedAt;
+
+ /**
+  * One sentence, second person, true at this instant. An overdue question is open only until the next world tick closes
+  * it (`expireDecisions`), and the tick comes every two days. A question is dealt with by an answer on Home or by acting
+  * on its own screen (the raisers' own `resolvedAt`); one closed after its date may have been either, or the tick.
+  */
+ function decisionSentence(decision: DecisionItem, stage: Stage, sim: Simulation): string {
+   switch (stage) {
+     case 'open':
+       if (decision.dueAt < sim.now) {
+         return `Its date passed ${ago(decision.dueAt, sim.now)}. It stays at the top of What Needs You until it closes by itself, within ${countWord(TICK_DAYS)} days.`;
+       }
+       return `Answer it by ${formatDate(decision.dueAt, sim.zone)}. That’s ${formatRelativeWords(decision.dueAt, sim.now)}.`;
+     case 'answered':
+       return `It was dealt with ${ago(closedAtOf(decision) ?? sim.now, sim.now)}, so it’s no longer in What Needs You.`;
+     case 'ran out':
+       return 'It closed after its date had passed, so it isn’t asking you for anything now.';
+     case 'let go':
+       return `You dismissed it from Home ${ago(closedAtOf(decision) ?? sim.now, sim.now)}. Dismissing only takes it off the list: what it was about still stands, and its date is ${formatDate(decision.dueAt, sim.zone)}.`;
+   }
+ }
+
+ defineLook<DecisionItem>('decision', {
+   gone: `That question closed more than ${FORGOTTEN_AFTER_DAYS} days ago, so there’s nothing left to open.`,
+   resolve: (sim, id) => sim.universe.decisions[id],
+   seeds: (sim) => {
+     const waiting = openDecisions(sim).map((d) => d.id);
+     const rest = Object.keys(sim.universe.decisions).filter((id) => !waiting.includes(id));
+     return [...waiting, ...rest].slice(0, 12);
+   },
+   look: (decision, { sim }) => {
+     const stage = stageOf(decision);
+     const urgency = Math.round(decision.urgency);
+     const waiting = openDecisions(sim);
+     const place = waiting.findIndex((d) => d.id === decision.id) + 1;
+     const overdue = decision.dueAt < sim.now;
+     const closedAt = closedAtOf(decision);
+     const forgottenAt = (closedAt ?? sim.now) + FORGOTTEN_AFTER_DAYS * MS_DAY;
+
+     const ways: Way[] = [];
+     const about = subjectForRef(decision);
+     const aboutWay = about && wayTo(sim, about, 'Open what this question is about');
+     if (aboutWay) ways.push(aboutWay);
+
+     // The order is `openDecisions`': overdue first, then the most urgent, then the soonest due.
+     const standing = stage === 'open'
+       ? (overdue
+         ? 'Being overdue puts it first, ahead of anything more urgent.'
+         : waiting.length === 1
+           ? 'It’s the only question waiting on you.'
+           : `It’s ${ordinal(place)} of the ${countWord(waiting.length)} questions waiting on you.`)
+       : `It closed ${ago(closedAt ?? sim.now, sim.now)}, and Home no longer lists it.`;
+
+     const ending = stage === 'open'
+       ? `It closes when you answer it on Home or deal with it on its own screen. If you don’t, it closes by itself within ${countWord(TICK_DAYS)} days after its date, ${formatDate(decision.dueAt, sim.zone)}. You can still open it here for ${FORGOTTEN_AFTER_DAYS} days after it closes.`
+       : `You can still open it here until ${formatDate(forgottenAt, sim.zone)}, ${FORGOTTEN_AFTER_DAYS} days after it closed.`;
+
+     // Home renders the actions, Go There where there is a route, and Dismiss on every row it prints, but only for the
+     // rows it prints.
+     const labels = decision.actions.map((action) => titleCaseLabel(action.label));
+     const onPanel = stage === 'open' && place > 0 && place <= PANEL_ROWS;
+     const offered = stage !== 'open'
+       ? 'It’s no longer on Home, so there’s nothing to press.'
+       : !onPanel
+         ? `Home shows the first ${countWord(PANEL_ROWS)} questions, and this one is further down. Its buttons appear there once one of the questions above it closes.`
+         : `On Home, its buttons are ${spokenList([...labels, ...(decision.route ? ['Go There'] : []), 'Dismiss'])}. Reading it here changes nothing.`;
+
+     return {
+       name: nameOf(decision.title, 'A Question For You'),
+       kind: stage === 'open' ? 'Waiting On You' : 'No Longer Waiting',
+       parent: at('person', sim.universe.playerId),
+       summary: decisionSentence(decision, stage, sim),
+       body: (
+         <>
+           {/* What it asks, then what to press, then when it closes, then where it ranks (from 2026-10-20, brief 17): until
+               then the buttons came last, under its urgency and its closing rules. */}
+           {decision.detail && <p className="small muted">{decision.detail}</p>}
+           <p className="small muted">{offered}</p>
+           <p className="small muted">{ending}</p>
+           <p className="small muted">
+             {`It came up ${ago(decision.createdAt, sim.now)}, about ${aboutOf(decision.category)}. Its urgency is ${weightOf(urgency)}, at ${outOf(urgency)}. `}
+             {'If it comes up again while it’s open, its urgency can only go up. '}
+             {standing}
+           </p>
+           <div className="grid grid-3">
+             <Stat label="Urgency" value={urgency} note="Out of 100. Home shows it only as a colored stripe" />
+             <Stat label="About" value={categoryLabel(decision.category)} />
+             <Stat
+               label="Raised"
+               value={formatDate(decision.createdAt, sim.zone)}
+               // An undated row’s note was the day it would go quiet ("Quiet by"), until 2026-10-14, when every row
+               // had a date and the rule went.
+               note={stage !== 'open' ? `Closed ${formatDate(closedAt ?? sim.now, sim.zone)}` : 'It closes by itself after its date'}
+             />
+             <Stat
+               label="Due"
+               value={formatDate(decision.dueAt, sim.zone)}
+               note={formatRelative(decision.dueAt, sim.now)}
+               tone={overdue ? 'negative' : undefined}
+             />
+             <Stat
+               label="Place On Home"
+               value={stage === 'open' ? `${place} of ${waiting.length}` : 'Not listed'}
+               note={stage === 'open' ? 'Overdue first, then the most urgent' : STAGE_WORD[stage]}
+             />
+             <Stat
+               label="Answers"
+               value={decision.actions.length > 0 ? decision.actions.length : 'None'}
+               note={decision.actions.length > 0 ? 'On Home, beside Dismiss' : 'It can only be dismissed'}
+             />
+           </div>
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways,
+       // Until 2026-10-14 it said the save kept a row waved away early to its date, and an undated row’s ninety days.
+       provenance: 'Urgency is estimated, from 0 to 100.',
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // A notification — something you were told
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ defineLook<Notice>('notification', {
+   gone: `That notice is gone. SLATE keeps only your latest ${NOTICES_KEPT} notices, and this one was older.`,
+   resolve: (sim, id) => sim.universe.notifications.find((n) => n.id === id),
+   seeds: (sim) => {
+     const unread = unreadNotifications(sim).slice(0, 6).map((n) => n.id);
+     const read = sim.universe.notifications.filter((n) => n.read).slice(-6).map((n) => n.id);
+     return [...unread, ...read];
+   },
+   look: (note, { sim }) => {
+     const unread = unreadNotifications(sim);
+     const place = unread.findIndex((n) => n.id === note.id) + 1;
+     const importance = Math.round(note.importance);
+
+     const ways: Way[] = [];
+     const about = subjectForRef(note);
+     const aboutWay = about && wayTo(sim, about, 'Open what this notice is about');
+     if (aboutWay) ways.push(aboutWay);
+     const alsoWaiting = note.refType
+       ? openDecisions(sim).find((d) => d.refType === note.refType && d.refId === note.refId)
+       : undefined;
+     if (alsoWaiting) {
+       ways.push({
+         to: at('decision', alsoWaiting.id),
+         label: nameOf(alsoWaiting.title, 'The Open Question'),
+         detail: 'The question about the same thing, still waiting on you',
+       });
+     }
+
+     // Mark Read on Home sends no ids, so it marks every unread notice read (`world.mark_read`). Go There is on Home’s row
+     // for an unread notice with a route, and Home lists only the unread: until 2026-10-20 (brief 17) a notice already
+     // read was told "On Home, Go There opens the screen it’s about" too, where it’s on no list with one.
+     const marking = unread.length === 1 ? 'Mark 1 Read marks it read' : `Mark ${unread.length} Read marks all ${unread.length} unread notices read at once`;
+     const onHome = note.route ? `On Home, Go There opens the screen it’s about, and ${marking}.` : `On Home, ${marking}.`;
+
+     return {
+       name: nameOf(note.title, 'A Notice With No Title'),
+       kind: 'Notice',
+       parent: at('person', sim.universe.playerId),
+       summary: note.read
+         ? `You’ve read this notice. It came in ${ago(note.at, sim.now)}.`
+         : unread.length === 1
+           ? `It came in ${ago(note.at, sim.now)}, and it’s your only unread notice.`
+           : `It came in ${ago(note.at, sim.now)}. It’s ${ordinal(place)} of your ${countWord(unread.length)} unread notices.`,
+       body: (
+         <>
+           {/* What it says, then what to press, then where it ranks (from 2026-10-20, brief 17): until then one paragraph
+               of five sentences, its importance and the order first and the buttons last. */}
+           {note.body && <p className="small muted">{note.body}</p>}
+           <p className="small muted">
+             {note.read
+               ? `SLATE keeps your latest ${NOTICES_KEPT} notices, so this one stays until ${NOTICES_KEPT} newer ones have come in.`
+               : `Opening it here doesn’t mark it read. ${onHome}`}
+           </p>
+           <p className="small muted">
+             {`It’s about ${aboutOf(note.category)}, and its importance is ${outOf(importance)}. Unread notices are listed most important first, and the newer first when two are equal.`}
+           </p>
+           <div className="grid grid-3">
+             <Stat label="Importance" value={importance} note="Out of 100. It sets the order" />
+             <Stat label="Arrived" value={formatDate(note.at, sim.zone)} note={formatRelative(note.at, sim.now)} />
+             <Stat label="About" value={categoryLabel(note.category)} />
+             <Stat
+               label="Status"
+               value={note.read ? 'Read' : 'Unread'}
+               note={note.read ? 'No longer listed on Home' : `${place} of ${unread.length} unread`}
+             />
+             <Stat
+               label="What It’s About"
+               value={aboutWay ? aboutWay.label : 'Not named'}
+               note={aboutWay ? 'Open it below' : 'This notice doesn’t name one'}
+             />
+             <Stat label="Kept" value={`Latest ${NOTICES_KEPT}`} note="Older ones are dropped" />
+           </div>
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways,
+       // Until 2026-10-17 it said, under a notice that named nothing, that nothing in the world named one so far, and
+       // that the day something did it would open onto it: the game’s history, not the player’s (brief 14).
+       provenance: aboutWay ? 'The link below opens what this notice is about.' : undefined,
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — the bank, and a line on its statement.
+  *
+  * The Bank screen names two things the money looks did not: the bank itself,
+  * at the head of the screen, and every line on a statement. Both were dead
+  * text. A bank is a thing in the world — a real institution in a real
+  * country, holding real accounts in your name — and a statement line is a
+  * moment money moved, between accounts that are themselves things. So both
+  * open, and both lead somewhere: the bank into the accounts it holds and the
+  * last money through them, a line into each account it touched and the day it
+  * happened.
+  *
+  * Nothing here is a figure anybody typed. A bank’s total is the sum of the
+  * balances it holds, each the sum of its postings; a line’s amount is what its
+  * postings did to the account (`Ledger.effectOn`).
+  */
+
+ import { formatMoney, saveCurrency } from '@/engine/core/money';
+ import { Ledger, isLiability, type Account, type LedgerTransaction } from '@/engine/core/ledger';
+ import { dateKey, formatDate, formatWeekdayDate } from '@/engine/core/time';
+ import { titleCaseLabel } from '@/engine/core/text';
+ import { bankById, type Bank } from '@/engine/content/banks';
+ import { COUNTRIES } from '@/engine/content/geography';
+ import { bankOf } from '@/engine/systems/banking';
+ import { theCountry } from '@/engine/systems/documents';
+ import { balanceText, heldOf } from '@/engine/systems/abroad';
+ import type { Simulation } from '@/engine';
+ import { Stat } from '@/ui/components/primitives';
+ import { defineLook, lookExists, type Way } from './registry';
+ import { at } from './subject';
+ import { spokenList, nameable } from './words';
+
+ /** How many of the last lines through a bank its look offers. */
+ const RECENT_LINES = 5;
+
+ /** Whether a string reads as a name: no identifier shapes, and a plain capital or digit first. */
+ const passesAsName = nameable;
+
+ /**
+  * A world word that passes as a name. A memo has each word capitalized, as a
+  * label is written; a bank’s own name is left as the bank writes it. One that
+  * opens on a marked letter, as Íslandsbanki does, is written without the mark
+  * before it falls back to the plain word.
+  */
+ function asName(text: string, fallback: string, recase = true): string {
+   const trimmed = text.trim();
+   const named = recase ? trimmed.split(' ').map((w) => w.replace(/^[a-z]/, (c) => c.toUpperCase())).join(' ') : trimmed;
+   if (passesAsName(named)) return named;
+   const plain = named.normalize('NFD').replace(/[̀-ͯ]/g, '');
+   return passesAsName(plain) ? plain : fallback;
+ }
+
+ /** The accounts a person has open at one bank, the one the day comes out of first. */
+ function accountsAt(sim: Simulation, bankId: string): Account[] {
+   const player = sim.universe.people[sim.universe.playerId];
+   return Object.values(sim.universe.accounts)
+     .filter((a) => a.ownerId === sim.universe.playerId && a.bankId === bankId && !a.nominal && !a.closedAt)
+     .sort((a, b) => Number(b.id === player?.primaryAccountId) - Number(a.id === player?.primaryAccountId));
+ }
+
+ /** The latest lines through any of a set of accounts, newest first. */
+ function latestThrough(sim: Simulation, ids: ReadonlySet<string>, count: number): LedgerTransaction[] {
+   const list = sim.universe.transactions;
+   const out: LedgerTransaction[] = [];
+   for (let i = list.length - 1; i >= 0 && out.length < count; i -= 1) {
+     const txn = list[i]!;
+     if (txn.postings.some((p) => ids.has(p.accountId))) out.push(txn);
+   }
+   return out;
+ }
+
+ /** The country a bank is in, by its ISO code, where the world has it. */
+ const countryOfIso = (iso: string) => COUNTRIES.all().find((c) => c.iso2?.toUpperCase() === iso.toUpperCase());
+
+ /**
+  * What an owed or held figure says about an account, in a few words: an account kept at home in its own money, with the
+  * dollars beside (`balanceText`, from 2026-10-16).
+  */
+ function standing(sim: Simulation, a: Account, cur: string): string {
+   return isLiability(a.kind)
+     ? `${formatMoney(Math.max(0, -a.balance), cur)} owed on it`
+     : `${balanceText(sim, a)} in it`;
+ }
+
+ /** What a line moved on an account kept in another currency, in that currency: the sum of its postings’ own figures. */
+ function nativeOn(txn: LedgerTransaction, account: Account): number | undefined {
+   if (!account.currency) return undefined;
+   return txn.postings.filter((p) => p.accountId === account.id).reduce((sum, p) => sum + (p.native ?? 0), 0);
+ }
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // The bank
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ interface TheBank { bank: Bank; accounts: Account[]; home: boolean }
+
+ defineLook<TheBank>('bank', {
+   gone: 'You don’t have anything at that bank anymore, so there’s nothing to show.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => {
+     const bank = bankById(id);
+     if (!bank) return undefined;
+     const player = sim.universe.people[sim.universe.playerId];
+     const home = player ? bankOf(sim, player)?.id === bank.id : false;
+     const accounts = accountsAt(sim, bank.id);
+     if (!home && accounts.length === 0) return undefined;
+     return { bank, accounts, home };
+   },
+   seeds: (sim) => {
+     const player = sim.universe.people[sim.universe.playerId];
+     const id = player ? bankOf(sim, player)?.id : undefined;
+     return id ? [id] : [];
+   },
+   look: ({ bank, accounts, home }, { sim }) => {
+     const cur = saveCurrency(sim.universe);
+     const held = accounts.filter((a) => !isLiability(a.kind)).reduce((s, a) => s + a.balance, 0);
+     const owed = accounts.filter((a) => isLiability(a.kind)).reduce((s, a) => s + Math.max(0, -a.balance), 0);
+     const country = countryOfIso(bank.iso);
+     // A bank kept at home holds its accounts in its own money: said in it, with the dollars beside (from 2026-10-16).
+     const kept = accounts.some((a) => a.currency);
+     const heldWords = kept ? `${formatMoney(accounts.filter((a) => !isLiability(a.kind)).reduce((s, a) => s + heldOf(a), 0), bank.currency)} (${formatMoney(held, cur)})` : formatMoney(held, cur);
+
+     const ways: Way[] = accounts.map((a) => ({
+       to: at('account', a.id),
+       label: a.name,
+       detail: `${a.last4 ? `Ending ${a.last4}, ` : ''}${standing(sim, a, cur)}`,
+     }));
+     for (const txn of latestThrough(sim, new Set(accounts.map((a) => a.id)), RECENT_LINES)) {
+       ways.push({
+         to: at('transaction', txn.id),
+         label: asName(txn.memo, 'A Payment'),
+         detail: `A recent payment through your accounts here, on ${formatDate(txn.at, sim.homeZone)}`,
+       });
+     }
+     if (country && lookExists(sim, at('country', country.id))) {
+       ways.push({ to: at('country', country.id), label: country.name, detail: 'The country whose rules the bank follows, and whose money it uses' });
+     }
+     if (lookExists(sim, at('currency', bank.currency))) {
+       ways.push({ to: at('currency', bank.currency), label: bank.currency, detail: 'The currency your accounts there are kept in, and what it’s worth' });
+     }
+
+     const named = accounts.map((a) => a.name);
+     return {
+       name: asName(bank.name, 'Your Bank', false),
+       kind: home ? 'Your Everyday Bank' : 'Another Bank You Use',
+       parent: at('person', sim.universe.playerId),
+       summary: accounts.length === 0
+         ? 'You have nothing open here now.'
+         : owed > 0
+           ? `You have ${heldWords} here and owe it ${formatMoney(owed, cur)}, across ${named.length === 1 ? 'one account' : `${named.length} accounts`}.`
+           : `You have ${heldWords} here, across ${named.length === 1 ? 'one account' : `${named.length} accounts`}.`,
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <p className="small">
+             {bank.name} is a bank{country ? ` in ${theCountry(country.name)}` : ''}, and keeps its accounts in {bank.currency}.
+             {named.length > 0 ? ` You have ${spokenList(named)} here.` : ''}
+             {home ? ' Your primary account is here, so your debit card’s everyday purchases come from it.' : ' Your primary account is at another bank. What’s here stays here until you move it.'}
+           </p>
+           <div className="grid grid-3">
+             <Stat label="Held Here" value={<span className="mono">{kept ? heldWords : formatMoney(held, cur)}</span>} note="In your accounts here" />
+             <Stat label="Owed Here" value={<span className="mono">{formatMoney(owed, cur)}</span>} tone={owed > 0 ? 'negative' : undefined} note="On its cards and loans" />
+             <Stat label="Accounts" value={String(accounts.length)} note="Open in your name" />
+           </div>
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways,
+       provenance: 'Each balance is the total of every payment in and out of the account, added up again each time you look.',
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // One line on a statement
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ interface TheLine { txn: LedgerTransaction; touched: { account: Account; delta: number }[] }
+
+ /** A transaction by its id, newest first, since the latest are the ones asked for. */
+ function transactionById(sim: Simulation, id: string): LedgerTransaction | undefined {
+   const list = sim.universe.transactions;
+   for (let i = list.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) if (list[i]!.id === id) return list[i];
+   return undefined;
+ }
+
+ /** What one account saw of a line, in words: on an account kept at home, its own figure with the dollars beside. */
+ function movedWords(account: Account, delta: number, cur: string, native?: number): string {
+   const amount = native !== undefined && account.currency ? `${formatMoney(Math.abs(native), account.currency)} (${formatMoney(Math.abs(delta), cur)})` : formatMoney(Math.abs(delta), cur);
+   if (isLiability(account.kind)) {
+     return delta < 0 ? `added ${amount} to what you owe on ${account.name}` : `took ${amount} off what you owe on ${account.name}`;
+   }
+   return delta > 0 ? `put ${amount} into ${account.name}` : `took ${amount} out of ${account.name}`;
+ }
+
+ defineLook<TheLine>('transaction', {
+   gone: 'That entry is no longer on any of your statements.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => {
+     const txn = transactionById(sim, id);
+     if (!txn) return undefined;
+     const touched = txn.postings
+       .map((p) => sim.ledger.tryAccount(p.accountId))
+       .filter((a): a is Account => !!a && !a.nominal && a.ownerId === sim.universe.playerId)
+       .filter((a, i, all) => all.findIndex((b) => b.id === a.id) === i)
+       .map((account) => ({ account, delta: Ledger.effectOn(txn, account.id) }))
+       .filter((one) => one.delta !== 0);
+     if (touched.length === 0) return undefined;
+     return { txn, touched };
+   },
+   seeds: (sim) => {
+     const mine = new Set(sim.ledger.accountsOf(sim.universe.playerId).filter((a) => !a.nominal).map((a) => a.id));
+     return latestThrough(sim, mine, 3).map((t) => t.id);
+   },
+   look: ({ txn, touched }, { sim }) => {
+     const cur = saveCurrency(sim.universe);
+     const zone = sim.homeZone;
+     const when = formatWeekdayDate(txn.at, zone);
+     const pending = txn.postsAt !== undefined && txn.postsAt > sim.now;
+     const said = touched.map((one) => movedWords(one.account, one.delta, cur, nativeOn(txn, one.account)));
+     const first = touched[0]!;
+     const category = titleCaseLabel(txn.category.replace(/_/g, ' '));
+
+     const ways: Way[] = touched
+       .filter((one) => lookExists(sim, at('account', one.account.id)))
+       .map((one) => ({
+         to: at('account', one.account.id),
+         label: one.account.name,
+         detail: `The account it ${one.delta > 0 ? 'came into' : 'came out of'}, and ${standing(sim, one.account, cur)} now`,
+       }));
+     ways.push({ to: at('day', dateKey(txn.at, zone)), label: when, detail: 'The day it went through, and everything else on it' });
+     for (const other of [txn.reverses, txn.reversedBy]) {
+       if (other && transactionById(sim, other)) {
+         ways.push({
+           to: at('transaction', other),
+           label: other === txn.reverses ? 'The Entry It Reversed' : 'The Entry That Reversed It',
+           detail: other === txn.reverses ? 'The entry this one reversed, to the cent' : 'The entry that reversed this one, to the cent',
+         });
+       }
+     }
+
+     return {
+       name: asName(txn.memo, category || 'A Payment'),
+       kind: 'An Entry On A Statement',
+       parent: at('account', first.account.id),
+       summary: `It ${spokenList(said)}, on ${when}.`,
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <p className="small">
+             The bank files it under {category.toLowerCase() || 'nothing in particular'}.{' '}
+             {pending
+               ? `It’s pending: it’s already taken off your available balance, and it posts on ${formatDate(txn.postsAt!, zone)}.`
+               : txn.reversedBy ? 'It was reversed later, so it no longer counts against you.' : 'It has posted.'}
+           </p>
+           <div className="grid grid-3">
+             <Stat
+               label="Amount"
+               value={<span className="mono">{first.account.currency ? `${formatMoney(Math.abs(nativeOn(txn, first.account) ?? 0), first.account.currency)} (${formatMoney(Math.abs(first.delta), cur)})` : formatMoney(Math.abs(first.delta), cur)}</span>}
+               tone={first.delta < 0 ? 'negative' : 'positive'}
+               note={first.delta > 0 ? (isLiability(first.account.kind) ? 'Off what’s owed' : 'In') : (isLiability(first.account.kind) ? 'Onto what’s owed' : 'Out')}
+             />
+             <Stat label="When" value={formatDate(txn.at, zone)} note={pending ? 'Still pending' : 'Posted'} />
+             <Stat label="Accounts" value={String(touched.length)} note={touched.length === 1 ? 'Your account it touched' : 'Your accounts it moved money between'} />
+           </div>
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways,
+       provenance: 'Every entry has a matching one on the other side of the books, and the two add up to zero.',
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — a classmate, opened (from 2026-10-12).

+ interface TheClassmate { person: Person; mate: Classmate; i: number }

+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — the day you are standing in, and everything the clock puts on it.
+  *
+  * Home’s head prints a weekday, a date, a clock time, a zone and a season, and
+  * every one of them is a dead end today. So is the Calendar’s next commitment,
+  * and so are the five rows under it. They are not thin things: `calendar.ts`
+  * already buckets the timeline into days, flags the collisions, and hangs the
+  * observances of whatever country the player is standing in off each one, and
+  * `time.ts` and `sun.ts` know what the light is doing on any date at all.
+  *
+  * Three kinds live here. `day` is one date — today by default, any date by
+  * key — with its entries, its observances, its season and its light. `entry`
+  * is one thing on the calendar, and it says everything `CalendarWorkspace`'s
+  * read-only EntryDetail modal says — the same four facts, the same three
+  * sentences — plus the two that modal never said: whether you are in the
+  * right city for it, and what it is colliding with. `season` is the quarter
+  * of the year the day sits in, a real thing in a place rather than a label:
+  * at Reykjavík’s latitude a season is the difference between twenty-one hours
+  * of light and four.
+  *
+  * A day hangs beneath the city it is a day in, because a day is kept in that
+  * city’s clock, keeps that country’s holidays and takes its light from that
+  * latitude. Walking from one day to the next stops at a week out in either
+  * direction — the calendar runs forever and a chain that runs forever is not
+  * a chain.
+  */
+
+ import { normalFor, toFahrenheit, usesFahrenheit } from '@/engine/content/climate';
+ import { CITIES, COUNTRIES, REGIONS, type City } from '@/engine/content/geography';
+ import { holidayLabel, holidaysAcross, type KeptHoliday } from '@/engine/content/holidays';
+ import { formatDaylight, sunTimes, type SunTimes } from '@/engine/core/sun';
+ import { plural, titleCaseLabel } from '@/engine/core/text';
+ import {
+   MONTH_NAMES, MS_DAY, MS_HOUR, MS_MINUTE, WEEKDAY_NAMES,
+   addDays, dateKey, daysBetween, formatDate, formatDuration, formatTime,
+   instantFromZoned, parseDateKey, seasonOf, startOfDay, startOfNextDay, zoneAbbreviation, zonedParts,
+   type Instant, type Season, type TimeZone, type ZonedParts,
+ } from '@/engine/core/time';
+ import { forecastFor } from '@/engine/systems/weather';
+ import { LEGEND_BY_CATEGORY, entriesBetween, keptCalendars, upcoming, type CalendarEntry } from '@/engine/world/calendar';
+ import { PLAN_KIND } from '@/engine/world/plans';
+ import type { Simulation } from '@/engine';
+ import { Stat } from '@/ui/components/primitives';
+ import { Open } from './Look';
+ import { defineLook, type Way } from './registry';
+ import { at } from './subject';
+ import { isAre, spokenList, toStart } from './words';
+
+ /** How far either side of today one day will walk to another. */
+ const REACH = 6;
+
+ /** How many days ahead the sky is worked out, matching the weather’s own week. */
+ const FORECAST = 6;
+
+ const SEASONS: readonly Season[] = ['Spring', 'Summer', 'Autumn', 'Winter'];
+
+ const A_DATE = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/;
+
+ /** Numbers under ten are words in prose, and figures only in the facts. */
+ const SMALL = ['no', 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', 'five', 'six', 'seven', 'eight', 'nine'];
+
+ /** A number the way it is said in a sentence: "three", "eleven". */
+ const spokenNumber = (n: number): string => `${SMALL[n] ?? n}`;
+
+ /** "two things", "eleven things", agreeing with itself the way `plural` does. */
+ function count(n: number, one: string, many = `${one}s`): string {
+   return `${spokenNumber(n)} ${n === 1 ? one : many}`;
+ }
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // Reading the world
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ /** The city the player is standing in. Every day is somewhere. */
+ function standingIn(sim: Simulation): City | undefined {
+   const player = sim.universe.people[sim.universe.playerId];
+   return player ? CITIES.get(player.currentLocationId) : undefined;
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * Whether a city opens onto anything.
+  *
+  * The place look needs a region to resolve its taxes through, and a handful
+  * of territories in the gazetteer carry none. A way in is never painted
+  * unless it would open.
+  */
+ const placeOpens = (city: City | undefined): boolean => !!city && !!REGIONS.get(city.parentId);
+
+ /**
+  * A label made safe to be a name: no underscore, no slash, Title Case.
+  *
+  * The trailing full stop is taken off first, because `titleCaseLabel` reads
+  * anything ending in one as prose and hands it back untouched — which is how
+  * a lower-case sentence would arrive where a name belongs. Whatever survives
+  * that, the first letter is raised, so a name always starts as a name does.
+  */
+ function asName(title: string): string {
+   const clean = title.replace(/\s*\/\s*/g, ' and ').replace(/_+/g, ' ')
+     .replace(/[.?!]+$/, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
+   const cased = titleCaseLabel(clean).trim();
+   return cased ? cased[0]!.toUpperCase() + cased.slice(1) : cased;
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * An entry’s own state, in the word the game shows for it.
+  *
+  * A label map, because the schedule’s ids are not renamed to improve a label
+  * and two of them read badly on a screen: `done` is not what a person calls a
+  * thing they turned up to, and `cancelled` is spelled the other way here.
+  */
+ const STATUS_WORD: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
+   pending: 'Pending',
+   done: 'Completed',
+   cancelled: 'Canceled',
+   missed: 'Missed',
+   observance: 'Observance',
+ };
+
+ const statusWord = (entry: CalendarEntry): string =>
+   STATUS_WORD[entry.status] ?? titleCaseLabel(entry.status);
+
+ /** "Monday, March 2". The date a person says, and never the year. */
+ const dayName = (parts: ZonedParts): string =>
+   `${WEEKDAY_NAMES[parts.weekday]}, ${MONTH_NAMES[parts.month - 1]} ${parts.day}`;
+
+ /** What the eyebrow calls a date, counted from today. */
+ function dayKindOf(offset: number): string {
+   if (offset === 0) return 'The Day';
+   if (offset === 1) return 'Tomorrow';
+   if (offset === -1) return 'Yesterday';
+   return offset > 0 ? 'A Day Coming' : 'A Day Gone';
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * When something is, the way a person says it.
+  *
+  * `formatRelative` is the engine’s own answer and it is not prose: it prints
+  * "in 2d 3h" and "in 1.5 years", which is a readout, not a sentence. A look
+  * leads with a sentence, so this counts in whole days off the local calendar
+  * and spells the small numbers out.
+  */
+ function spokenWhen(target: Instant, sim: Simulation, zone: TimeZone): string {
+   const offset = daysBetween(sim.now, target, zone);
+   if (offset === 0) {
+     const hours = Math.round((target - sim.now) / MS_HOUR);
+     if (hours === 0) return 'within the hour';
+     return hours > 0 ? `in ${count(hours, 'hour')}` : `${count(-hours, 'hour')} ago`;
+   }
+   if (offset === 1) return 'tomorrow';
+   if (offset === -1) return 'yesterday';
+   const away = Math.abs(offset);
+   if (away < 14) return offset > 0 ? `in ${count(away, 'day')}` : `${count(away, 'day')} ago`;
+   if (away < 60) {
+     const weeks = Math.round(away / 7);
+     return offset > 0 ? `in ${count(weeks, 'week')}` : `${count(weeks, 'week')} ago`;
+   }
+   const months = Math.round(away / 30.44);
+   return offset > 0 ? `in ${count(months, 'month')}` : `${count(months, 'month')} ago`;
+ }
+
+ /** How long a commitment runs, or nothing when it is a point in the day. */
+ const lengthOf = (entry: CalendarEntry): string | undefined =>
+   (entry.durationMinutes ? formatDuration(entry.durationMinutes * MS_MINUTE) : undefined);
+
+ /**
+  * What missing a commitment costs, as its handler has it (`systems/school.ts`).
+  * Until 2026-09-27 the entry look said only that it cost "what the Guide
+  * says". It also had the career’s costs (`systems/career.ts`): an audition an
+  * agency got you, a job’s day and a showcase. Those kinds went with the career
+  * on 2026-10-09 and their cases stayed here, so a save from before it, which
+  * keeps what it had settled, was still told an agency would let it go; the
+  * cases went from 2026-10-12.
+  */
+ function missCost(sim: Simulation, id: string): string {
+   const item = sim.universe.scheduled.find((one) => one.id === id);
+   const call = item?.payload.call;
+   switch (item?.kind) {
+     // The excuses classes' handler takes (from 2026-10-20, brief 17): a sick day called in, a hospital bed or an injury
+     // that lays you up (`offSick`). Until then "unless you’re sick or in hospital", where being ill excuses nothing that
+     // isn’t called in, and an injury does.
+     case 'school.classes': return ': an unexcused absence, which the faculty weigh at the term review, unless you called in sick, or you’re in hospital or laid up with an injury';
+     case 'school.call':
+       return call === 'performance' ? ': a grave breach, straight to academic warning, or from warning to dismissal'
+         : call === 'oncall' ? ', and if you’re sent on and not there, it’s a grave breach, straight to academic warning'
+           : ': counted against your attendance, and enough missed calls take you out of the casting pool';
+     case 'school.lab': return ': counted against your attendance and your calls';
+     case 'school.shift': return ': the hours aren’t paid, and an assigned shift counts against your attendance';
+     case 'school.summer': return call === 'performance' ? ', and the company lets you go' : ', and the rehearsal goes on without you';
+     case 'school.cabaret': return ', and the show goes on without you';
+     default: return '';
+   }
+ }
+
+ /** The window an entry occupies, for working out what it collides with. */
+ const endOf = (entry: CalendarEntry): Instant => entry.endsAt ?? entry.at;
+
+ /** The city an entry wants you in, where it names one. */
+ const cityOf = (entry: CalendarEntry): City | undefined =>
+   (entry.locationId ? CITIES.get(entry.locationId) : undefined);
+
+ /**
+  * The clock a time is read off for one entry.
+  *
+  * The calendar is cut into days by the zone the player keeps house in, but a
+  * call time is local: an entry that names a city is at ten-thirty in that
+  * city, and printing the home clock beside that city’s name would be wrong by
+  * however many hours lie between them.
+  */
+ const clockOf = (entry: CalendarEntry, fallback: TimeZone): TimeZone =>
+   cityOf(entry)?.timeZone ?? fallback;
+
+ /** What a way into an entry says before it is taken. */
+ function entryDetail(entry: CalendarEntry, zone: TimeZone): string {
+   const parts = [formatTime(entry.at, clockOf(entry, zone))];
+   const length = lengthOf(entry);
+   if (length) parts.push(length);
+   const city = cityOf(entry);
+   if (city) parts.push(city.name);
+   const line = parts.join(' · ');
+   if (entry.conflicted) return `${line} — it clashes with something else you need to be at`;
+   if (entry.status === 'observance') return `${line} — an observance, not a commitment`;
+   return entry.requiresPlayer ? `${line} — you need to be there` : `${line} — it happens without you`;
+ }
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // One day
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ interface TheDay {
+   key: string;
+   start: Instant;
+   parts: ZonedParts;
+   zone: TimeZone;
+   city: City;
+   offset: number;
+   entries: CalendarEntry[];
+   holidays: KeptHoliday[];
+   sun: SunTimes;
+   season: Season;
+ }
+
+ /** The day a date key names, read out of the live world. */
+ function dayAt(sim: Simulation, key: string): TheDay | undefined {
+   const zone = sim.homeZone;
+   const city = standingIn(sim);
+   if (!city || !A_DATE.test(key)) return undefined;
+
+   const start = startOfDay(parseDateKey(key, zone), zone);
+   if (!Number.isFinite(start) || dateKey(start, zone) !== key) return undefined;
+
+   // The day ends where the next date begins. It was a day added to its start,
+   // which on a day whose clocks skipped midnight was one the next morning, so
+   // the day of the jump listed the next day’s first hour as its own too.
+   const end = startOfNextDay(start, zone);
+   // A day either side, so a collision that starts before midnight is seen.
+   const around = entriesBetween(sim, start - MS_DAY, end + MS_DAY);
+
+   return {
+     key,
+     start,
+     parts: zonedParts(start, zone),
+     zone,
+     city,
+     offset: daysBetween(sim.now, start, zone),
+     entries: around.filter((e) => e.at >= start && e.at < end),
+     holidays: holidaysAcross(start, zone, keptCalendars(sim)),
+     sun: sunTimes(start + MS_DAY / 2, city.latitude, city.longitude, city.timeZone),
+     season: seasonOf(start, zone, city.latitude),
+   };
+ }
+
+ defineLook<TheDay>('day', {
+   gone: 'There’s no such date. The calendar runs on real days, and that isn’t one of them.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => dayAt(sim, id || dateKey(sim.now, sim.homeZone)),
+   seeds: (sim) => {
+     const zone = sim.homeZone;
+     return [
+       dateKey(sim.now, zone),
+       dateKey(addDays(sim.now, 1, zone), zone),
+       dateKey(addDays(sim.now, -1, zone), zone),
+     ];
+   },
+   look: (day, { sim }) => {
+     const { city, entries, holidays, offset, zone } = day;
+     const wants = entries.filter((e) => e.requiresPlayer && e.status === 'pending');
+     const clashes = entries.filter((e) => e.conflicted);
+     const country = COUNTRIES.get(city.countryId)?.name ?? city.countryId.toUpperCase();
+     const observed = holidays.map((h) => h.englishName || h.name);
+     // Whose day it is: the calendar keeps the year of where the player is
+     // standing, and a day says so in that country’s name.
+     const named = (h: KeptHoliday) => h.englishName || h.name;
+     const keptHere = holidays.filter((h) => h.countryId === city.countryId).map(named);
+     // `holidaysAcross` has already dropped the ones kept in another region, so
+     // anything still carrying a subdivision code is kept here and not nationally.
+     const regional = holidays.filter((h) => h.regionCode).length;
+     // A life keeps more than one country’s year. Grouped by whose it is,
+     // because "Iceland and the United States both keep it" and "one is theirs
+     // and one is yours" are different facts about the same day.
+     const byCountry = [...new Map(holidays.map((h) => [h.countryId, h.countryName])).entries()]
+       .map(([id, name]) => ({ name, kept: holidays.filter((h) => h.countryId === id) }));
+
+     const ways: Way[] = entries.slice(0, 8).map((entry) => ({
+       to: at('entry', entry.id),
+       label: asName(entry.title),
+       detail: entryDetail(entry, zone),
+     }));
+
+     ways.push({
+       to: at('season', `${city.id}/${day.season}`),
+       label: day.season,
+       detail: `What ${day.season.toLowerCase()} is like in ${city.name}, and how long it lasts`,
+     });
+     ways.push({
+       to: at('daylight', city.id),
+       label: 'Daylight',
+       detail: lightDetail(day),
+     });
+
+     // The sky, but only as far ahead as the weather is worked out.
+     if (offset >= 0 && offset < FORECAST) {
+       const ahead = forecastFor(sim, city.id, FORECAST)[offset];
