+ // A city
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ defineLook<PlaceProfile>('place', {
+   gone: 'That place isn’t on the map, or the game has too little about it to show.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => profileFor(sim, cityFor(sim, id)),
+   seeds: (sim) => {
+     const ids = [standingIn(sim)?.id, homeCityOf(sim)?.id];
+     return [...new Set(ids.filter((id): id is string => !!id))];
+   },
+   look: (place, { sim }) => {
+     // Where the player stands is where they live (`homeCityOf`, since the scope of 2026-10-09 moved nobody), so a city
+     // is theirs or another. Until 2026-10-13 the look told standing here from living here too, and had words for each
+     // apart, “Where You Are”, “Home, … back”, “You’re … from home” and “you’re not in it today”, that no life reached.
+     const isHome = place.homeCity?.id === place.city.id;
+     const region = REGIONS.get(place.city.parentId);
+     const climate = CLIMATE_NAMES[climateTypeFor(place.city)].toLowerCase();
+     const label = placeKindLabel(place.city);
+     const people = formatPeople(place.cityPopulation);
+     const rent = place.localRent ?? formatAtlasCompact(place.medianRentCents);
+     const layers = resolveIncomeTaxLayers(place.city.id, sim.now);
+     // A state with no income tax still has a rule, so that the resolver has
+     // something to say. It is not a layer that takes anything, and printing it
+     // as one is how "Texas (No State Income Tax)" ends up in a list of what
+     // the taxman takes.
+     const taking = layers.filter((l) => l.kind !== 'none');
+     const takesNone = layers.filter((l) => l.kind === 'none').map((l) => l.label.replace(/\s*\(.*\)$/, ''));
+     const salesRule = resolveRule(SALES_TAX_RULES, place.city.id, sim.now);
+     const propertyRule = resolveRule(PROPERTY_TAX_RULES, place.city.id, sim.now);
+
+     const ways: Way[] = [];
+     if (region) {
+       const towns = CITIES.childrenOf(region.id).length;
+       ways.push({
+         to: at('region', region.id),
+         label: spokenName(region.name),
+         detail: `The part of ${theCountry(place.countryName)} it’s in, with ${said(towns, 'town')} on the map`,
+       });
+     }
+     ways.push({
+       to: at('country', place.countryId),
+       label: place.countryName,
+       detail: 'Its languages, its money and which side of the road they drive on',
+     });
+     ways.push({
+       to: at('currency', place.currency.code),
+       label: place.currency.name || place.currency.code,
+       // Code first, then the symbol. A symbol is whatever the country writes —
+       // kr, zł, ₫ — and half of them start lowercase, which is wrong at the
+       // front of a line and not something to correct: it is their spelling.
+       detail: `${place.currency.code}, written ${place.currency.symbol}, and what a hundred US dollars comes to here`,
+     });
+     ways.push({
+       to: at('daylight', place.city.id),
+       label: 'Daylight',
+       detail: lightLine(place.sun, place.zone),
+     });
+     if (place.away && place.homeCity && placeOpens(place.homeCity)) {
+       ways.push({
+         to: at('place', place.homeCity.id),
+         label: spokenName(place.homeCity.name),
+         // Until 2026-10-13 a city the player stood in away from home said “Home, … back” here: none is.
+         detail: `Where you actually live, and it’s ${formatTime(sim.now, place.homeCity.timeZone)} there`,
+       });
+     }
+
+     return {
+       name: spokenName(place.city.name),
+       kind: isHome ? 'Where You Live' : 'A City On The Map',
+       parent: region ? at('region', region.id) : at('country', place.countryId),
+       summary: summaryOfPlace(place, isHome),
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <p className="small muted">
+             {label === 'Capital'
+               ? `It’s the capital of ${theCountry(place.countryName)}, ${people} people live here, and the climate is ${climate}.`
+               : label
+                 ? `It’s the ${label.toLowerCase()} of ${spokenName(region?.name ?? place.countryName)}, ${people} people live here, and the climate is ${climate}.`
+                 : `${people} people live here, in ${spokenName(region?.name ?? place.countryName)}, and the climate is ${climate}.`}
+           </p>
+           {/* Its tags as Home’s place line has them, a line of their own (from 2026-10-20, brief 17). From 2026-10-19 (brief
+               15’s coordinator, at the health and frame areas’ report) they were "In short: …", and before that "What it’s
+               known for: …", both a sentence a list of nouns and adjectives can’t make: "In short: production hub,
+               incentives and affordable." */}
+           {place.tags.length > 0 && <p className="small muted">{place.tags.map(titleCaseLabel).join(' · ')}</p>}
+           <p className="small muted">
+             {place.medianRentCents > 0 && `Rent on a one-bedroom runs about ${rent} a month, `}
+             {place.medianRentCents > 0
+               ? `and the cost of living sits at ${place.costOfLivingIndex}, where a hundred is the United States’ price level.`
+               : `The cost of living sits at ${place.costOfLivingIndex}, where a hundred is the United States’ price level.`}
+             {(() => { const figure = rentAt(place.city.id, 'USD'); return figure.kind === 'published' ? ` The rent is published: ${figure.measure}, ${figure.period}; source: ${figure.source}.` : ''; })()}
+             {layers.length === 0
+               ? ` The game has no income tax table for ${theCountry(place.countryName)}, so Tax On A Wage says Not On File rather than zero.`
+               : taking.length === 0
+                 ? ` No income tax comes out of a wage here, at any level.`
+                 : ` Income tax comes in ${said(taking.length, 'layer')} here: ${spokenList(taking.map((l) => l.label))}${takesNone.length > 0 ? `, and ${spokenList(takesNone)} ${takesNone.length === 1 ? 'adds' : 'add'} nothing on top` : ''}.`}
+           </p>
+           {/* Another city’s distance from the player’s. Until 2026-10-13 one they stood in said “You’re … from home in”:
+               none is. */}
+           {place.away && place.homeCity && (
+             <p className="small muted">
+               It’s {place.distanceFromHome} from home in{' '}
+               <Open subject={at('place', place.homeCity.id)}>{spokenName(place.homeCity.name)}</Open>, and{' '}
+               {clockAgainstHome(place.hoursFromHome)}.
+             </p>
+           )}
+           <div className="grid grid-3">
+             <Stat label="Local Time" value={place.localTime} note={place.zoneAbbreviation} />
+             <Stat
+               label="Daylight"
+               value={place.sun.polar === 'day' ? 'Midnight Sun' : place.sun.polar === 'night' ? 'Polar Night'
+                 : `${formatTime(place.sun.sunrise ?? sim.now, place.zone)} – ${formatTime(place.sun.sunset ?? sim.now, place.zone)}`}
+               note={`${formatDaylight(place.sun.daylightMinutes)} of daylight`}
+             />
+             <Stat
+               label="Currency"
+               value={`${place.currency.symbol} ${place.currency.code}`}
+               note={rateLine(place.currency)}
+             />
+             <Stat label="Cost Of Living" value={place.costOfLivingIndex} note="A hundred is the United States’ price level" />
+             <Stat
+               label="Tax On A Wage"
+               value={layers.length > 0 ? `${Math.round(place.effectiveIncomeTax * 100)}%` : 'Not On File'}
+               note={layers.length > 0 ? 'Income tax and payroll both, on a US$60,000 wage' : 'No tax table for this country'}
+             />
+             <Stat
+               label="Sales Tax"
+               value={salesRule ? `${(place.salesTax * 100).toFixed(1)}%` : 'Not On File'}
+               note={propertyRule ? `Property ${(place.propertyTax * 100).toFixed(2)}%` : 'Property tax not on file either'}
+             />
+             <Stat
+               label="Languages"
+               value={place.languages[0] ?? 'Not On File'}
+               note={spokenList(place.languages.slice(1)) || 'The only one listed'}
+             />
+           </div>
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways,
+       provenance: 'Its location, time zone and country are public record. '
+         + (rentAt(place.city.id, 'USD').kind === 'published'
+           ? 'Its rent is published, and its cost of living and tax rates are estimated.'
+           : rentAt(place.city.id, 'USD').kind === 'calibrated'
+             ? 'Its rent is estimated, scaled to published rents, and its cost of living and tax rates are estimated.'
+             : 'Its rent, cost of living and tax rates are estimated.'),
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ /**
+  * One sentence about standing here, or about not standing here. Home is where the player stands (`homeCityOf`); until
+  * 2026-10-13 this had a sentence for standing away from home, “You’re here and not home”, and one for home while away,
+  * “you’re not in it today”, which no life reached.
+  */
+ function summaryOfPlace(place: PlaceProfile, isHome: boolean): string {
+   if (isHome) {
+     return `This is where you live. It’s ${place.localTime}, and ${formatPeople(place.cityPopulation)} people live here.`;
+   }
+   if (!place.homeCity || !place.distanceFromHome) {
+     return `It’s ${place.localTime} there. You live somewhere else.`;
+   }
+   return `It’s ${place.localTime} there, ${place.distanceFromHome} from home.`;
+ }
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // The region above it
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ /** What a country calls its first-level pieces. The gazetteer knows the shape; this knows the word. */
+ const REGION_WORD: Record<string, string> = {
+   us: 'State', au: 'State', br: 'State', mx: 'State', in: 'State', de: 'State', ng: 'State', my: 'State', at: 'State',
+   ca: 'Province', cn: 'Province', za: 'Province', ar: 'Province', es: 'Province', kr: 'Province', ph: 'Province',
+   id: 'Province', pk: 'Province', th: 'Province', pl: 'Province', nl: 'Province', be: 'Province',
+   jp: 'Prefecture', ch: 'Canton', ie: 'County', uk: 'Nation',
+ };
+
+ const regionWord = (countryId: string): string => REGION_WORD[countryId] ?? 'Region';
+
+ /**
+  * How many first-level parts a country is divided into, said without the word.
+  *
+  * The gazetteer gives the United States fifty-one of them and Canada thirteen,
+  * because the District of Columbia is not a state and Nunavut is not a
+  * province. Counting them as states is a sentence that is wrong about the
+  * world, so the count is of parts and the word is kept for the one part the
+  * look is actually about. They were "pieces" the map "cuts" a country into
+  * until 2026-10-17 (brief 14).
+  */
+ const pieces = (countryId: string): string => said(REGIONS.childrenOf(countryId).length, 'part');
+
+ /**
+  * A capital, said the way a name is said.
+  *
+  * The country table and the city table are two different GeoNames files and
+  * they do not always agree on the accents — Reykjavik in one, Reykjavík in the
+  * other — so the city’s own spelling wins where the gazetteer can find it. It
+  * goes through the name gate either way, because a capital is a name.
+  */
+ function capitalName(country: Country): string {
+   const city = CITIES.byName(country.capital);
+   return spokenName(city?.countryId === country.id ? city.name : country.capital);
+ }
+
+ defineLook<Region>('region', {
+   gone: 'That region isn’t on the map.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => REGIONS.get(id || standingIn(sim)?.parentId || ''),
+   seeds: (sim) => {
+     const ids = [standingIn(sim)?.parentId, homeCityOf(sim)?.parentId];
+     return [...new Set(ids.filter((id): id is string => !!id && !!REGIONS.get(id)))];
+   },
+   look: (region, { sim }) => {
+     const country = COUNTRIES.get(region.parentId);
+     const countryName = country?.name ?? region.parentId.toUpperCase();
+     const word = regionWord(region.parentId);
+     const here = standingIn(sim);
+     const inIt = here?.parentId === region.id;
+     const towns = CITIES.childrenOf(region.id);
+     const named = towns.map((c) => spokenName(c.name));
+
+     // Read from a town inside it, not from where the player happens to be:
+     // California takes its own cut whether or not anybody is standing in it.
+     const sample = inIt && here ? here : [...towns].sort((a, b) => b.population - a.population)[0];
+     const layer = sample
+       ? resolveIncomeTaxLayers(sample.id, sim.now).find((l) => l.jurisdictionCode === region.jurisdictionCode)
+       : undefined;
+
+     const ways: Way[] = [{
+       to: at('country', region.parentId),
+       label: countryName,
+       // Only the one you came in through if you are actually in it. Read from
+       // a state on the other side of the country, that is somebody else’s.
+       detail: inIt
+         ? `The country it’s in, which the map divides into ${pieces(region.parentId)}, and you’re in this one`
+         : `The country it’s in, which the map divides into ${pieces(region.parentId)}`,
+     }];
+     for (const town of orderedTowns(towns, here?.id)) {
+       ways.push({
+         to: at('place', town.id),
+         label: spokenName(town.name),
+         detail: `${formatPeople(town.population)} people${placeKindLabel(town) ? `, and the ${placeKindLabel(town)!.toLowerCase()}` : ''}`,
+       });
+     }
+
+     return {
+       name: spokenName(region.name),
+       kind: `The ${word}`,
+       parent: at('country', region.parentId),
+       summary: inIt && here
+         ? `You’re in it, in ${spokenName(here.name)}, ${towns.length === 1 ? 'its only place' : `one of its ${said(towns.length, 'place')}`} on the map.`
+         : towns.length > 0
+           ? `Part of ${theCountry(countryName)}, with ${said(towns.length, 'place')} on the map. You’re in none of them.`
+           : `Part of ${theCountry(countryName)}, and none of its towns are on your map yet.`,
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <p className="small muted">
+             {towns.length > 0
+               ? `It’s one of the ${pieces(region.parentId)} the map divides ${theCountry(countryName)} into. ${named.length === 1 ? `Its one town on your map is ${named[0]}` : `Its towns on your map are ${spokenSome(named, 6)}`}.`
+               : `It’s one of the ${pieces(region.parentId)} the map divides ${theCountry(countryName)} into. A country’s towns show up once your life has a place in it.`}
+           </p>
+           {sample && (
+             <p className="small muted">
+               {layer && layer.kind !== 'none'
+                 ? `Income tax here isn’t only the country’s: ${layer.label} is added on top of it.`
+                 : `The ${word.toLowerCase()} adds no income tax of its own.`}
+             </p>
+           )}
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways,
+       provenance: `The ${word.toLowerCase()} and its towns come from a public gazetteer. A country’s towns show up once your life has a place in it.`,
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ /** The town you are standing in first, then the biggest, capped at four. */
+ function orderedTowns(towns: readonly City[], hereId: string | undefined): City[] {
+   const sorted = [...towns].sort((a, b) => b.population - a.population);
+   const here = sorted.find((c) => c.id === hereId);
+   const rest = sorted.filter((c) => c.id !== hereId);
+   return (here ? [here, ...rest] : rest).slice(0, 4);
+ }
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // The country above that
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ defineLook<Country>('country', {
+   gone: 'That country isn’t on the map.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => COUNTRIES.get(id || standingIn(sim)?.countryId || ''),
+   seeds: (sim) => {
+     const ids = [standingIn(sim)?.countryId, homeCityOf(sim)?.countryId];
+     return [...new Set(ids.filter((id): id is string => !!id))];
+   },
+   look: (country, { sim }) => {
+     const here = standingIn(sim);
+     const inIt = here?.countryId === country.id;
+     const languages = languageNames(country.languages ?? '');
+     const money = titleCaseLabel(country.currencyName || country.currency);
+     const capital = CITIES.byName(country.capital);
+     const capitalHere = capital?.countryId === country.id ? capital : undefined;
+     const region = inIt && here ? REGIONS.get(here.parentId) : undefined;
+
+     const ways: Way[] = [{
+       to: at('currency', country.currency),
+       label: money,
+       detail: `What everything in ${theCountry(country.name)} is priced in`,
+     }];
+     if (region) {
+       ways.push({
+         to: at('region', region.id),
+         label: spokenName(region.name),
+         detail: `The ${regionWord(country.id).toLowerCase()} you’re in, one of its ${pieces(country.id)}`,
+       });
+     }
+     if (capitalHere && capitalHere.id !== here?.id && placeOpens(capitalHere)) {
+       ways.push({
+         to: at('place', capitalHere.id),
+         label: spokenName(capitalHere.name),
+         detail: `The capital, ${formatPeople(capitalHere.population)} people`,
+       });
+     }
+
+     return {
+       name: country.name,
+       kind: 'The Country',
+       summary: inIt
+         ? `You’re in ${theCountry(country.name)}, a country of ${formatPeople(country.population)} people, and its money is the ${money.toLowerCase()}.`
+         : `A country in ${country.continent}, with ${formatPeople(country.population)} people. You’re in ${here ? spokenName(here.name) : 'another country'}.`,
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <p className="small muted">
+             {country.capital ? `The capital is ${capitalName(country)}. ` : ''}
+             {`The country is in ${country.continent}, with ${formatPeople(country.population)} people across `}
+             {`${country.areaKm2.toLocaleString('en-US')} square kilometers.`}
+           </p>
+           <p className="small muted">
+             {`They drive on the ${country.drivesOn}, measure distance in ${usesMiles(country.id) ? 'miles' : 'kilometers'} and read the temperature in ${usesFahrenheit(country.id) ? 'Fahrenheit' : 'Celsius'}.`}
+             {languages.length > 0 && ` ${spokenList(languages)} ${isAre(languages.length)} spoken${languages.length > 1 ? ', in the order the country lists them' : ''}.`}
+           </p>
+           <div className="grid grid-3">
+             <Stat label="Capital" value={country.capital ? capitalName(country) : 'Not On File'} note={country.continent} />
+             <Stat label="People" value={formatPeople(country.population)} note={`${country.areaKm2.toLocaleString('en-US')} sq km`} />
+             <Stat label="Money" value={`${currencyInfo(country.currency).symbol} ${country.currency}`} note={money} />
+             <Stat label="Languages" value={languages[0] ?? 'Not On File'} note={spokenList(languages.slice(1)) || 'The only one listed'} />
+             <Stat label="Calling Code" value={country.phone ? `+${country.phone.replace(/^\+/, '')}` : 'Not On File'} note="Dialed from outside" />
+             <Stat label="Drives On" value={titleCaseLabel(country.drivesOn)} note={usesMiles(country.id) ? 'Miles on the signs' : 'Kilometers on the signs'} />
+           </div>
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways,
+       provenance: 'These facts come from a public gazetteer.',
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // The money
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ interface TheMoney {
+   info: CurrencyInfo;
+   name: string;
+   users: Country[];
+   /** The country whose money this is, from where the player is standing. */
+   home?: Country;
+ }
+
+ defineLook<TheMoney>('currency', {
+   gone: 'No country on the map uses that currency.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => {
+     const here = standingIn(sim);
+     const country = COUNTRIES.get(here?.countryId ?? '');
+     const code = (id || country?.currency || '').toUpperCase();
+     if (!code) return undefined;
+     const users = COUNTRIES.all().filter((c) => c.currency === code);
+     if (users.length === 0) return undefined;
+     const home = country?.currency === code ? country : undefined;
+     const named = home?.currencyName || users.find((c) => c.currencyName)?.currencyName || code;
+     return { info: currencyInfo(code), name: titleCaseLabel(named), users, home };
+   },
+   seeds: (sim) => {
+     const codes = [
+       COUNTRIES.get(standingIn(sim)?.countryId ?? '')?.currency,
+       COUNTRIES.get(homeCityOf(sim)?.countryId ?? '')?.currency,
+     ];
+     return [...new Set(codes.filter((c): c is string => !!c))];
+   },
+   look: (money, { sim }) => {
+     const here = standingIn(sim);
+     const place = profileFor(sim, here);
+     const hundred = formatLocal(100_00, money.info.code);
+     const users = money.users.map((c) => c.name.trim());
+
+     const ways: Way[] = money.users
+       .slice()
+       .sort((a, b) => (a.id === money.home?.id ? -1 : b.id === money.home?.id ? 1 : b.population - a.population))
+       .slice(0, 3)
+       .map((c) => ({
+         to: at('country', c.id),
+         label: c.name,
+         detail: c.population > 0
+           ? `${formatPeople(c.population)} people${c.capital ? `, with its capital at ${capitalName(c)}` : ''}`
+           : 'Nobody lives there',
+       }));
+
+     return {
+       name: money.name,
+       kind: 'The Money',
+       parent: money.home ? at('country', money.home.id) : undefined,
+       summary: money.home
+         ? `The ${money.name.toLowerCase()} is the money here, written ${money.info.symbol}. ${money.info.code === 'USD' ? 'Every exchange rate is quoted against it.' : money.info.unitsPerUsd === undefined ? 'The game has no exchange rate for it.' : `It’s about ${money.info.unitsPerUsd.toLocaleString('en-US')} to the US dollar, estimated.`}`
+         : `The money of ${spokenSome(users, 4)}. You’re not in ${users.length === 1 ? 'it' : 'any of them'}.`,
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <p className="small muted">
+             {money.info.code === 'USD'
+               ? 'Every exchange rate in the game is quoted against the US dollar, so every conversion goes through it.'
+               : hundred
+                 ? `A hundred US dollars is ${hundred} ${money.home ? 'here' : 'there'}.`
+                 : 'The game has no exchange rate for it, so nothing is converted into it, and a life started here keeps its money in euros.'}
+             {money.info.decimals === 0
+               ? ' It has no smaller unit, so prices in it are whole numbers.'
+               : ' Prices in it are written to two decimal places.'}
+             {money.info.symbolAfter
+               ? ' Its symbol goes after the number.'
+               : ' Its symbol goes before the number.'}
+           </p>
+           <p className="small muted">
+             {`It’s used in ${spokenSome(users, 4)}.`}
+             {place && place.currency.code === money.info.code && place.localRent
+               && ` A one-bedroom in ${spokenName(place.city.name)} is about ${place.localRent} a month.`}
+           </p>
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways,
+       provenance: RATES_NOTE,
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // The light
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ interface TheLight {
+   city: City;
+   today: SunTimes;
+   tomorrow: SunTimes;
+   midsummer: SunTimes;
+   midwinter: SunTimes;
+ }
+
+ defineLook<TheLight>('daylight', {
+   gone: 'That place isn’t on the map, so its daylight can’t be shown.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => {
+     const city = cityFor(sim, id);
+     if (!city) return undefined;
+     const { latitude: lat, longitude: lon, timeZone: zone } = city;
+     const year = zonedParts(sim.now, zone).year;
+     return {
+       city,
+       today: sunTimes(sim.now, lat, lon, zone),
+       tomorrow: sunTimes(addDays(sim.now, 1, zone), lat, lon, zone),
+       midsummer: sunTimes(Date.UTC(year, lat >= 0 ? 5 : 11, 21, 12), lat, lon, zone),
+       midwinter: sunTimes(Date.UTC(year, lat >= 0 ? 11 : 5, 21, 12), lat, lon, zone),
+     };
+   },
+   seeds: (sim) => {
+     const ids = [standingIn(sim)?.id, homeCityOf(sim)?.id];
+     return [...new Set(ids.filter((id): id is string => !!id))];
+   },
+   look: (light, { sim }) => {
+     const { city, today, tomorrow, midsummer, midwinter } = light;
+     const swing = today.polar || tomorrow.polar
+       ? 0
+       : Math.round(tomorrow.daylightMinutes - today.daylightMinutes);
+     const north = city.latitude >= 0;
+     const degrees = Math.abs(Math.round(city.latitude));
+
+     return {
+       name: 'Daylight',
+       kind: 'The Light Today',
+       // The light falls on a city whether or not the tax tables can reach it,
+       // so the parent is declared only where it would open.
+       parent: placeOpens(city) ? at('place', city.id) : undefined,
+       summary: today.polar === 'day'
+         ? 'The sun doesn’t set here today, so it’s light all day and all night.'
+         : today.polar === 'night'
+           ? 'The sun doesn’t rise here today.'
+           : `Daylight runs from ${formatTime(today.sunrise ?? 0, city.timeZone)} to ${formatTime(today.sunset ?? 0, city.timeZone)} today, ${formatDurationWords(today.daylightMinutes * MS_MINUTE)}, and ${swingLine(swing)}.`,
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <p className="small muted">
+             {`${spokenName(city.name)} is at ${degrees}° ${north ? 'north' : 'south'}, ${latitudeLine(city.latitude)}`}
+           </p>
+           <p className="small muted">{yearLine(midsummer, midwinter)}</p>
+           <div className="grid grid-3">
+             <Stat
+               label="Sunrise"
+               value={today.polar ? 'None Today' : formatTime(today.sunrise ?? 0, city.timeZone)}
+               note={today.polar === 'day' ? 'It doesn’t get dark' : today.polar === 'night' ? 'It stays below the horizon' : 'Local time'}
+             />
+             <Stat
+               label="Sunset"
+               value={today.polar ? 'None Today' : formatTime(today.sunset ?? 0, city.timeZone)}
+               note={today.polar ? 'The sun doesn’t cross the horizon' : 'Local time'}
+             />
+             <Stat
+               label="Length"
+               value={today.polar === 'day' ? 'All Of It' : today.polar === 'night' ? 'None Of It' : formatDaylight(today.daylightMinutes)}
+               note={swing === 0 ? 'Barely changing' : `${swing > 0 ? 'Gaining' : 'Losing'} ${plural(Math.abs(swing), 'minute')} a day`}
+             />
+             <Stat
+               label="Longest Day"
+               value={midsummer.polar === 'day' ? 'All Of It' : formatDaylight(midsummer.daylightMinutes)}
+               note={north ? 'At the June solstice' : 'At the December solstice'}
+             />
+             <Stat
+               label="Shortest Day"
+               value={midwinter.polar === 'night' ? 'None Of It' : formatDaylight(midwinter.daylightMinutes)}
+               note={north ? 'At the December solstice' : 'At the June solstice'}
+             />
+             <Stat label="Time Zone" value={zoneAbbreviation(sim.now, city.timeZone)} note="The local time zone" />
+           </div>
+         </>
+       ),
+       provenance: 'Calculated from the Earth’s tilt, the day of the year and this latitude, as an almanac does, and good to a minute or two.',
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ /** How fast the day is growing or shrinking, in the words you would use. */
+ function swingLine(minutes: number): string {
+   if (minutes === 0) return 'the days are barely changing in length';
+   const size = Math.abs(minutes);
+   return `the days are getting about ${said(size, 'minute')} ${minutes > 0 ? 'longer' : 'shorter'} each day`;
+ }
+
+ /** What this latitude does to a year, said plainly. */
+ function latitudeLine(latitude: number): string {
+   const size = Math.abs(latitude);
+   const circle = latitude >= 0 ? 'Arctic Circle' : 'Antarctic Circle';
+   if (size >= 66.5) return `inside the ${circle}, where for part of the year the sun doesn’t set, and for part of it, it doesn’t rise.`;
+   if (size >= 58) return `just short of the ${circle}, so the days are very long in summer and very short in winter.`;
+   if (size >= 45) return 'far enough from the equator that winter afternoons end early and summer evenings run late.';
+   if (size >= 23.5) return 'in the middle latitudes, where the length of the day changes by a few hours over the year.';
+   return 'close enough to the equator that the day is about twelve hours long all year.';
+ }
+
+ /** The two ends of the year, from the same geometry. */
+ function yearLine(midsummer: SunTimes, midwinter: SunTimes): string {
+   const long = midsummer.polar === 'day' ? 'the sun doesn’t set at all' : `there’s ${formatDaylight(midsummer.daylightMinutes)} of daylight`;
+   const short = midwinter.polar === 'night' ? 'it doesn’t rise at all' : `there’s ${formatDaylight(midwinter.daylightMinutes)}`;
+   return `On the longest day of the year ${long}, and on the shortest, ${short}.`;
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — the things you put on your own calendar, opened.
+  *
+  * A plan is a commitment somebody made on purpose, and everything about it is
+  * a thing in the world: the hours it takes, the sky over those hours, the day
+  * it sits in, the place it wants you, the thing it collides with. This is the
+  * half of that chain the calendar could not reach before — the run of hours
+  * itself, and the set of everything you have decided to do.
+  *
+  * Nothing here invents anything. The hours come off the same curve the
+  * weather reads, the collisions off the same detector the calendar draws, and
+  * a plan that was called off says so rather than disappearing.
+  */
+
+ import { CITIES, type City } from '@/engine/content/geography';
+ import { MS_MINUTE, dateKey, formatDate, formatRelativeWords, formatTime, startOfDay, startOfNextDay } from '@/engine/core/time';
+ import { entriesBetween, upcoming, type CalendarEntry } from '@/engine/world/calendar';
+ import { PLAN_KIND } from '@/engine/world/plans';
+ import { hoursOn, type HourWeather } from '@/engine/systems/weather';
+ import type { Simulation } from '@/engine';
+ import { Stat } from '@/ui/components/primitives';
+ import { clockWord } from './weather';
+ import { defineLook } from './registry';
+ import { at } from './subject';
+ import { isAre, said, spokenList, toStart } from './words';
+
+ /** How far out the calendar is asked about when gathering what you planned. */
+ const AHEAD_DAYS = 365;
+
+ const cityOf = (entry: CalendarEntry, sim: Simulation): City | undefined =>
+   CITIES.get(entry.locationId ?? sim.player.currentLocationId);
+
+ const endOf = (entry: CalendarEntry): number =>
+   entry.endsAt ?? entry.at + (entry.durationMinutes ?? 60) * MS_MINUTE;
+
+ /** The title as a name: trimmed, and never carrying its own punctuation. */
+ const asName = (title: string): string =>
+   title.replace(/\s*\/\s*/g, ' and ').replace(/[.?!]+$/, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim()
+     .replace(/\b\w/g, (c) => c.toUpperCase());
+
+ /** Everything on the calendar the player put there. */
+ function plansOf(sim: Simulation): { pending: CalendarEntry[]; settled: CalendarEntry[] } {
+   const window = entriesBetween(sim, sim.now - AHEAD_DAYS * 86_400_000, sim.now + AHEAD_DAYS * 86_400_000);
+   const mine = window.filter((entry) => sim.timeline.get(entry.id)?.kind === PLAN_KIND);
+   return {
+     pending: mine.filter((e) => e.status === 'pending'),
+     settled: mine.filter((e) => e.status !== 'pending'),
+   };
+ }
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // The hours a commitment takes
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ interface Stretch {
+   entry: CalendarEntry;
+   city: City | undefined;
+   hours: HourWeather[];
+   minutes: number;
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * Every whole hour the window touches, from the hour it starts in.
+  *
+  * An hour runs until the next one on the clock begins, or until the day ends.
+  * On the day the clocks go back the hour they repeat is listed once and runs
+  * twice as long; taken as sixty minutes, a plan in its second run touched no
+  * hour at all, and its stretch said the hours were free again.
+  */
+ function hoursAcross(sim: Simulation, entry: CalendarEntry, city: City | undefined): HourWeather[] {
+   if (!city) return [];
+   const from = startOfDay(entry.at, city.timeZone);
+   const finish = endOf(entry);
+   const hours = hoursOn(sim, city.id, from);
+   const endOfHour = (i: number) => hours[i + 1]?.at ?? startOfNextDay(from, city.timeZone);
+   return hours.filter((hour, i) => hour.at < finish && endOfHour(i) > entry.at);
+ }
+
+ defineLook<Stretch>('stretch', {
+   gone: 'Those hours are free again.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => {
+     const item = sim.timeline.get(id);
+     if (!item) return undefined;
+     const start = startOfDay(item.at, sim.homeZone);
+     const entry = entriesBetween(sim, start, start + 2 * 86_400_000).find((e) => e.id === id);
+     if (!entry) return undefined;
+     const city = cityOf(entry, sim);
+     const hours = hoursAcross(sim, entry, city);
+     if (hours.length === 0) return undefined;
+     return { entry, city, hours, minutes: Math.round((endOf(entry) - entry.at) / MS_MINUTE) };
+   },
+   seeds: (sim) => upcoming(sim, 6).map((entry) => entry.id),
+   look: ({ entry, city, hours, minutes }, { sim }) => {
+     const zone = city?.timeZone ?? sim.homeZone;
+     const first = hours[0]!;
+     const last = hours[hours.length - 1]!;
+     const dark = hours.filter((h) => !h.daylight);
+     const wet = hours.filter((h) => h.wet);
+     const unit = first.fahrenheit ? '°F' : '°C';
+     const cold = hours.reduce((a, b) => (b.temperature < a.temperature ? b : a));
+     const warm = hours.reduce((a, b) => (b.temperature > a.temperature ? b : a));
+
+     return {
+       name: `${formatTime(entry.at, zone)} To ${formatTime(endOf(entry), zone)}`,
+       kind: 'Its Hours',
+       parent: at('entry', entry.id),
+       summary: `It runs from ${formatTime(entry.at, zone)} to ${formatTime(endOf(entry), zone)}, `
+         + `${said(Math.round(minutes / 60), 'hour')} on ${formatDate(entry.at, zone)}, `
+         + `at ${cold.temperature === warm.temperature
+           ? `${cold.temperature}${unit} throughout`
+           : `${cold.temperature}${unit} to ${warm.temperature}${unit}`}.`,
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <p className="small">
+             {dark.length === 0
+               ? 'The sun is up for all of it.'
+               : dark.length === hours.length
+                 ? 'All of it is after dark.'
+                 : `${toStart(said(dark.length, 'hour'))} of it ${isAre(dark.length)} after dark.`}
+             {' '}
+             {wet.length === 0
+               ? 'It stays dry the whole way through.'
+               : `There’s ${spokenList([...new Set(wet.map((h) => h.condition.toLowerCase()))])} for `
+                 + `${said(wet.length, 'hour')} of it.`}
+           </p>
+           <div className="grid grid-3">
+             <Stat label="Starts" value={formatTime(entry.at, zone)} note={formatDate(entry.at, zone)} />
+             <Stat label="Ends" value={formatTime(endOf(entry), zone)} note={said(hours.length, 'hour')} />
+             <Stat
+               label="Coldest Hour"
+               value={`${cold.temperature}${unit}`}
+               note={clockWord(cold.hour)}
+             />
+           </div>
+         </>
+       ),
+       waysAs: 'strip',
+       ways: hours.map((hour) => ({
+         to: at('skyhour', `${hour.cityId}/${hour.dateKey}/${hour.hour}`),
+         label: clockWord(hour.hour),
+         detail: `${hour.temperature}${unit}, ${hour.condition.toLowerCase()}${hour.daylight ? '' : ', after dark'}`,
+         glance: { icon: undefined, lines: [`${hour.temperature}°`, hour.daylight ? 'Light' : 'Dark'] },
+       })),
+       provenance: `${first.hour === last.hour ? 'The hour is' : 'Each hour is'} estimated from the day’s forecast.`,
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // Everything you decided to do
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ interface Plans { pending: CalendarEntry[]; settled: CalendarEntry[] }
+
+ defineLook<Plans>('plans', {
+   gone: 'There’s no calendar to have put anything on.',
+   resolve: (sim) => plansOf(sim),
+   seeds: () => [''],
+   look: ({ pending, settled }, { sim }) => {
+     const zone = sim.homeZone;
+     const next = pending[0];
+     const called = settled.filter((e) => e.status === 'cancelled');
+     const missed = settled.filter((e) => e.status === 'missed');
+
+     return {
+       name: 'Your Own Plans',
+       kind: 'What You Put On The Calendar',
+       parent: at('person', sim.universe.playerId),
+       summary: pending.length === 0
+         ? 'You haven’t put anything on the calendar yourself, so everything on it was put there for you.'
+         : `You’ve put ${said(pending.length, 'thing')} on the calendar yourself. `
+           + `The next is ${formatRelativeWords(next!.at, sim.now)}.`,
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <p className="small">
+             {pending.length === 0
+               ? 'A plan of your own needs a name, a start time and a length, and it’s in the city you’re in when you make it.'
+               : `${asName(next!.title)} is the next one, ${formatDate(next!.at, zone)} at ${formatTime(next!.at, zone)}.`}
+             {missed.length > 0 && ` ${toStart(said(missed.length, 'plan'))} ${missed.length === 1 ? 'has' : 'have'} gone by without you.`}
+             {called.length > 0 && ` ${toStart(said(called.length, 'plan'))} ${called.length === 1 ? 'was' : 'were'} called off.`}
+           </p>
+           <div className="grid grid-3">
+             <Stat label="Waiting" value={pending.length} note="Still ahead of you" />
+             <Stat label="Called Off" value={called.length} note="You called them off" />
+             <Stat label="Gone By" value={missed.length} note="You weren’t there" />
+           </div>
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways: pending.slice(0, 10).map((entry) => ({
+         to: at('entry', entry.id),
+         label: asName(entry.title),
+         detail: `${formatRelativeWords(entry.at, sim.now)}, ${formatDate(entry.at, zone)} at ${formatTime(entry.at, zone)}`,
+       })),
+       // The clash by the chip’s own word (from 2026-10-20, brief 17): until then "and a clash is marked".
+       provenance: 'Your plans are ordinary calendar items: the clock stops at them, and two at once are marked Clash.',
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ /** The day key an entry falls on, for anything wiring a way to its day. */
+ export const dayOfEntry = (entry: CalendarEntry, zone: string): string => dateKey(entry.at, zone);
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — what a kind of thing opens into, declared once.
+  *
+  * A screen names a subject; it never writes a body. The body is declared here,
+  * per kind, so the same calendar entry opens the same way on Home, on the
+  * Calendar, and from a notification about it. Openability belongs to the
+  * thing, not to the screen that happens to be printing it.
+  *
+  * The shape of a declaration is data, not markup, wherever it can be: `ways`
+  * is an array of addresses rather than JSX, which is what lets a test crawl
+  * the whole graph and prove every way in opens onto something. A body may
+  * still be markup — some things are best said in a paragraph — but the edges
+  * are never buried inside it.
+  */
+
+ import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
+ import type { Simulation } from '@/engine';
+ import type { Subject } from './subject';
+
+ /** A way further in. `detail` says what is behind it before you take it. */
+ export interface Way {
+   to: Subject;
+   label: string;
+   detail: string;
+   /**
+    * What the cell shows when the ways are laid out as a strip.
+    *
+    * The edges stay data either way — this says how one is drawn, not where it
+    * goes — so the crawl still walks the whole graph. A picture is always
+    * beside the word and never instead of it, and it is hidden from a screen
+    * reader, which has the word and the lines.
+    */
+   glance?: {
+     icon?: string;
+     lines?: readonly string[];
+     /**
+      * Whether this cell is the one the level is about.
+      *
+      * A strip of seven bands with no mark on the one you are standing in is a
+      * chart of somebody else’s life: the sentence said which rung you were on
+      * and the picture did not, so the eye had to go back to the prose to find
+      * out. Marked cells still open like any other.
+      */
+     marked?: boolean;
+   };
+ }
+
+ /** Another face of the same thing. Costs no depth and has no address. */
+ export interface Facet {
+   id: string;
+   label: string;
+   body: ReactNode;
+   ways?: readonly Way[];
+ }
+
+ /** What a look says about its subject. */
+ export interface Looked {
+   /** The world’s word for it, Title Case. The only string a trail prints. */
+   name: string;
+   /** What kind of thing this is, in the world’s words: 'The Day', 'One Of Nine'. */
+   kind: string;
+   /** One sentence, second person, present tense, true at this instant. */
+   summary: string;
+   /** What this hangs beneath, for the trail and for where it opens. */
+   parent?: Subject;
+   body?: ReactNode;
+   facets?: readonly Facet[];
+   ways?: readonly Way[];
+   /**
+    * How the ways are laid out.
+    *
+    * A list by default: a name and a line saying what is behind it. A strip
+    * goes across the way a week of weather does on Home — a name, a picture
+    * and the figures under it — for a set whose members are a sequence and
+    * whose whole point is being compared side by side.
+    */
+   waysAs?: 'list' | 'strip';
+   /** One footnote line. Never a level, never openable. */
+   provenance?: string;
+ }
+
+ export interface LookView<T> {
+   /** Read from the live world every time. undefined means it is not there. */
+   resolve(sim: Simulation, id: string): T | undefined;
+   /** What the world says when it is not there. A sentence, in voice. */
+   gone: string;
+   look(subject: T, ctx: { sim: Simulation; id: string }): Looked;
+   /**
+    * Ids worth crawling in a test, for a kind whose ids are not enumerable
+    * from the save alone. A dial cannot be discovered by reading a universe;
+    * it has to say what its nine are.
+    */
+   seeds?(sim: Simulation): readonly string[];
+ }
+
+ const REGISTRY = new Map<string, LookView<unknown>>();
+
+ /**
+  * Whether the module graph is being swapped under a running page.
+  *
+  * Two declarations of one kind is a real mistake and throwing on it is right —
+  * but a hot reload re-runs a declaration file, which is the same call a second
+  * time and not a mistake at all. Left throwing, every save of a look file took
+  * the registry down and the page with it: the first drill through Home
+  * recorded five of them. In dev the later declaration wins, which is what
+  * "reload this file" means; in a build there is no `hot` and the guard stands.
+  */
+ const swapping = (): boolean =>
+   typeof import.meta !== 'undefined' && Boolean((import.meta as { hot?: unknown }).hot);
+
+ export function defineLook<T>(kind: string, view: LookView<T>): void {
+   if (REGISTRY.has(kind) && !swapping()) throw new Error(`Two declarations for the same kind: ${kind}`);
+   REGISTRY.set(kind, view as LookView<unknown>);
+ }
+
+ /** Every registered kind. The crawl and the coverage matrix read this. */
+ export function lookKinds(): string[] {
+   return [...REGISTRY.keys()].sort();
+ }
+
+ export function hasKind(kind: string): boolean {
+   return REGISTRY.has(kind);
+ }
+
+ /** The ids of a kind worth crawling, where the kind can say. */
+ export function seedsFor(kind: string, sim: Simulation): readonly string[] {
+   return REGISTRY.get(kind)?.seeds?.(sim) ?? [];
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * What is behind a subject right now, or nothing.
+  *
+  * Returns `gone` rather than throwing when the subject has left the world: a
+  * person who moved out, an account that closed, a day that passed. The screen
+  * says what became of it in the world’s own words instead of blanking.
+  */
+ export function resolveLook(sim: Simulation, subject: Subject): Looked | { gone: string } | undefined {
+   const view = REGISTRY.get(subject.kind);
+   if (!view) return undefined;
+   const found = view.resolve(sim, subject.id);
+   if (found === undefined) return { gone: view.gone };
+   return view.look(found, { sim, id: subject.id });
+ }
+
+ /** Whether a subject would open onto anything. A name is not painted as a way in unless it would. */
+ export function lookExists(sim: Simulation, subject: Subject): boolean {
+   const view = REGISTRY.get(subject.kind);
+   if (!view) return false;
+   return view.resolve(sim, subject.id) !== undefined;
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * The chain of names from the outermost thing down to this one.
+  *
+  * Walked from `parent` rather than replayed from clicks, so arriving at the
+  * stress dial from Home and arriving at it from inside yourself give the same
+  * trail. Stops at twelve, which no real chain reaches, so a view that
+  * accidentally parents itself fails loudly here instead of hanging.
+  */
+ export function trailTo(sim: Simulation, subject: Subject): { subject: Subject; name: string }[] {
+   const chain: { subject: Subject; name: string }[] = [];
+   const seen = new Set<string>();
+   let current: Subject | undefined = subject;
+   for (let guard = 0; current && guard < 12; guard++) {
+     const key = `${current.kind}:${current.id}`;
+     if (seen.has(key)) throw new Error(`A look parents itself: ${key}`);
+     seen.add(key);
+     const found: Looked | { gone: string } | undefined = resolveLook(sim, current);
+     if (!found || 'gone' in found) break;
+     chain.unshift({ subject: current, name: found.name });
+     current = found.parent;
+   }
+   return chain;
+ }
+
+ /** Only for tests: forget every declaration. */
+ export function resetLooks(): void {
+   REGISTRY.clear();
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — the school, its courses, and the skills they train.
+  *
+  * The School screen names a school, a year’s courses and twenty-one skills,
+  * and until 2026-10-02 none of them opened. They are things: the school is a
+  * real one in a real town, each course is the Bulletin’s with its own code
+  * and teachers, and each skill is a number the classes grow and the chair
+  * casts by. So the school opens into the year’s courses and the town; a course
+  * into the skills it trains and the next day it meets; a skill into where you
+  * stand in it against the class and every course that trains it.
+  *
+  * Every figure is the school system’s own (`systems/school.ts`): the craft,
+  * the reach the ceiling allows, the class’s best and middle, and your place.
+  */
+
+ import { dateKey, formatDate, instantFromZoned, zonedParts } from '@/engine/core/time';
+ import { CITIES } from '@/engine/content/geography';
+ import { COURSES, LEAVE_RULES, SKILLS, YALE_DRAMA, type Course, type Skill } from '@/engine/content/school';
+ import {
+   STANDING_LABEL, ceilingOf, coursesFor, meanCraft, nextClasses, rankIn, termLabel, termOf, termStart, yearOfStudy,
+   schoolEnded, type SchoolRecord,
+ } from '@/engine/systems/school';
+ import type { Person } from '@/engine/domain/model';
+ import { MASTERED, TECHNIQUES } from '@/engine/content/abilities';
+ import { templateById, type PrepDim } from '@/engine/content/coursework';
+ import { BAND_LABEL, assignmentById, courseworkOf, preparedParts, weightsOf, type Assignment } from '@/engine/systems/coursework';
+ import type { Simulation } from '@/engine';
+ import { Stat } from '@/ui/components/primitives';
+ import { defineLook, lookExists, type Way } from './registry';
+ import { at } from './subject';
+ import { said, spokenList } from './words';
+
+ const YEAR_WORD = ['', 'First', 'Second', 'Third'] as const;
+ /**
+  * A standing still at the School, as the school look’s sentence says it (from 2026-10-12): until then the sentence
+  * put “standing” after the label, which ends in it already, so good standing was said with the word twice, and a
+  * warning as “in academic warning standing”.
+  */
+ const STANDING_SAID: Readonly<Record<'good' | 'concern' | 'warning', string>> = { good: 'in good standing', concern: 'with a notice of academic concern', warning: 'on academic warning' };
+ const schoolZone = () => CITIES.require(YALE_DRAMA.cityId).timeZone;
+ const skillLabel = (id: Skill) => SKILLS.find((s) => s.id === id)?.label ?? id;
+ const median = (xs: number[]) => { const s = [...xs].sort((a, b) => a - b); return s[Math.floor(s.length / 2)] ?? 0; };
+
+ /** The player, while they have a school and a craft to read. */
+ function student(sim: Simulation): Person | undefined {
+   const person = sim.universe.people[sim.universe.playerId];
+   return person?.school && person.craft ? person : undefined;
+ }
+
+ /** "3rd", for a place in the class. */
+ function ordinal(n: number): string {
+   const tens = n % 100;
+   if (tens >= 11 && tens <= 13) return `${n}th`;
+   return `${n}${n % 10 === 1 ? 'st' : n % 10 === 2 ? 'nd' : n % 10 === 3 ? 'rd' : 'th'}`;
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * The calendar term a moment falls in, by New Haven’s calendar, past the program’s sixth too. Until 2026-10-12 it was
+  * capped at the sixth, so a third-year fall after a leave or a repeated year was named as the spring before it, and
+  * read that spring’s courses.
+  */
+ function termNow(sim: Simulation): number {
+   const p = zonedParts(sim.now, schoolZone());
+   return termOf({ year: p.year, month: p.month, day: p.day });
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * The courses a student takes in a calendar term (from 2026-10-12): none on a leave, an additional term’s retaken
+  * ones in it, and otherwise their program year’s for the season. Until then the looks took a year’s courses on a
+  * leave, as `nextClasses` doesn’t, and none in an additional term, whose year of study reads past the third.
+  */
+ function takenIn(school: SchoolRecord, year: number, term: number): Course[] {
+   if (school.leave?.status === 'on') return [];
+   const extra = school.extra;
+   if (extra && extra.term === term) return COURSES.filter((c) => extra.courses.some((x) => x.code === c.code));
+   const season = termStart(term).fall ? 'fall' : 'spring';
+   return COURSES.filter((c) => c.year === year && c.terms.includes(season));
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * The program’s terms begun, for Terms Begun (from 2026-10-12): the calendar’s less those a leave or a repeated year
+  * took, as `yearOfStudy` counts them. Before that it was the calendar’s, which a leave carried to eight of six. On a
+  * leave, or with the School left during one, it’s the program’s terms before the term the leave began in, which is
+  * taken again on return: `startLeave` adds the whole leave to the offset as it begins, while `termsBegun` follows the
+  * calendar only to that term. Until a second reading the same day, a leave read short by all but one of its terms for
+  * the whole of it, a two-term leave one short (measured: back from the first year and on leave from the second fall,
+  * 1 of 6 with two terms passed, and still 1 once withdrawn), and a leave from the first term read 0 only because the
+  * figure was clamped at 0; nothing needs the clamp now.
+  */
+ function programTermsBegun(school: SchoolRecord): number {
+   const away = school.leave?.status === 'on' ? school.leave : school.leaves?.find((l) => l.status === 'dismissed' || l.status === 'withdrawn');
+   if (away) return away.firstTerm - ((school.offset ?? 0) - (away.terms ?? LEAVE_RULES.terms));
+   return school.termsBegun - (school.offset ?? 0);
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * The next day, within six weeks, a course meets for a student, as an instant at nine in New Haven: their own
+  * timetable (`coursesFor`), the program’s year a leave or a repeated year left them in and an additional term’s
+  * courses. Until 2026-10-12 it read the calendar year’s, so back from a leave a first-year course never met next.
+  */
+ function nextMeeting(sim: Simulation, school: SchoolRecord, course: Course): number | undefined {
+   const start = new Date(sim.now);
+   for (let n = 0; n < 42; n += 1) {
+     const t = new Date(Date.UTC(start.getUTCFullYear(), start.getUTCMonth(), start.getUTCDate() + n));
+     const day = { year: t.getUTCFullYear(), month: t.getUTCMonth() + 1, day: t.getUTCDate() };
+     const nine = instantFromZoned({ ...day, hour: 9 }, schoolZone());
+     if (nine <= sim.now) continue;
+     if (coursesFor(school, day).some((c) => c.code === course.code)) return nine;
+   }
+   return undefined;
+ }
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // The school
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ /**
+  * The school is a real one in a real town whether or not this life went to
+  * it, so it resolves either way; what it says about you is what differs. A
+  * life that began somewhere else sees the school as a stranger would: its
+  * degree, its town, its courses, and nothing of yours.
+  */
+ interface TheSchool { person: Person | undefined }
+
+ defineLook<TheSchool>('school', {
+   gone: 'There’s no such school in this world.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => (id === YALE_DRAMA.id ? { person: student(sim) } : undefined),
+   seeds: () => [YALE_DRAMA.id],
+   look: ({ person }, { sim }) => {
+     const school = person?.school;
+     const done = !school || schoolEnded(school.standing);
+     const year = person ? yearOfStudy(person) : 1;
+     const term = termNow(sim);
+     const courses = school ? takenIn(school, year, term) : COURSES.filter((c) => c.year === year);
+     // What this term is for them (from 2026-10-12): a leave, an additional term, or their year’s courses.
+     const thisTerm = school?.leave?.status === 'on' ? `and you’re on leave until ${termLabel(school.leave.returnTerm)}.`
+       : school?.extra?.term === term ? `your additional term, and you’re retaking ${spokenList(courses.map((c) => c.name))} in it.`
+         : `and ${courses.length} courses meet in it for your year.`;
+     const begun = school ? programTermsBegun(school) : 0;
+     const rank = person ? rankIn(person) : 0;
+     const next = done ? undefined : nextClasses(sim.now, person.school);
+     const city = CITIES.get(YALE_DRAMA.cityId);
+     const player = sim.universe.playerId;
+
+     const ways: Way[] = (school && done) ? [] : courses.map((c) => ({
+       to: at('course', c.code),
+       label: c.name,
+       detail: `${c.perWeek === 1 ? 'Once' : `${c.perWeek} times`} a week with ${c.teachers}, training ${spokenList(c.skills.map((s) => skillLabel(s).toLowerCase()))}`,
+     }));
+     if (next !== undefined) {
+       ways.push({ to: at('day', dateKey(next, sim.homeZone)), label: `Next Classes ${formatDate(next, schoolZone())}`, detail: 'Nine to three on the next class day, and what else is on it' });
+     }
+     if (city && lookExists(sim, at('place', city.id))) {
+       ways.push({ to: at('place', city.id), label: city.name, detail: school ? 'Where the school stands, and where you have to be at nine on a class day' : 'Where the school stands, and the life of the town around it' });
+     }
+     if (school) ways.push({ to: at('person', player), label: 'You', detail: 'Your life beside the school, all of it' });
+
+     const summary = !school
+       ? `You never studied here; it takes ${YALE_DRAMA.classSize} actors a year into its ${YALE_DRAMA.degree} in ${YALE_DRAMA.program}.`
+       : school.standing === 'graduated'
+         ? `You graduated with the ${YALE_DRAMA.degree} in ${YALE_DRAMA.program}, ${ordinal(rank)} of ${YALE_DRAMA.classSize} in the class overall.`
+         : school.standing === 'dismissed'
+           ? 'The school dismissed you, and you left without the degree.'
+           : school.standing === 'withdrawn'
+             ? 'You withdrew from the school, and left without the degree.'
+             : school.standing === 'withheld'
+               ? 'You finished the three years, and the faculty didn’t recommend the degree.'
+           : `You’re in your ${YEAR_WORD[year]?.toLowerCase() ?? 'last'} year of three, ${STANDING_SAID[school.standing]}, and ${ordinal(rank)} of ${YALE_DRAMA.classSize} in the class overall.`;
+
+     return {
+       name: YALE_DRAMA.name,
+       kind: !school ? 'A Drama School' : done ? 'Where You Trained' : 'Where You Train',
+       parent: school ? at('person', player) : undefined,
+       summary,
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <p className="small">
+             {/* The chair named as every notice names them, the chair of Acting, and the terms in words (from 2026-10-20, brief 17):
+                 until then “the chair of acting” and “over 6 terms”. */}
+             The {YALE_DRAMA.degree} in {YALE_DRAMA.program}{school ? `, class of ${school.classOf},` : ''} in {city?.name ?? 'New Haven'}, over {['no', 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', 'five', 'six', 'seven', 'eight', 'nine'][YALE_DRAMA.terms] ?? YALE_DRAMA.terms} terms. {YALE_DRAMA.dean.name} is the dean, and {YALE_DRAMA.actingChair.name}, the chair of Acting, casts every student.
+             {school && !done ? ` This is ${termLabel(term)}, ${thisTerm}` : ''}
+             {!school ? ` It teaches ${courses.length} courses in the first year, each training part of an actor’s craft.` : ''}
+           </p>
+           {school && person?.craft && (
+             <div className="grid grid-3">
+               <Stat label="Standing" value={STANDING_LABEL[school.standing]} note={school.castable ? 'In the casting pool' : 'Out of the casting pool'} />
+               <Stat label="Terms Begun" value={`${Math.min(begun, YALE_DRAMA.terms)} of ${YALE_DRAMA.terms}`} note={`Class of ${school.classOf}${school.offset ? `; ${school.offset} on leave or repeated` : ''}${begun > YALE_DRAMA.terms ? `; ${said(begun - YALE_DRAMA.terms, 'additional term')}` : ''}`} />
+               <Stat label="Your Place" value={`${ordinal(rank)} of ${YALE_DRAMA.classSize}`} note={`Overall craft ${meanCraft(person.craft).toFixed(1)}`} />
+             </div>
+           )}
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways,
+       provenance: 'Source: the Yale Bulletin, for the school, its courses and its teachers. How often each course meets is estimated.',
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // One course
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ interface TheCourse { course: Course; person: Person | undefined }
+
+ defineLook<TheCourse>('course', {
+   gone: 'That course isn’t one the school teaches, so there’s nothing to sit in on.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => {
+     const course = COURSES.find((c) => c.code === id);
+     return course ? { course, person: student(sim) } : undefined;
+   },
+   look: ({ course, person }, { sim }) => {
+     const craft = person?.craft;
+     const school = person?.school;
+     const year = person ? yearOfStudy(person) : 0;
+     const enrolled = !!school && !schoolEnded(school.standing);
+     const taking = enrolled && takenIn(school, year, termNow(sim)).some((c) => c.code === course.code);
+     const next = taking ? nextMeeting(sim, school, course) : undefined;
+     const terms = course.terms.length === 2 ? 'the fall and the spring' : `the ${course.terms[0]}`;
+     const often = course.perWeek === 1 ? 'once' : `${course.perWeek} times`;
+
+     const ways: Way[] = course.skills.map((s) => ({
+       to: at('skill', s),
+       label: skillLabel(s),
+       detail: craft ? `You’re at ${craft[s].toFixed(1)} in it, and can reach ${ceilingOf(craft, s).toFixed(1)}` : 'Part of an actor’s craft, and every course that trains it',
+     }));
+     if (next !== undefined) {
+       ways.push({ to: at('day', dateKey(next, sim.homeZone)), label: `Meets Next ${formatDate(next, schoolZone())}`, detail: 'Its next class day on the timetable, and what else is on it' });
+     }
+     // Its work set and open, each opening into how far it’s prepared (from 2026-10-09).
+     for (const a of person ? (courseworkOf(sim, person)?.assignments ?? []).filter((x) => x.course === course.code && (x.status === 'open' || x.status === 'revising')) : []) {
+       ways.push({ to: at('assignment', a.id), label: templateById(a.template)?.title ?? 'Work Set', detail: `Set for this course, due ${a.status === 'revising' && a.revision ? a.revision.dueOn : a.dueOn}, and how far it’s prepared` });
+     }
+     ways.push({ to: at('school', YALE_DRAMA.id), label: YALE_DRAMA.short, detail: school ? 'Where it’s taught, and where you stand there' : 'Where it’s taught, and in what town' });
+
+     return {
+       name: course.name,
+       kind: `A ${YEAR_WORD[course.year]}-Year Course`,
+       parent: at('school', YALE_DRAMA.id),
+       summary: taking
+         ? `You’re taking it this term, ${often} a week, with ${course.teachers}.`
+         : !school
+           ? `It’s taught ${often} a week in ${terms} of the ${YEAR_WORD[course.year].toLowerCase()} year, by ${course.teachers}, and you never sat in it.`
+           : course.year > year && enrolled
+             ? `You take it in your ${YEAR_WORD[course.year].toLowerCase()} year, in ${terms}, with ${course.teachers}.`
+             : `You aren’t taking it this term; it runs in ${terms} of the ${YEAR_WORD[course.year].toLowerCase()} year, with ${course.teachers}.`,
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <p className="small">
+             {course.code} trains {spokenList(course.skills.map((s) => skillLabel(s).toLowerCase()))}. A class you come to, rested and in New Haven at nine, grows them; the nearer a skill is to what you can reach, the less each class adds.
+           </p>
+           {craft && (
+             <div className="grid grid-3">
+               {course.skills.map((s) => (
+                 <Stat key={s} label={skillLabel(s)} value={craft[s].toFixed(1)} note={`Of a reach of ${ceilingOf(craft, s).toFixed(1)}`} />
+               ))}
+             </div>
+           )}
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways,
+       provenance: 'Source: the Yale Bulletin, for its code, name and teachers. Where it falls in the week is estimated.',
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // One skill
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ interface TheSkill { skill: Skill; label: string; person: Person | undefined }
+
+ defineLook<TheSkill>('skill', {
+   gone: 'That isn’t part of an actor’s craft as the school teaches it.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => {
+     const found = SKILLS.find((s) => s.id === id);
+     return found ? { skill: found.id, label: found.label, person: student(sim) } : undefined;
+   },
+   look: ({ skill, label, person }) => {
+     const craft = person?.craft;
+     const training = COURSES.filter((c) => c.skills.includes(skill));
+     const ways: Way[] = [
+       ...training.map((c) => ({
+         to: at('course', c.code),
+         label: c.name,
+         detail: `${YEAR_WORD[c.year]} year, ${c.perWeek === 1 ? 'once' : `${c.perWeek} times`} a week, with ${c.teachers}`,
+       })),
+       { to: at('school', YALE_DRAMA.id), label: YALE_DRAMA.short, detail: craft ? 'Whose classes grow it, and where you stand there' : 'Whose classes train it, and in what town' },
+     ];
+     const taught = training.length
+       ? `${training.length === 1 ? 'One course trains' : `${training.length} courses train`} it over the three years.`
+       : 'No course trains it.';
+
+     if (!craft || !person?.school) {
+       return {
+         name: label,
+         kind: 'Part Of An Actor’s Craft',
+         parent: at('school', YALE_DRAMA.id),
+         summary: `Nobody has measured you in it, since you never trained at the school, where ${training.length === 1 ? 'one course teaches' : `${training.length} courses teach`} it.`,
+         body: <p className="small">{taught} Rehearsals, performances and the work grow it too, in an actor who has been measured in it.</p>,
+         ways,
+       };
+     }
+
+     const mine = craft[skill];
+     const reach = ceilingOf(craft, skill);
+     const theirs = person.school.classmates.map((m) => m.craft[skill]);
+     const best = theirs.length ? Math.max(...theirs) : mine;
+     const rank = rankIn(person, skill);
+     return {
+       name: label,
+       kind: 'Part Of Your Craft',
+       parent: at('school', YALE_DRAMA.id),
+       summary: `You’re at ${mine.toFixed(1)} in it, ${ordinal(rank)} of ${YALE_DRAMA.classSize} in the class, with room to grow to ${reach.toFixed(1)}.`,
+       body: (
+         <>
+           <p className="small">
+             {taught} Rehearsals, performances and later the work grow it too, more when you come rested and less the nearer you are to what you can reach.
+             {/* Where the work stops reading it, said (from 2026-10-16): a technique counts mastered at MASTERED, and no piece asks more. */}
+             {TECHNIQUES.includes(skill) ? ` A piece counts it up to ${MASTERED}, and no piece asks for more, so ${mine >= MASTERED ? 'growing it further changes no result' : `the last ${100 - MASTERED} points change no result`}.` : ''}
+           </p>
+           <div className="grid grid-3">
+             <Stat label="You" value={mine.toFixed(1)} note={`Can reach ${reach.toFixed(1)}`} />
+             <Stat label="Class Best" value={best.toFixed(1)} note={`Middle of the class ${median(theirs).toFixed(1)}`} />
+             <Stat label="Your Place" value={`${ordinal(rank)} of ${YALE_DRAMA.classSize}`} note="Among the class" />
+           </div>
+         </>
+       ),
+       ways,
+       provenance: 'How much a session adds, and the scale, are estimated; the ceiling is fitted to published studies of practice.',
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ // A piece of coursework (from the connected world of 2026-10-09)
+ // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ interface TheWork { person: Person; a: Assignment }
+
+ const STATUS_WORD: Record<Assignment['status'], string> = { open: 'Open', revising: 'To Show Again', done: 'Shown', missed: 'Missed', lapsed: 'Not Shown Before The Term Ended', excused: 'Excused' };
+
+ defineLook<TheWork>('assignment', {
+   gone: 'That work isn’t set, or was never yours.',
+   resolve: (sim, id) => {
+     const person = student(sim);
+     const a = person ? assignmentById(sim, person, id) : undefined;
+     return person && a ? { person, a } : undefined;
+   },
+   seeds: (sim) => { const p = student(sim); return p ? (courseworkOf(sim, p)?.assignments ?? []).slice(-3).map((a) => a.id) : []; },
+   look: ({ person, a }) => {
+     const t = templateById(a.template)!;
+     const course = COURSES.find((c) => c.code === a.course);
+     const due = a.status === 'revising' && a.revision ? a.revision.dueOn : a.dueOn;
+     const parts = preparedParts(person, a, due);
+     const weights = weightsOf(a);
+     const dims = (Object.keys(t.dims) as PrepDim[]).filter((d) => t.dims[d]);
+     const [y, m, d] = due.split('-').map(Number);
+     const dueAt = instantFromZoned({ year: y!, month: m!, day: d!, hour: 9 }, schoolZone());
+     const ways: Way[] = [];
+     if (course) ways.push({ to: at('course', course.code), label: course.name, detail: 'The course that set it, and what it trains' });
+     ways.push({ to: at('day', due), label: `Due ${formatDate(dueAt, schoolZone())}`, detail: 'The day it’s shown, and what else is on it' });
+     ways.push({ to: at('readiness', person.id), label: 'Readiness', detail: 'Your sharpness for the work, which affects each step of preparing it' });
+     return {
+       name: `${course?.name ?? a.course}: ${t.title}`,
+       kind: 'A Piece Of Coursework',
+       summary: `${STATUS_WORD[a.status]}. ${t.deliverable}, due ${formatDate(dueAt, schoolZone())}.${a.shown ? ` Shown: ${BAND_LABEL[a.shown.band]}.` : ''}`,
+       parent: course ? at('course', course.code) : undefined,
+       body: (
+         <table>
+           <thead><tr><th scope="col">Part</th><th scope="col" className="num">Prepared</th><th scope="col" className="num">Note Priority</th></tr></thead>
+           <tbody>
+             {dims.map((k) => (
+               <tr key={k}>
+                 <td className="small">{t.dims[k]!.label}</td>
+                 <td className="num mono">{Math.round((parts[k] ?? a.prep[k] ?? 0) * 100)}%</td>
+                 <td className="num mono dim">{Math.round((weights[k] ?? 0) * 100)}%</td>
+               </tr>
+             ))}
+           </tbody>
+         </table>
+       ),
+       ways,
+       // Until 2026-10-12 the weights were headed Of The Showing, and this said Prepared was how far each part stood on
+       // the day it was due, what faded by then taken off, and that the showing weighed each part by its share. Nothing
+       // fades (`preparedParts` reads the parts as they stand), and the result reads each part through the dimensions
+       // it bears on, each held to its least prepared part; the weights only choose the note (`noteCandidates`). Weighs
+       // is the coursework panel’s name for the same figure. Under a line long, as `tests/looks.test.ts` holds every
+       // look’s provenance.
+       provenance: 'Prepared is how far each part stands now; nothing fades. Note Priority is how much a part counts when the teacher picks what to note. Its steps are on the Coursework tab.',
+     };
+   },
+ });
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — the address of a thing you can look at.
+  *
+  * A subject is a kind and an id. The kind says what sort of thing it is and
+  * picks the declaration that knows how to open it; the id is opaque to
+  * everything except that declaration. `at('dial', 'stress')` is the stress
+  * dial; `at('place', 'is-39-reykjavik')` is Reykjavík; `at('person', id)` is
+  * somebody.
+  *
+  * Deliberately not a route. There is no URL in this build — `route` is React
+  * state in the game provider and react-router is in package.json and imported
+  * nowhere — so a subject addresses a thing in the world, not a location in an
+  * application. If routing ever arrives, `?look=` can carry a subject key
+  * without any of this changing.
+  */
+
+ /** A thing you can look at. */
+ export interface Subject {
+   readonly kind: string;
+   readonly id: string;
+ }
+
+ /** The short way to write one. An id is optional for things there is only one of. */
+ export const at = (kind: string, id = ''): Subject => ({ kind, id });
+
+ /** One string, for keying React children and comparing two subjects. */
+ export const subjectKey = (s: Subject): string => (s.id ? `${s.kind}:${s.id}` : s.kind);
+
+ export const sameSubject = (a: Subject | null, b: Subject | null): boolean =>
+   a !== null && b !== null && a.kind === b.kind && a.id === b.id;
+
+ /** Back from a key. Returns undefined rather than a half-made subject. */
+ export function parseSubject(key: string): Subject | undefined {
+   if (!key) return undefined;
+   const cut = key.indexOf(':');
+   if (cut < 0) return { kind: key, id: '' };
+   const kind = key.slice(0, cut);
+   return kind ? { kind, id: key.slice(cut + 1) } : undefined;
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * The typed pointer five record types carry, resolved into a subject.
+  *
+  * `refType` and `refId` are declared on five record shapes — a decision, a
+  * notification, a ledger transaction, a scheduled item and a calendar entry.
+  * The engine writes four on decisions: `'account'`, which has a look;
+  * `'unclaimed-notice'`, whose id is the account’s, so it opens the account
+  * (from 2026-10-10; until then it opened nothing); and `'return'` and
+  * `'us-status'`, which have no look, their decision routing to Papers
+  * instead. An older save carries the film side’s `'project'`, `'audition'`
+  * and `'property'`, none of which has a look in this build. This said until
+  * 2026-10-10 that nothing in the engine wrote one.
+  *
+  * This returns the subject regardless rather than guessing, and every caller
+  * guards on `lookExists` before painting a way, so a kind with no look paints
+  * nothing rather than a dead link.
+  */
+ export function subjectForRef(ref: { refType?: string; refId?: string }): Subject | undefined {
+   if (!ref.refType || !ref.refId) return undefined;
+   if (ref.refType === 'unclaimed-notice') return at('account', ref.refId);
+   return at(ref.refType, ref.refId);
+ }
+
+ /**
+  * SLATE — the sky, where you are, and the days coming after it.
+  *
+  * Home prints a temperature, a row of six days and a climate chip, and every
+  * one of them is a dead end today. They are not dead things: the weather is a
+  * pure function of the save’s seed, the city and the day (`systems/weather.ts`),
+  * so Thursday in Reykjavík is the same Thursday before and after a reload, and
+  * asking about it costs nothing until somebody looks.
+  *
+  * Two kinds live here. `weather` is the sky over one city at this hour — the
+  * thing you are standing in. `forecastday` is one day of the week ahead, which
+  * is a moment, and moments are a floor a chain is allowed to end on. The
+  * climate band is not a third kind: it is another face of the same sky, so it
+  * is a facet, and it hangs off the weather rather than pretending to be a level
+  * of its own.
+  *
+  * That SLATE’s weather is a climate model and not a forecast service is said
+  * once, at the foot of the weather itself, and nowhere else.
+  */
+
+ import { normalFor, toFahrenheit, type ClimateType } from '@/engine/content/climate';
+ import { THUNDER_DAYS, thunderDaysFor } from '@/engine/content/thunder';
+ import { CITIES, type City } from '@/engine/content/geography';
+ import { MONTH_NAMES, MS_DAY, WEEKDAY_NAMES, instantFromZoned, noonOf, startOfDay, zonedParts } from '@/engine/core/time';
+ import {
+   WEATHER_EMOJI, forecastFor, hoursOn, weatherAt, weatherShort,
+   type DayWeather, type HourWeather, type WeatherCondition, type WeatherNow,
+ } from '@/engine/systems/weather';
+ import type { Simulation } from '@/engine';
+ import { Stat } from '@/ui/components/primitives';
+ import { defineLook, type Way } from './registry';
+ import { at } from './subject';
+ import { isAre, spokenList, toStart } from './words';
+
+ /** How many days the look shows: today, and the five after it. */
+ const WEEK = 6;
+
+ const A_DATE = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/;
+
+ /**
+  * How far either way the sky will answer at all.
+  *
+  * The model is a pure function of the date and can be asked about any day
+  * ever, which is not the same as every day being a thing in the world. A year
+  * each way covers anything the calendar can hold and keeps the graph finite.
+  */
+ const HORIZON_DAYS = 400;
+
+ /** The condition as a person says it is doing right now. */
+ const DOING: Record<WeatherCondition, string> = {
+   Clear: 'clear',
+   'Partly Cloudy': 'partly cloudy',
+   Overcast: 'overcast',
+   Drizzle: 'drizzling',
+   Rain: 'raining',
+   Thunderstorm: 'storming',
+   Snow: 'snowing',
+   Fog: 'foggy',
+   Windy: 'blowing',
+ };
+
+ /** The condition as a thing a day brings. */
+ const BRINGS: Record<WeatherCondition, string> = {
+   Clear: 'clear skies',
+   // The condition’s own words, as the stat beside it and Home say it (from 2026-10-20, brief 17): until then "broken cloud".
+   'Partly Cloudy': 'partly cloudy skies',
+   Overcast: 'an overcast day',
+   Drizzle: 'drizzle',
+   Rain: 'rain',
+   Thunderstorm: 'a thunderstorm',
+   Snow: 'snow',
+   Fog: 'fog',
+   Windy: 'a windy day',
+ };
+
+ /** What each band is like to live in, in the words a person would use. */
+ const BAND: Record<ClimateType, string> = {
+   equatorial: 'hot and wet all year, with little change between the seasons',
+   monsoon: 'a long dry season, then months of heavy rain',
+   savanna: 'hot all year, with a wet season and a dry one',
+   arid: 'hot, dry and sunny, with very little rain',
+   semi_arid: 'dry most of the year, with rain that comes in short, heavy bursts',
+   mediterranean: 'dry, sunny summers and mild, rainy winters',
+   humid_subtropical: 'hot, humid summers and short, mild winters',
+   oceanic: 'mild and often wet and gray, without extremes of heat or cold',
+   continental: 'warm summers and cold winters, with short springs and autumns between them',
+   subpolar_oceanic: 'cool and wet all year, with the sea keeping summers cool and winters mild',
+   subarctic: 'long, dark, cold winters and short, cool summers',
+   polar: 'cold all year, with daylight that changes hugely between the seasons',
+   highland: 'thin air, warm days and cold nights, in any month',
+ };
+
+ /** What the eyebrow calls a day, counting from today. */
+ const WHEN_KIND = [
+   'Today', 'Tomorrow', 'Two Days Out', 'Three Days Out', 'Four Days Out',
+   'Five Days Out', 'Six Days Out',
+ ];
+
+ const unitOf = (day: DayWeather): string => (day.fahrenheit ? '°F' : '°C');
+
+ /** A gazetteer name as a person says it. A slashed name is spoken, never read out with the slash. */
+ const spokenName = (name: string): string => name.replace(/\s*\/\s*/g, ' and ');
+
+ /** A word that has to open a sentence. */
+ const sentenceStart = (word: string): string => word.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + word.slice(1);
+
+ /** Small numbers the way prose spells them. */
+ const COUNT_WORDS = ['no', 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', 'five', 'six'];
+ const countWord = (n: number): string => COUNT_WORDS[n] ?? String(n);
+
+ /** Wind in the unit the country reads it in. */
+ const windOf = (day: DayWeather): string =>
+   (day.fahrenheit ? `${Math.round(day.windKph * 0.621)} mph` : `${day.windKph} km/h`);
+
+ /** The city you are standing in, or the one asked for by name. */
+ function cityFor(sim: Simulation, id: string): City | undefined {
+   return CITIES.get(id || sim.player.currentLocationId);
+ }
+
+ /** The local weekday for a day this far ahead of now. */
+ function weekdayAt(sim: Simulation, city: City, offset: number): string {
+   const parts = zonedParts(noonOf(sim.now, offset, city.timeZone), city.timeZone);
+   return WEEKDAY_NAMES[parts.weekday] ?? 'Today';
+ }
+
+ /** "September 12", from the day’s own key. Never the year — a name carries no run of four digits. */
+ function dateWords(dateKey: string): string {
+   const [, month, day] = dateKey.split('-').map(Number);
+   return `${MONTH_NAMES[(month ?? 1) - 1]} ${day ?? 1}`;
+ }
+
+ /** How far the day sits from what the date usually brings, in the degrees on show. */
+ function offNormal(day: DayWeather): number {
+   return Math.round(day.fahrenheit ? day.anomalyC * 1.8 : day.anomalyC);
+ }
+
+ /** "three degrees warmer than the date usually is", or nothing worth saying. */
+ function againstNormal(day: DayWeather): string {
+   const off = offNormal(day);
+   if (Math.abs(off) < 2) return 'about normal for the date';
+   return `${Math.abs(off)}° ${off > 0 ? 'warmer' : 'colder'} than normal for the date`;
+ }
+
+ /** The high the date usually brings here, in the degrees this country reads. */
